16.meaning: A thing; something or anything. With a negation it commonly amounts to 'nothing at all.'
16.grammar: A singular masculine noun, indefinite ('a thing'). The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative, often used here as an object or an adverbial 'in any respect / at all.'

17.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
17.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

18.meaning: A verb meaning 'he intended', 'he willed', or 'he meant' — to direct one's purpose toward something, to want or aim at it.
18.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'), in the derived (form IV) pattern arāda. The bare stem with a final -a denotes a completed action by a single male subject, with the sense of actively willing or purposing something.
18.root: ر-و-د (r-w-d) — to seek, want, aim at

19.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
19.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'
19.root: — (particle; no root)

20.meaning: 'That he/it destroy, cause to perish, do away with'. A causative verb meaning to bring about the ruin or annihilation of something.
20.grammar: A third-person masculine singular present-tense verb of the causative 'af'ala' pattern ('he causes to perish' = 'destroys'). The final -a is the subjunctive ending, the mood used after particles meaning 'to / that / so that', giving the sense 'that he should destroy'.
20.root: ه-ل-ك (h-l-k) — to perish, be destroyed

21.meaning: 'The Messiah / the Anointed One' — the title of Jesus son of Mary (ʿĪsā). Derived from a root meaning 'to wipe/anoint,' it designates the one specially anointed or set apart. The al- ('the') marks it as the well-known, definite title.
21.grammar: A definite noun (title) made definite by al- ('the'). The final -a is the accusative case, the form used when the noun is the direct object of a verb (the one being acted upon).
21.root: م-س-ح (m-s-ḥ) — to wipe, anoint, stroke; hence 'the anointed one'

22.meaning: "son" — a male child or descendant.
22.grammar: A noun beginning with a helping (elidable) vowel. The -a ending is accusative, which marks the word as the object of a verb or as an appositive describing a preceding accusative noun. When placed between two names, it functions as "son of …"
22.root: ب-ن-ي (b-n-y) — to build; son, offspring

23.meaning: "Maryam" — the personal name Mary, the mother of the prophet Jesus.
23.grammar: A proper name (feminine, foreign origin). It is diptote: it takes no -n (nunation), and in the genitive and accusative it ends in -a rather than -i, so the -a ending shown serves for both object and "of" positions.

24.meaning: 'And his mother' — the female parent, with the sense 'his mother'.
24.grammar: Prefix wa- means 'and'. The noun umm ('mother') carries the attached possessive -hu ('his'). The -a before the pronoun is the accusative ending — the case typically marking a direct object (the one acted upon) or going along with a preceding accusative.

25.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
25.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

26.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
26.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
26.root: — (particle)

27.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
27.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

28.meaning: A word meaning 'all together', 'all of them', or 'the whole lot' — emphasising that no one and nothing is left out of a group.
28.grammar: A noun meaning 'all/entirety' carrying the -an ending: accusative case with tanwīn (the indefinite '-n'). This accusative form is typical of a word that comes alongside another to specify it as 'all of them, every one', describing the manner or extent.
28.root: ج-م-ع (j-m-ʿ) — gathering, joining, bringing together

29.meaning: A phrase meaning 'and to Allah (belongs)' — expressing ownership or rightful belonging to Allah; the lām conveys possession or entitlement.
29.grammar: The conjunction 'wa-' ('and') joined to the prepositional phrase 'lillāhi'. This phrase is the preposition 'li-' ('to/for', here showing possession) prefixed to the name 'Allah'; when 'li-' attaches, the connecting hamza and the first lām of the definite article are elided in writing, leaving a single written lām for the preposition followed by the doubled (shadda-bearing) lām of the name. 'Allah' takes the -i (genitive) ending required after a preposition.

30.meaning: Kingdom, dominion, sovereign rule — full ownership and authority over a realm; the right and power to command and dispose.
30.grammar: A singular noun. The final -u marks the nominative case, used when the noun is the subject of a sentence or the thing being identified ('the dominion is …'). The absence of nunation here points to its being made definite by a following possessor in a genitive link.
30.root: م-ل-ك (m-l-k) — to own, rule; kingship, dominion

31.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
31.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.

32.meaning: 'And the earth' — the connective 'and' joined to 'the earth', meaning the ground, land, or the world beneath the sky.
32.grammar: The connective 'wa-' ('and') with the definite feminine noun 'al-arḍ' ('the earth'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the earth') or follows a preposition, here matching the case of what it is joined to.

33.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
33.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

34.meaning: Between the two of them — the space or relation lying amid a pair.
34.grammar: An adverb of place, 'between,' fixed in the accusative as adverbs of place commonly are; the -a marks its adverbial function ('in the place that is between'). The attached -humā is the dual pronoun 'the two of them' (exactly two).
34.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction; that which lies between

35.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'he creates / he brings into being'. It denotes originating and forming something, bringing it into existence — an act distinctively ascribed to Allah.
35.grammar: A present/future verb (Form I, khalaqa, 'to create'). The ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular ('he'). The final -u ending is indicative, expressing a plain statement of present or ongoing/repeated action (as opposed to subjunctive or jussive forms).
35.root: خ-ل-ق (kh-l-q) — to create, originate, shape, measure out

36.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
36.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

37.meaning: "He wills / wishes / desires" — denotes an act of will or volition, the choosing of something. As an ongoing/present-tense verb it expresses willing as a continuous, sovereign act.
37.grammar: A present/future-tense verb in the 'he' form. The ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular ('he'). The final -u ending is the indicative mood, marking a plain, ongoing statement of fact ('he wills').

38.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
38.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
38.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

39.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
39.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

40.meaning: 'every,' 'each,' or 'all' — a word expressing totality or completeness. It indicates the entirety of something: when joined to a singular indefinite noun it means 'every (single) one,' and when joined to a definite noun it can mean 'all of' or 'the whole of.'
40.grammar: A noun of totality. The final '-i' ending is genitive (the 'of/possession' case): it marks the word as governed by a preceding preposition or as the first term of a possessive link to a following noun, so it typically reads 'of every…' or 'every…' leading into what follows.

41.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
41.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
41.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

42.meaning: All-powerful, fully able, ever-capable — possessing complete and effective power to do whatever is willed; one whose ability never falls short.
42.grammar: An intensive adjective on the faʿīl pattern, which stresses a deep, abiding quality ('thoroughly able'). The final -un is the indefinite nominative (nunation) — the doubled-n shows no 'the', and the -u base vowel marks the nominative case, used when the word is a subject or a predicate ('… is all-powerful').

1.meaning: And she said / and … said; the connector 'and' joined to a past-tense 'said' in the feminine form — reporting that a feminine (or grammatically feminine) subject spoke or stated something.

parts.en: she (feminine past marker), here read with -i

1.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') + a past-tense verb 'said.' The -t is the feminine marker showing the subject is grammatically feminine ('she said'). This -t would normally be silent (-at), but here it is voiced as -ti to ease pronunciation before a following word that begins with a connecting (un-pronounced) alif.

2.meaning: The Jews; the religious community of the Children of Israel known as the Yahūd — the people of Judaism, traditionally linked to Judah (Yahūdā) or to the idea of 'turning (back) (to Allah).'
2.grammar: A noun made definite by the prefix al- ('the'). The -u ending is the nominative case, typically used when the noun is the subject of a sentence (the one doing the action) or what something is equated with.
2.root: ه-و-د (h-w-d) — to turn back, return, repent (the Yahūd, 'those who turned')

3.meaning: 'And the Christians' — the followers of ʿĪsā (Jesus). The word is a plural form (commonly traced to 'helpers' or to Nazareth) joined to wa- ('and') and the definite article.
3.grammar: A definite plural noun (the al- prefix means 'the') preceded by wa- ('and'). It ends in a fixed long -ā and does not change its form for case; the alif of the article assimilates in sound to the following n (an-naṣārā).

4.meaning: 'We' — the standalone pronoun for a speaker including others (or a single speaker of majesty). It stands alone to name or emphasize the subject 'we'.
4.grammar: A detached (standalone) personal pronoun, first-person plural, 'we'. Such independent pronouns are used to state or emphasize the subject, often highlighting 'we' as the ones who do or are something.

5.meaning: 'Sons, children, offspring' — the plural of 'son/child'; descendants or progeny.
5.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of ibn ('son'). The -u ending marks the nominative case — typically used for the subject of a sentence or a thing being identified ('the children are …').
5.root: ب-ن-ي (b-n-y) — son, to build (offspring as 'built up')

6.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
6.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

7.meaning: 'And His beloved ones / those dear to Him' — the plural of 'beloved', i.e. ones who are loved and cherished, with the sense 'His beloved'.
7.grammar: Prefix wa- means 'and'. The noun is a broken (irregular) plural of ḥabīb ('beloved'), carrying the attached possessive -hu ('his'). The -u before the pronoun marks the nominative case — typically the subject of a sentence or a thing being identified.
7.root: ح-ب-ب (ḥ-b-b) — to love; love, affection

8.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
8.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

9.meaning: 'Then why? / so for what reason?' — a compound asking the reason for something, combining 'then/so' with the interrogative 'why / for what.'
9.grammar: A question word, not a verb. It joins 'fa-' ('then/so') with the preposition 'li-' ('for') and the interrogative 'mā' ('what') — which loses its long vowel when a preposition is attached, giving 'lima' ('for what / why'). The whole expression asks for a reason.

10.meaning: 'He/it punishes / torments / chastises you (plural)'. An intensive verb conveying the infliction of severe pain or punishment, here directed at 'you'.
10.grammar: A third-person masculine singular present-tense verb of the intensive faʿʿala pattern (the doubled middle letter adds force: 'punishes severely'). The yu- prefix marks a 'he/it' subject; the -u ending is indicative ('he does/will'); the attached -kum is the object, 'you (plural)'.

11.meaning: 'For / because of your (plural) sins'. The base noun is the plural of 'sin' — wrongdoings or offences — combined with 'for/by' and 'your'.
11.grammar: Prefix bi- is a preposition ('for / because of / by'). The noun is a broken (irregular) plural of dhanb ('sin'). The -i ending is genitive, the case required after a preposition; the attached -kum means 'your (plural)'.

12.meaning: A particle of retraction meaning 'rather,' 'no, but,' or 'nay' — it cancels or sets aside what was just said and shifts to a corrected or contrasting statement that follows.
12.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it never changes form). Its function is to redirect the discourse: it dismisses a prior idea and introduces what is actually the case.

13.meaning: You — the standalone pronoun for a group of people ('you all', masculine or mixed). It is used for emphasis or as the subject standing on its own.
13.grammar: A detached subject pronoun meaning 'you all' (second-person masculine/mixed plural). Unlike pronoun endings attached to verbs or nouns, this word stands alone — typically to emphasize the subject or to begin an equational sentence ('you [are]…'). Its form is fixed and does not change for case.

14.meaning: 'A human being, a mortal man' — bashar denotes humankind as flesh-and-blood mortals. It emphasizes the human, bodily nature of a person.
14.grammar: A noun (also usable collectively for 'mankind'). The -un ending is nominative with tanwīn (nunation — the doubled 'n' sound marking an indefinite noun, 'a human being'). The nominative case marks it as the subject of a sentence (e.g. the one who acts) or as a noun whose existence is being affirmed or denied.
14.root: ب-ش-ر (b-sh-r) — skin/outer surface; humankind, mortal

15.meaning: 'than whoever / than the one who' — a fusion of the comparative preposition 'min' ('than, from') with the relative 'man' ('who/whoever'), introducing the person being compared to.
15.grammar: A contraction of the preposition 'min' ('than/from') and the relative-interrogative pronoun 'man' ('who'). The final 'n' of 'min' has merged into the 'm' of 'man' (shown by the doubling), so the two words are pronounced as one: 'mimman.' Both pieces are invariant particles with no case ending.

16.meaning: 'He created' — to bring into being, to originate and shape something that did not exist before, from the root denoting creation and the fashioning of things from nothing.
16.grammar: Past tense, third-person masculine singular ('he'), completed action ('he created'). This is a form I verb of the CaCaCa pattern. The masculine singular 'he' here is the unmarked (zero-suffix) form — there is no separate person ending; the final -a is the inherent stem vowel of the base pattern, not a person or tense suffix.

17.meaning: 'He forgives / pardons' — to cover over and wipe away sins, granting protective pardon. The root carries the image of covering a fault so it is no longer held against a person.
17.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'). The separate final -u is the indicative ending, marking a plain, ongoing statement of fact ('he forgives').

18.meaning: 'for whoever / to the one who' — the preposition 'for/to' joined with the relative word 'who', introducing the person(s) about whom something is said.
18.grammar: A preposition ('for/to') combined with the relative/interrogative word 'man' ('who, whoever'). Together they single out a person or group as the focus ('for the one(s) who...').

19.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'he wills, he wishes, he chooses' — to want or intend something by one's own decision.
19.grammar: A present/ongoing action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular, and the final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact ('he wills'), as opposed to a command or a verb governed by 'that.'
19.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — willing, wishing; the root behind 'thing' (shayʾ)

20.meaning: "and He punishes / and He will torment" — the prefix wa- joins this to what precedes; the verb itself means to subject someone to painful chastisement or torment. The doubled middle consonant gives an intensive, deliberate sense (to inflict severe, drawn-out suffering).
20.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'). The yu- prefix marks 'he' in a derived (intensive) form, and the final -u ending marks the ordinary (indicative) present, signalling an action that is ongoing or yet to happen ('he punishes / he will punish').
20.root: ع-ذ-ب (ʿ-dh-b) — pain, torment, chastisement

21.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
21.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.
21.root: — (pronoun)

22.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'he wills, he wishes, he chooses' — to want or intend something by one's own decision.
22.grammar: A present/ongoing action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular, and the final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact ('he wills'), as opposed to a command or a verb governed by 'that.'
22.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — willing, wishing; the root behind 'thing' (shayʾ)

23.meaning: A phrase meaning 'and to Allah (belongs)' — expressing ownership or rightful belonging to Allah; the lām conveys possession or entitlement.
23.grammar: The conjunction 'wa-' ('and') joined to the prepositional phrase 'lillāhi'. This phrase is the preposition 'li-' ('to/for', here showing possession) prefixed to the name 'Allah'; when 'li-' attaches, the connecting hamza and the first lām of the definite article are elided in writing, leaving a single written lām for the preposition followed by the doubled (shadda-bearing) lām of the name. 'Allah' takes the -i (genitive) ending required after a preposition.

24.meaning: Kingdom, dominion, sovereign rule — full ownership and authority over a realm; the right and power to command and dispose.
24.grammar: A singular noun. The final -u marks the nominative case, used when the noun is the subject of a sentence or the thing being identified ('the dominion is …'). The absence of nunation here points to its being made definite by a following possessor in a genitive link.
24.root: م-ل-ك (m-l-k) — to own, rule; kingship, dominion

25.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
25.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.

26.meaning: 'And the earth' — the connective 'and' joined to 'the earth', meaning the ground, land, or the world beneath the sky.
26.grammar: The connective 'wa-' ('and') with the definite feminine noun 'al-arḍ' ('the earth'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the earth') or follows a preposition, here matching the case of what it is joined to.
26.root: أ-ر-ض (ʾ-r-ḍ) — earth, land

27.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
27.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

28.meaning: 'Between the two of them / in between them both'. An adverb of place meaning the space or relation lying between two parties.
28.grammar: An adverb of place, bayna ('between'), with the attached pronoun -humā, the special dual form meaning 'the two of them / both'. The fixed -a on bayna is its standard adverbial/accusative form.
28.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction; what lies between

29.meaning: And to Him / toward Him. The wa- means 'and'; ilā is the preposition 'to/toward' indicating direction or destination; the attached pronoun -hi means 'him'.
29.grammar: Wa- means 'and'. Ilā ('to/toward') is a preposition of direction; it takes the special form 'ilay-' before a pronoun. The attached -hi is the genitive pronoun 'him', the form pronouns take after prepositions; the -i vowel reflects that genitive attachment.

30.meaning: Al-maṣīr — the destination, the place or state one finally comes to; the journey's end or ultimate outcome to which things return.
30.grammar: A definite noun of place/result on the pattern mafʿil, with the long ī arising from the weak root letter yāʾ (ص-ي-ر). The final -u ending is nominative, the case used for the subject of a sentence or what something ultimately is. The word denotes the final place or state to which one comes.
30.root: ص-ي-ر (ṣ-y-r) — to become, come to, end up at

1.meaning: 'O people of… / O folk of…' — a vocative call ('O!') addressed to the 'people' or 'folk' belonging to something (such as the people of a household, place, or scripture).
1.grammar: The vocative particle ya ('O') used to address or call out, plus the noun 'people/folk'. The -a ending is accusative, which is the case a called-upon noun takes when it is attached to a following word ('O people OF …'). It denotes those who belong to or are associated with something.
1.root: ا-ه-ل (ʾ-h-l) — family, folk, those belonging to

2.meaning: 'The Book / the Scripture' — a written record or revealed scripture; literally that which is written.
2.grammar: The definite article al- with the noun kitāb ('book, scripture'), itself a verbal noun from 'to write.' The -i ending is genitive, typically marking the word as following a preposition or standing in an 'of' relationship to a preceding noun.

3.meaning: A short particle placed before a verb to emphasize or affirm it. Before a past-tense verb it means 'indeed / certainly / has already (happened)'; before a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes / may'. It sharpens and confirms the verb that follows.
3.grammar: An indeclinable particle (its form never changes). It does not take case or tense endings; its job is to color the following verb — affirming and intensifying a past action ('has indeed done') or signaling occasional possibility with a present verb.

4.meaning: "he/it came to you" — a past verb "came" with the pronoun "you" as the one reached, i.e. something arrived at or reached a group of people.
4.grammar: A past-tense verb in its base third-person masculine singular form ("he/it came"), with no extra subject suffix. The verb "to come" is intransitive, so the attached -kum is not a direct object but an indirect (dative) pronoun — "to you" (masculine plural), equivalent to "came to you (all)."

5.meaning: 'Our messenger / envoy.' The noun denotes one who is sent bearing a message — an emissary commissioned and dispatched to deliver word on behalf of the sender.
5.grammar: A noun ('messenger') with the attached possessive -nā ('our'). The -u vowel on the noun is the nominative ending, which typically marks the word as the subject — the one doing or being something in the sentence.
5.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; hence a messenger, envoy

6.meaning: He makes clear / He explains; to set something forth plainly so that its meaning is evident.
6.grammar: A Form II present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'). The yu- prefix marks 'he', and the final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain, ongoing statement of fact (he makes clear / he is making clear).

7.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
7.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

8.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
8.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

9.meaning: 'An interval, a gap, a pause / a period of cessation' — a stretch of time during which something lets up or comes to a halt, a lull or interruption.
9.grammar: A singular feminine noun (the feminine ending is sounded as -t- before the case vowel). The -in ending (nunation with 'i') marks it as indefinite ('an interval') and genitive — the case used after a preposition or when linking as 'of …'.

10.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
10.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

11.meaning: 'the messengers' — the envoys sent by Allah, taken definitely as a known group.
11.grammar: The prefix al- ('the') makes it definite (its 'l' assimilates to the following 'r'). The base is the broken plural of rasūl. The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the messengers') or follows a preposition.

12.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
12.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'
12.root: — (particle; no root)

13.meaning: You (all) say / utter — referring to speaking or saying words, addressed to a group. In context it is the form used after a particle so that it reads 'do not say' / 'that you may say'.
13.grammar: Present-tense verb, second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The ta- prefix marks the second person; plurality is supplied by the -ū ending. The plain ending here (without final -na) is the form a verb takes after certain particles such as 'do not' or 'so that', signalling command-prohibition or purpose.
13.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak, utter

14.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
14.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

15.meaning: 'He/it came to us / reached us'. A past-tense verb of arriving or coming, here with 'us' as the ones reached.
15.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb. With no added subject pronoun and the bare -a ending, it means 'he/it came' (third-person masculine singular, a completed action). The attached -nā is the object, 'us' — 'he came to us'.
15.root: ج-ي-ء (j-y-') — to come, arrive

16.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
16.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

17.meaning: 'A bringer of good news / a bearer of glad tidings' — one who announces something joyful and welcome.
17.grammar: An intensive/agent noun on the faʿīl pattern ('one who gives good news'). The -in ending (nunation with 'i') marks it as indefinite ('a bearer of good news') and genitive — the case used after a preposition or when linking as 'of …'.
17.root: ب-ش-ر (b-sh-r) — good news, glad tidings; to announce joy

18.meaning: 'And not' — a connector 'and' joined to the negative particle 'not,' negating a following statement.
18.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the negator lā ('not'). Lā commonly negates a present-tense verb or a noun. Neither particle takes case endings.

19.meaning: 'A warner / one who gives warning' — one who cautions of impending danger or consequences.
19.grammar: An intensive/agent noun on the faʿīl pattern ('one who warns'). The -in ending (nunation with 'i') marks it as indefinite ('a warner') and genitive — the case used after a preposition or when linking as 'of …'.
19.root: ن-ذ-ر (n-dh-r) — to warn, caution, give notice

20.meaning: A two-part connector: fa- means 'so', 'then', or 'and so', linking what follows as a result or consequence; qad before a past-tense verb intensifies it, conveying 'certainly', 'indeed', or 'already' — stressing that the action has truly and definitely occurred.
20.grammar: fa- is a connecting particle meaning 'so' or 'then', often marking a result. qad is a particle of emphasis; placed before a completed (past-tense) verb it affirms that the action has definitely or already happened. Neither part takes a case ending.

21.meaning: "he/it came to you" — a past verb "came" with the pronoun "you" as the one reached, i.e. something arrived at or reached a group of people.
21.grammar: A past-tense verb in its base third-person masculine singular form ("he/it came"), with no extra subject suffix. The verb "to come" is intransitive, so the attached -kum is not a direct object but an indirect (dative) pronoun — "to you" (masculine plural), equivalent to "came to you (all)."
21.root: ج-ي-ء (j-y-ʾ) — to come, arrive

22.meaning: 'A bringer of good news / a bearer of glad tidings' — one who announces something joyful and welcome.
22.grammar: An intensive/agent noun on the faʿīl pattern ('one who gives good news'). The -un ending (nunation with 'u') marks it as indefinite ('a bearer of good news') and nominative — the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or a thing being identified.
22.root: ب-ش-ر (b-sh-r) — good news, glad tidings; to announce joy

23.meaning: And a warner: one who gives warning, alerting people to coming danger or consequences so they may take heed. Often used of a messenger sent to caution a people.
23.grammar: An active-participle noun on the pattern faʿīl, naming the doer of the act ('one who warns'). The final -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a warner') and in the nominative case, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate. The prefixed wa- means 'and', joining it to what precedes.
23.root: ن-ذ-ر (n-dh-r) — to warn, to give notice; also to vow

24.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
24.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
24.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

25.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
25.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

26.meaning: 'every,' 'each,' or 'all' — a word expressing totality or completeness. It indicates the entirety of something: when joined to a singular indefinite noun it means 'every (single) one,' and when joined to a definite noun it can mean 'all of' or 'the whole of.'
26.grammar: A noun of totality. The final '-i' ending is genitive (the 'of/possession' case): it marks the word as governed by a preceding preposition or as the first term of a possessive link to a following noun, so it typically reads 'of every…' or 'every…' leading into what follows.
26.root: ك-ل-ل (k-l-l) — totality, comprising the whole

27.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
27.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
27.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

28.meaning: 'All-Powerful,' 'fully able,' 'one who has complete power and capability.' An intensive form expressing that the one described possesses perfect, unrestricted power to do whatever is willed — a quality applied supremely to Allah.
28.grammar: An intensive adjective on the faʿīl pattern, conveying a deep, established capability. The '-un' ending (tanwīn al-ḍamm) marks the nominative case (the 'subject/predicate' case) together with indefiniteness — typically the role of a subject or, very often, a predicate describing who or what something is.
28.root: ق-د-ر (q-d-r) — power, capability, measuring out

1.meaning: 'And when / and at the time when' — the connective 'and' joined to a word that points to a past moment or circumstance ('when'), introducing the recollection of an event or situation.
1.grammar: A connective particle plus a time-word. The wa- prefix means 'and'. 'Idh' is an invariable adverb pointing to a definite time in the past ('when, at the moment that'); it has no case ending and typically introduces a clause recalling a past event.

2.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
2.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

3.meaning: Mūsā (Moses) — the proper name of the prophet. As a name it has no Arabic root meaning; it is a non-inflecting (indeclinable) noun whose ending does not change for case.
3.grammar: A proper name ending in a fixed long -ā (written as alif maqṣūra). It is fully indeclinable (invariable): the final -ā never changes, so the word shows no case distinction at all — it looks and sounds identical whether subject, object, or possessor. (This is unlike a diptote, which still alternates between two case vowels; here there is no alternation.)

4.meaning: 'To/for his people' — a compound joining the preposition 'to/for', the noun 'people' (a community or folk, especially one's own kinfolk and nation), and 'his'. It expresses a community belonging to, or addressed by, a single male individual.
4.grammar: The preposition li- ('to/for') governs the noun, which therefore takes the genitive -i ending — the case that regularly follows a preposition or links one noun to another ('… of …'). The attached -hi means 'his'; the i-vowel form -hi (rather than -hu) is used because it harmonises with the preceding -i sound.
4.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to rise; a people who stand together

5.meaning: 'O my people!' — a vocative call: 'people' (one's own community/folk) addressed directly, with 'my' attached. A speaker uses it to summon and appeal to his own community.
5.grammar: The particle yā- is the vocative ('O …'), used to call or address someone. The final -i here is the remnant of the possessive 'my' (the fuller -ī), commonly shortened to -i in direct address, so the whole means 'O my people!' The case ending proper is suppressed because the noun is being called, not used as subject or object.
5.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to rise; a people who stand together

6.meaning: 'Remember! / call to mind, mention' — a command to bring something to mind, keep it in memory, or speak of it.
6.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a masculine plural 'you.' The '-ū' ending directs the order to a group ('you all remember!'); the initial connecting 'a-' is a helping vowel that lets the word begin.

7.meaning: Favour, blessing, or grace; a bestowed benefit or state of ease and well-being granted as a gift, especially divine favour.
7.grammar: A noun meaning favour or blessing. The -a ending is accusative: it typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon).
7.root: ن-ع-م (n-ʿ-m) — favour, blessing, comfort, grace

8.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
8.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

9.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
9.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.

10.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
10.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

11.meaning: 'He made,' 'He appointed,' 'He set up' — to bring about, fashion, or assign something to a state or role. Beyond mere 'making,' it often means rendering one thing into another or establishing something for a purpose.
11.grammar: A past-tense verb. The stem is the three root letters; the '-a' ending on it marks 'he' as the doer and places the action in the completed past ('he made / appointed'). This verb commonly governs two objects, in the sense of 'made X into Y.'

12.meaning: Among you / in you: locates something within a group of people addressed in the plural.
12.grammar: A preposition 'in/among' with an attached pronoun -kum meaning 'you' for a group of males (or mixed group). Words after the preposition fī stand in the genitive, which is why the pronoun takes this object form. The whole expresses presence or location within the addressed group.

13.meaning: 'Prophets' — the plural of nabī, one who brings news from Allah; those raised up to convey divine guidance.
13.grammar: A 'broken' (irregular) plural noun. The -a ending here is the accusative case (the word being of a type that does not take tanwīn), which typically marks the direct object of a verb — the receiver of the action. It names 'prophets' as that object.
13.root: ن-ب-ء (n-b-ʾ) — news, tidings; a nabī is a bringer of news from Allah

14.meaning: And He made you / appointed you: to set, render, or establish someone in a certain state or role; to bring something into a condition.
14.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third-person masculine singular ('he made'), shown by the bare -a ending on the stem. The attached -kum is the object pronoun 'you' (a group of males). Prefixed wa- means 'and'. The verb often takes two objects: it makes X into Y.
14.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, to render, to appoint

15.meaning: Kings: sovereign rulers who hold authority and dominion over a realm and its people.
15.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of malik ('king'). The final -an (nunation) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case, the case typically used for the object of a verb or a predicate of certain verbs ('made [them] kings').
15.root: م-ل-ك (m-l-k) — to own, to rule; kingship, dominion

16.meaning: And He gave you / brought you: to give, grant, or bring something to someone; the giving of a gift or bestowal.
16.grammar: A past-tense verb of Form IV (the causative pattern afʿala), third-person masculine singular ('he gave'), ending in a weak final vowel written as ā. The attached -kum is the object pronoun 'you' (a group of males). Prefixed wa- means 'and'. This verb typically takes two objects: He gave [someone] [something].
16.root: ء-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; in Form IV, to bring, to give

17.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
17.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.

18.meaning: A negating particle, 'not', used specifically to deny that an action happened in the past, even though it attaches to a present-tense verb form. It turns 'you do X' into 'you did not do X'.

parts.en: did not (negation of a completed act)

18.grammar: An indeclinable particle that governs the verb after it, putting that verb into the jussive (clipped) mood and giving it past-time meaning. In short: lam + a present-form verb = 'did not [verb]'.
18.root: — (particle; no triliteral root)

19.meaning: He gives / grants / bestows — to hand over, confer, or bring something to someone. The root centrally means 'to come,' and in this (Form IV) sense 'to cause to come,' i.e. to give or bring forth.
19.grammar: A present/imperfect Form IV verb (afʿala, causative: 'to bring / give'). The yu- prefix means 'he / it (masculine).' The final weak letter is dropped, leaving the bare -i sound, which marks the jussive mood — the clipped form used after particles of condition, command, or negation.
19.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (Form IV) to bring, give, grant

20.meaning: Anyone / a single one: 'one' used to mean a sole individual, especially in negative or conditional contexts ('not anyone', 'any single person').
20.grammar: A noun meaning 'one / a single one', frequently used for 'anyone' when paired with a negation. The final -an (nunation) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case, the case typically used for a verb's object.
20.root: ء-ح-د (ʾ-ḥ-d) — oneness, a single one

21.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
21.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

22.meaning: The worlds, all created realms — the totality of beings and peoples; in 'Lord of the worlds,' the whole of creation across all its kinds.
22.grammar: A definite plural noun ('the worlds') with 'al-' ('the'). The '-īna' ending marks a masculine sound plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) form — the form used after a preposition, in an 'of' linkage, or as a direct object.
22.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know; a 'world' as a sign by which the Creator is known

1.meaning: 'O my people!' — a vocative call: 'people' (one's own community/folk) addressed directly, with 'my' attached. A speaker uses it to summon and appeal to his own community.
1.grammar: The particle yā- is the vocative ('O …'), used to call or address someone. The final -i here is the remnant of the possessive 'my' (the fuller -ī), commonly shortened to -i in direct address, so the whole means 'O my people!' The case ending proper is suppressed because the noun is being called, not used as subject or object.
1.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to rise; a people who stand together

2.meaning: 'Enter!' — a command to a group to go into or enter a place.
2.grammar: An imperative (command) verb. The -ū ending directs the command at a group ('you all, enter!'). The initial alif is a helping-vowel prefix that lets the word begin (pronounced 'u-' here), needed because the stem would otherwise start with a vowelless consonant. The silent alif after the wāw spells the plural ending.

3.meaning: 'the earth,' 'the ground,' 'the land' — the earth as a whole, or the land/ground beneath us. It denotes the terrestrial expanse on which creatures live and walk.
3.grammar: A definite noun ('the earth'). The '-a' ending marks the accusative (the 'object' case) — the role of the thing acted upon, e.g. the direct object of a verb. The prefixed 'al-' makes it definite, 'the earth.'

4.meaning: The holy / the sanctified: that which has been made sacred, set apart and purified, consecrated for Allah.
4.grammar: A passive participle of Form II (the intensive pattern), meaning 'made holy / sanctified', describing the receiver of the action. It carries the feminine tā-marbūṭa, whose full pronunciation -ata bundles together the feminine marker and the accusative case vowel as a single unit (the accusative being the case typically used for an object or for an adjective agreeing with one). The prefixed al- means 'the', making it definite.

5.meaning: A feminine singular relative pronoun: 'the one which / that which / who' (referring to a single feminine thing). It introduces a descriptive clause that tells us more about a preceding feminine noun.
5.grammar: A relative pronoun, feminine singular, fixed in form (it does not change for case). It links a feminine noun to a following clause describing it, the equivalent of English 'which,' 'that,' or 'who.'

6.meaning: He wrote / decreed / prescribed: literally 'to write', and by extension to ordain, make obligatory, or settle something as a binding decree.
6.grammar: A past-tense verb of the basic Form I, third-person masculine singular ('he wrote/decreed'), shown by the bare -a ending. Beyond literal writing, it commonly means to prescribe or make something binding, as in a divine decree.
6.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — to write; writing, decree, prescription

7.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
7.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
7.root: — (proper divine name)

8.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
8.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

9.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
9.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

10.meaning: You turn back / revert / retreat: to turn around and go back the way you came, to relapse or withdraw from a course.
10.grammar: A present/subjunctive verb of Form VIII (the reflexive pattern), second-person masculine plural ('you all turn back'). The ta- prefix marks a 'you' subject; the -ū ending marks a plural male subject, and its normally-final -na is dropped here, signalling the subjunctive or jussive mood that follows certain particles. The doubled dd arises from two combined sources: the Form VIII infixed -t- assimilates to the following first radical d (giving -rtadd-, not -rtatt-), and the root ر-د-د itself has identical second and third radicals (both d), so the two d's merge into one geminate.
10.root: ر-د-د (r-d-d) — to return, to turn back, to revert

11.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on, upon, over,' and by extension 'against' or 'incumbent upon.' It can mark something resting on top of, an obligation laid on someone, or being set over/above something.
11.grammar: An indeclinable preposition (its form never changes). It governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case, and conveys location 'on/upon,' or figuratively duty or opposition ('against').

12.meaning: Your backs: the back parts or rear; what is behind one. Idiomatically tied to retreating or turning away.
12.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of dubur ('back, rear'). The -i ending is genitive, the case typically used after a preposition or to link a noun to a following possessor. The attached -kum means 'your' (a group of males), the possessor that pulls the noun into the genitive.
12.root: د-ب-ر (d-b-r) — back, rear; that which is behind

13.meaning: Then you would turn back / be overturned — to revert, return, or be flipped over to a (often worse) state. 'Inqalaba' is to turn around or be turned upside-down.
13.grammar: A present/future verb in the reflexive 'infa'ala' pattern (turning back upon oneself). The ta-…-ū frame marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all'). The -ū (without final -na) signals the subjunctive mood, typically after 'so that / then' (fa-), giving 'so that you would turn back'.
13.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — to turn, flip, overturn; the heart (qalb) as that which turns

14.meaning: Losers — those who suffer loss and ruin, ending up with a deficit. A 'khāsir' is one whose venture or final account comes out at a loss.
14.grammar: An active participle (one in the state of the action) in the masculine plural. The -īna ending marks the accusative/genitive plural — used for a direct object, after a preposition, or (as often here) describing a state, e.g. 'as losers'.
14.root: خ-س-ر (kh-s-r) — loss, ruin, falling short

1.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

2.meaning: O Moses: a direct address (a call) to the Prophet Moses by name.
2.grammar: The vocative particle yā ('O'), used to call or address someone, followed by the proper name Mūsā (Moses). A called noun like this stands in the vocative; for a name ending in a fixed long ā the ending does not visibly change.

3.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
3.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

4.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
4.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

5.meaning: 'A people, a folk, a community' — a group of human beings bound together, often by kinship, tribe, or shared standing.
5.grammar: An indefinite collective noun. The -an ending (accusative with tanwīn, the 'n' sound) marks it as the object of an action.
5.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a standing group, people

6.meaning: Mighty tyrants / overpowering giants: people of overbearing strength and force, domineering and oppressive, often imposing their will by sheer power.
6.grammar: An intensive noun on the pattern faʿʿāl, conveying great or habitual force ('a mighty/overbearing one'), here in the sound masculine plural. The -īna ending marks a plural of males in the accusative or genitive case (the object or post-preposition form), as opposed to the -ūna used for the subject.

7.meaning: And indeed we: 'we' stated with emphasis. The particle inna strongly affirms and stresses the statement that follows, like saying 'truly' or 'most certainly'.
7.grammar: An emphasizing particle inna ('indeed, truly') with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā meaning 'we/us' (the doubled nūn shared between inna and the pronoun is written once as a shadda). After inna a pronoun takes this object-style form. The prefixed wa- means 'and'. The whole strongly asserts a statement about 'we'.

8.meaning: 'Never / will not' — a particle that negates a future action emphatically. Lan denies that something will ever happen, stronger and more absolute than a simple 'not'.
8.grammar: A negating particle that applies to present-tense verbs to deny them in the future ('will never…'). Grammatically it also puts the following verb into the subjunctive mood, which clips that verb's ending to a short -a. Lan itself does not change.

9.meaning: We enter it: to go into a place. The 'it' refers to some place or thing being entered.
9.grammar: A present-tense verb of Form I with the na- prefix meaning 'we'. The final -a on the stem is the subjunctive mood, typically triggered by particles such as 'that', 'until', or 'never'. The attached -hā is the object pronoun 'it' for a feminine noun.
9.root: د-خ-ل (d-kh-l) — to enter, to go in

10.meaning: 'Until / up to the point that; so that' — a particle marking a limit or goal. It expresses the end-point reached ('until') or the purpose aimed at ('so that, in order that').
10.grammar: A particle indicating a goal or limit. When followed by a present-tense verb it places that verb in the subjunctive mood (clipping its ending to -a), conveying 'until / so that' something comes about. Ḥattā itself is invariable.

11.meaning: They go out / depart / exit: to leave a place, to come or go forth from within.
11.grammar: A present/subjunctive verb of Form I, third-person masculine plural ('they go out'). The ya- prefix marks a third-person subject and the -ū ending marks a plural of males. The normally-final -na is dropped, signalling the subjunctive or jussive mood that follows certain particles.
11.root: خ-ر-ج (kh-r-j) — to go out, to exit, to emerge

12.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'min' ('from / out of / some of') joined to the pronoun 'it' (feminine). Together: 'from it / out of it / of it,' indicating a source or a portion taken from a feminine thing.
12.grammar: A preposition 'min' with the attached pronoun '-hā' ('it/her'), referring to a feminine noun. 'Min' indicates origin, source, or a part taken from a whole; the attached pronoun is in the object form required after a preposition.

13.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'fa-' ('then', 'so', 'but') drawing a consequence, joined to the conditional particle 'in' ('if'). Together: 'then if …', 'but if …'.
13.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that signals a result or transition ('then/so'). 'in' is the conditional particle 'if', introducing a supposed condition. Both are indeclinable particles with no case ending.

14.meaning: They go out / depart / exit: to leave a place, to come or go forth from within.
14.grammar: A present/subjunctive verb of Form I, third-person masculine plural ('they go out'). The ya- prefix marks a third-person subject and the -ū ending marks a plural of males. The normally-final -na is dropped, signalling the subjunctive or jussive mood that follows certain particles.
14.root: خ-ر-ج (kh-r-j) — to go out, to exit, to emerge

15.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'min' ('from / out of / some of') joined to the pronoun 'it' (feminine). Together: 'from it / out of it / of it,' indicating a source or a portion taken from a feminine thing.
15.grammar: A preposition 'min' with the attached pronoun '-hā' ('it/her'), referring to a feminine noun. 'Min' indicates origin, source, or a part taken from a whole; the attached pronoun is in the object form required after a preposition.

16.meaning: Then indeed we: 'we' stated with emphasis and a connecting 'then/so'. The particle inna strongly affirms the statement, while the prefix fa- ties it as a consequence to what came before.
16.grammar: The connective fa- ('then, so', often marking a result) prefixed to the emphasizing particle inna ('indeed, truly'), with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā meaning 'we/us' (the doubled nūn shared between inna and the pronoun is written once as a shadda). After inna a pronoun takes this object-style form. The whole emphatically asserts a statement about 'we' as a consequence.

17.meaning: Ones who enter / those entering: active doers of entering, people in the act or state of going in.
17.grammar: An active participle of Form I (pattern fāʿil) naming the doer ('one who enters'), in the sound masculine plural. The -ūna ending marks a plural of males in the nominative case, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate (as opposed to -īna for the object form).
17.root: د-خ-ل (d-kh-l) — to enter, to go in

1.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
1.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

2.meaning: Two men: exactly two adult males. Arabic has a special dual form for pairs, distinct from singular and plural.
2.grammar: The noun rajul ('man') in the dual, meaning precisely 'two men'. The -āni ending marks the dual in the nominative case, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence. (In the object/genitive form this would instead be -ayni.)
2.root: ر-ج-ل (r-j-l) — man; foot, to go on foot

3.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
3.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

4.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
4.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

5.meaning: They fear: to be afraid of, to hold in awe or dread. Often used of reverent fear of Allah as well as ordinary fear of danger.
5.grammar: A present-tense verb of Form I (with a weak middle letter, giving the long ā), third-person masculine plural ('they fear'). The ya- prefix marks a third-person subject; the full -ūna ending (with its final -na intact) marks a plural of males in the indicative mood, used for a plain, ongoing statement of fact.

6.meaning: 'He bestowed favor / blessed / granted bounty' — a completed act of conferring grace, blessing, and comforts upon someone.
6.grammar: A past-tense verb on the 'afʿala' pattern, with a built-in sense of conferring something upon another. Its form marks a single masculine 'he' as the doer, with no attached subject suffix. So: 'he bestowed favor'.

7.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
7.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
7.root: — (proper divine name)

8.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon the two of them,' 'on both of them,' 'against them two.' It places a duty, blame, or claim on exactly two parties.
8.grammar: The preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, against') takes the form ʿalay- before an attached pronoun, often conveying obligation or something weighing on someone. The suffix -himā is the dual pronoun 'the two of them'; the -i- vowel is the form the pronoun takes after this preposition.

9.meaning: 'Enter!' — a command to a group to go into or enter a place.
9.grammar: An imperative (command) verb. The -ū ending directs the command at a group ('you all, enter!'). The initial alif is a helping-vowel prefix that lets the word begin (pronounced 'u-' here), needed because the stem would otherwise start with a vowelless consonant. The silent alif after the wāw spells the plural ending.

10.meaning: 'Upon them / against them' — the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, against') carrying an attached plural pronoun referring to a group of males.
10.grammar: ʿalā ('upon') takes the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The -him ending is the attached pronoun for a masculine plural 'them'; its final vowel appears as -u (himu) to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with the definite article.

11.meaning: 'The gate' / 'the door' — an entrance, doorway, or gateway. Carries the definite article 'the'.
11.grammar: A definite noun ('the gate'). The -a ending is accusative, the case typically marking the direct object of a verb (the thing entered or acted upon). The al- prefix makes it 'the' specific gate.

12.meaning: A connecting phrase meaning 'then when / and when', introducing a circumstance whose occurrence triggers a following response. 'Fa-' links it to what precedes; 'idhā' sets up a 'when … (then) …' condition for something expected to happen.
12.grammar: A particle cluster, not a noun or verb, so it has no case ending. 'Idhā' is a conditional/temporal particle ('when') used for events regarded as bound to occur, and it normally introduces a clause followed by a main response. The prefixed fa- ('then/so') ties the whole condition to the preceding statement.
12.root: — (particles)

13.meaning: You entered it: to have gone into a place. Combines a past act of 'you (plural)' with an object 'it'.
13.grammar: A past-tense verb of Form I. The suffix -tum is the subject 'you' (a group of males) attached to a past verb; its vowel is lengthened to -tumū before another pronoun. The final -hu is the object pronoun 'it/him'. So: 'you (all) entered it'.
13.root: د-خ-ل (d-kh-l) — to enter, to go in

14.meaning: Then indeed you: 'you' (plural) stated with emphasis and a connecting 'then/so'. The particle inna strongly affirms the statement, while fa- links it as a consequence.
14.grammar: The connective fa- ('then, so', often marking a result) prefixed to the emphasizing particle inna ('indeed, truly'), with the attached pronoun -kum meaning 'you' (a group of males). After inna a pronoun takes this object-style form. The whole emphatically asserts a statement about 'you' as a consequence.

15.meaning: Victors / ones who prevail: those who overcome, dominate, and gain the upper hand over an opponent.
15.grammar: An active participle of Form I (pattern fāʿil) naming the doer ('one who overcomes'), in the sound masculine plural. The -ūna ending marks a plural of males in the nominative case, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate (as opposed to -īna for the object form).
15.root: غ-ل-ب (gh-l-b) — to overcome, to prevail, to conquer

16.meaning: A two-part phrase: the joining word 'and' plus the preposition 'on / upon / incumbent upon,' often used to express an obligation resting on someone.
16.grammar: The connector 'wa' ('and') joined to the preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon'). Both are indeclinable particles with no case ending; a noun governed by 'ʿalā' takes the genitive.

17.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
17.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

18.meaning: Then put your trust / so rely: to entrust one's affair wholly to another and depend on them. In religious use, to place complete reliance upon Allah while still taking due means.
18.grammar: A command (imperative) verb of Form V (the reflexive pattern tafaʿʿala), addressed to a group of males ('you all, rely!'). The fa- prefix means 'then/so', tying it to what precedes. The -ū ending marks the plural-male addressee of a command. This verb is typically followed by 'upon' (ʿalā) the one relied on.
18.root: و-ك-ل (w-k-l) — to entrust, to commit, to rely upon

19.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
19.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

20.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
20.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
20.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

21.meaning: 'Believers / faithful ones' — the plural of muʾmin, one who has faith and trust in Allah and grants assent to the truth.

parts.en: believers (form IV participle, oblique masculine sound plural)

21.grammar: An active participle ('one who believes') from the form IV pattern, here a masculine sound plural. The single suffix -īna is the oblique (accusative/genitive) form of the masculine plural — used for a direct object or after a preposition — as opposed to the -ūna form used for the subject. Its nūn is part of the one ending and is not a separable morpheme.
21.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — security, trust; hence faith and belief

1.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

2.meaning: O Moses: a direct address (a call) to the Prophet Moses by name.
2.grammar: The vocative particle yā ('O'), used to call or address someone, followed by the proper name Mūsā (Moses). A called noun like this stands in the vocative; for a name ending in a fixed long ā the ending does not visibly change.

3.meaning: A two-part expression: an emphatic particle that strongly affirms and confirms a statement ('truly, indeed, certainly'), fused with the attached pronoun 'we.' Together: 'truly we…' / 'indeed we…'
3.grammar: The particle inna gives strong emphasis and certainty to the clause it opens. The attached -ā is the pronoun 'we,' serving as the subject being emphasized: 'truly we…'

4.meaning: 'Never / will not' — a particle that negates a future action emphatically. Lan denies that something will ever happen, stronger and more absolute than a simple 'not'.
4.grammar: A negating particle that applies to present-tense verbs to deny them in the future ('will never…'). Grammatically it also puts the following verb into the subjunctive mood, which clips that verb's ending to a short -a. Lan itself does not change.

5.meaning: We enter it: to go into a place. The 'it' refers to some place or thing being entered.
5.grammar: A present-tense verb of Form I with the na- prefix meaning 'we'. The final -a on the stem is the subjunctive mood, typically triggered by particles such as 'that', 'until', or 'never'. The attached -hā is the object pronoun 'it' for a feminine noun.
5.root: د-خ-ل (d-kh-l) — to enter, to go in

6.meaning: An adverb meaning 'ever / forever / at any time' — used to stress that something will never (or always) be the case throughout all time, especially with a negative to mean 'never, not ever'.
6.grammar: A noun used adverbially. The ending -an is the indefinite accusative, the form regularly used to turn a word into an adverb of time ('… ever / forever'); the -n (nunation) marks it as indefinite. Paired with a negation it strengthens it to 'never, not ever'.

7.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
7.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.
7.root: — (particle; no root)

8.meaning: A verb meaning 'they continued / they remained / they persisted (in a state)'. From the root for 'lasting/enduring', it conveys a thing going on without interruption; in the past tense it underlies the common construction 'as long as / so long as' (something keeps on being the case).
8.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb. The -ū ending is the masculine plural subject marker 'they (did)'. Because the act is grammatically completed, it frames an ongoing condition viewed as a whole — the basis of the idiom 'as long as they remain…'.

9.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
9.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

10.meaning: 'So go! / then depart!' — a command telling a single male to set out or go away. The opening particle adds a 'so/then' sense, linking the order to something said before it.
10.grammar: An imperative (command) addressed to one male: 'go!'. The bare, vowel-less ending (-b with a sukūn) is the typical shape of a direct order. The prefixed fa- means 'so/then', presenting the command as a consequence or next step.

11.meaning: 'You' — the standalone, independent pronoun for addressing a single male person directly.
11.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, second-person masculine singular. Unlike attached pronoun suffixes, it stands alone and is typically used to identify or emphasize the subject ('you [yourself]').

12.meaning: 'And your Lord' — joins with 'and' the word rabb, the Master, Sustainer, Owner and Nurturer who creates, provides for and governs His servant, attached to a 'your' (one male).
12.grammar: Noun with 'and' in front and an attached possessor. The -u on rabb is the nominative case, the form a noun takes as a subject or as the thing being named/identified. The suffix -ka means 'your' for a single male.
12.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, master, sustain

13.meaning: 'So fight, you two!' — a command to exactly two people to engage in combat or do battle. The form is the mutual/confrontational pattern of the verb, i.e. to fight against an opponent; the front particle adds 'so/then'.
13.grammar: An imperative addressed to two people (the dual). The -ā ending marks the dual subject 'you two'. The stem pattern (qātil-) is the mutual/confrontational form (Form III): to fight against someone. Prefixed fa- means 'so/then'.
13.root: ق-ت-ل (q-t-l) — to kill, fight, do battle

14.meaning: A two-part expression: an emphatic particle that strongly affirms and confirms a statement ('truly, indeed, certainly'), fused with the attached pronoun 'we.' Together: 'truly we…' / 'indeed we…'
14.grammar: The particle inna gives strong emphasis and certainty to the clause it opens. The attached -ā is the pronoun 'we,' serving as the subject being emphasized: 'truly we…'

15.meaning: Here, in this place / right here — a demonstrative adverb of place, pointing emphatically to a nearby spot. The prefixed element adds the sense of "behold/right (here)."
15.grammar: An adverb of place ("here"). It is invariable — a fixed word that does not change its ending for case. The leading hā- is a particle of attention/pointing that intensifies the "here," giving "right here."

16.meaning: 'Ones who are sitting / remaining seated; those who stay put'. An active participle naming a group of males characterized by sitting down — and, by extension, staying behind or holding back rather than going forth.
16.grammar: An active participle (a doer-word, 'one who sits') in the masculine plural. The -ūna ending marks a masculine plural in the nominative — the form used for a subject or for the thing being described/identified.
16.root: ق-ع-د (q-ʿ-d) — to sit, stay behind, remain

1.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
1.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.
