The yu-…-ū frame marks a third-person masculine plural subject undergoing the action ('they'). The missing final -na shows the verb is in the subjunctive/jussive after a governing particle, giving 'that they be crucified.'
14.root: ص-ل-ب (ṣ-l-b) — hardness/backbone; crucifixion, fixing upon a cross

15.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
15.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

16.meaning: A verb meaning 'is to be cut off / severed' — but in an intensive shape implying cutting in multiple places or thoroughly. It is passive, describing something being severed.
16.grammar: A passive verb ('it is cut off/severed'); the doubled middle letter (qaṭṭaʿa pattern) gives an intensive or multiple sense ('cut off in pieces / from several places'). The tu- prefix marks a third-person feminine singular subject undergoing the action ('it,' agreeing with a feminine noun such as 'hands'). The final -a is the subjunctive ending, present because the verb follows a governing particle ('that … be cut off').

17.meaning: Their hands. The plural noun 'hands' carrying the masculine plural possessive 'their'; often used idiomatically for what people do, produce, or are responsible for through their own deeds.
17.grammar: A plural noun with an attached possessive pronoun '-him' meaning 'their' (a group of males, or mixed). 'aydī' is the irregular ('broken') plural of 'yad' (hand). The pronoun ending makes the whole construction definite and possessed; the 'i'-coloured stem before the suffix reflects its genitive/possessed state, the form typically following a preposition or standing as object.

18.meaning: "and their feet" — the noun for the lower limbs/feet, joined by an opening connector "and" and carrying an attached pronoun meaning "their" (referring to a group of males).
18.grammar: A plural noun preceded by the connector "and" and followed by the possessive pronoun "-hum" ("their," a group of males). "arjul" is the broken (irregular) plural of "rijl" (foot/leg). The vowel linking the noun to the pronoun is the case ending: as written here it is fatḥa (-a), the accusative form; the same word also occurs read with kasra (-i), the genitive form, and the case carried can shift the grammatical relation. The attached pronoun makes the noun definite and shows ownership.
18.root: ر-ج-ل (r-j-l) — foot, leg; by extension a man (one who goes on foot)

19.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
19.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

20.meaning: "opposition, contrariness, being at variance" — a noun denoting difference or being on opposite sides; in legal idiom it describes alternating or crosswise arrangement (e.g., one from each side).
20.grammar: A masculine noun. The final "-in" (tanwīn kasra) is the indefinite genitive ending: it marks the word as indefinite ("an opposition") and typically follows a preposition or links to a preceding word in an "of"-type relation.
20.root: خ-ل-ف (kh-l-f) — to come after, differ, oppose; succession and contrariety

21.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
21.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

22.meaning: "they are expelled / banished / driven out of the land" — a verb describing being cast out and removed from one's territory.
22.grammar: A present-tense passive verb in the masculine plural, in the subjunctive/jussive mood. The "yu-" prefix marks the third person ("they/he"); it does not by itself mark voice. The passive is signalled by the internal vowel pattern (the present passive takes "u" on the prefix and "a" inside the stem), which is why it reads "are banished" rather than "banish." The plural "they" ending normally has a final "-na," but here the "-n" is dropped (leaving "-w/-aw"), which signals the subjunctive or jussive — the form used after certain particles or in conditional/purpose constructions.
22.root: ن-ف-ي (n-f-y) — to banish, drive away, negate, expel

23.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
23.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

24.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
24.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

25.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
25.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

26.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
26.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

27.meaning: 'Disgrace / humiliation / shame' — a state of public abasement and dishonour.
27.grammar: A verbal noun, masculine singular. The -un (tanwīn ḍamm) ending is nominative and indefinite, typical of a subject or predicate ('[there is] a disgrace'). It names the condition of being shamed and humiliated.
27.root: خ-ز-ي (kh-z-y) — disgrace, humiliation, being put to shame

28.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
28.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
28.root: — (particle)

29.meaning: 'The nearer (life) / this world' — literally 'the nearest/lowest,' a name for the present worldly life as opposed to the Hereafter.
29.grammar: The definite article al- with dunyā, a feminine superlative/elative adjective ('the nearest, the lowest') used as a name for the present world. Its ending (alif maqṣūra) is invariable — it does not change for case — and it commonly describes 'the [worldly] life.'
29.root: د-ن-و (d-n-w) — nearness, being close or low; hence the 'near' present world

30.meaning: 'And for them / and they have.' A combination expressing possession or entitlement belonging to a group of males: 'and to/for them (belongs).' The particle li- conveys 'for' or 'belonging to,' and the attached pronoun refers to 'them.'
30.grammar: A possessive/benefactive phrase: the preposition li- ('for, belonging to') with the attached object pronoun -hum ('them,' masculine plural). Such 'for X' phrases commonly express that something belongs to or is owed to that party.
30.root: — (particle plus pronoun; no root)

31.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
31.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

32.meaning: The Hereafter — the final, lasting life that comes after death and the present world; literally 'the last/latter (abode or life)', as opposed to the first, nearer life.
32.grammar: A feminine adjective used as a noun, with 'the'. The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF …'), or follows a preposition or oath particle.
32.root: ء-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to be last, to come after, end

33.meaning: Painful punishment, torment, or chastisement — suffering imposed as a penalty.
33.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The ending -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and in the nominative case, typically used for the subject or for the thing said to exist.

34.meaning: Great, immense, mighty — vast in magnitude or importance. Describes something tremendous, whether in size, weight, or gravity.
34.grammar: An adjective on the intensive 'faʿīl' pattern, conveying a strong, established quality. The '-un' ending marks it nominative and indefinite; as an adjective it typically agrees with and describes an indefinite noun ('a great …').

1.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
1.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: They turned back in repentance — a third-person masculine plural past verb meaning 'they repented,' i.e. they returned to Allah, abandoning sin and re-orienting the heart toward Him.
3.grammar: Past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks the subject as 'they' (a group of males or mixed). As a perfect verb it presents the action as completed: 'they turned (back) in repentance.'

4.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
4.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

5.meaning: A noun/adverb meaning 'before' — denoting that which precedes in time or order.
5.grammar: An adverb/noun of time. The -i ending is genitive, which here arises because it follows a preposition (commonly 'min', 'from'); it characteristically links to a following noun ('before … OF …').
5.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to precede, come before; the front or prior side

6.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
6.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

7.meaning: "you (all) have power over, are able to overpower, gain mastery over" — a verb of having capacity, control, or the upper hand.
7.grammar: A present-tense verb, second-person masculine plural ("you all"), in the subjunctive/jussive mood. The "ta-" prefix marks "you"; the plural ending's final "-na" is dropped to "-ū," which signals the subjunctive/jussive — used after certain particles or in conditional/purpose clauses.
7.root: ق-د-ر (q-d-r) — power, ability, measure, decree

8.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
8.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
8.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

9.meaning: "then know! / so be aware!" — a command to a group to know or recognize a fact, introduced by a connector meaning "then/so."
9.grammar: An imperative (command) verb addressed to a group of males, prefixed by "fa-" ("then/so"), which links it to a preceding statement as a result or consequence. The "-ū" ending marks the plural addressee ("you all"); the imperative drops the present-tense "ta-" prefix and takes a helping initial vowel.

10.meaning: An emphatic particle meaning 'that' (as in 'I know that...') or 'indeed/surely.' It introduces a statement and gives it certainty and emphasis, presenting what follows as an established fact.
10.grammar: An emphatic particle that introduces a noun-clause ('that...'). It puts the following noun into the accusative case and lends the whole statement a sense of certainty and assertion. It typically comes after verbs of knowing, saying, or informing.

11.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
11.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

12.meaning: An intensive adjective/name meaning 'much-forgiving, ever-ready to forgive, one who veils and pardons faults again and again'. The form stresses abundance, so it conveys forgiveness as a constant, far-reaching quality.
12.grammar: An intensive adjective (the ghafūr 'doer-in-abundance' pattern), used as a divine attribute of Allah. The -un ending is nunation in the nominative case: it marks the word as indefinite and in the nominative, the case typically used for the subject or for a predicate that describes the subject.
12.root: غ-ف-ر (gh-f-r) — to cover, veil, forgive

13.meaning: Most Merciful / ever-compassionate — one whose mercy is deep, constant, and abundantly bestowed; an intensive form stressing enduring tenderness and care. The '-un' nunation marks it as indefinite nominative.
13.grammar: An intensive adjective (faʿīl pattern) conveying a lasting, abundant quality. The '-un' (nunation on the ḍamma) marks it as indefinite and in the nominative case, typically used for a subject or predicate ("is most merciful").
13.root: ر-ح-م (r-ḥ-m) — mercy, compassion

1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: Be mindful and wary of — guard yourselves by placing a protective barrier between yourselves and harm or wrongdoing. This is the verb of taqwā: God-conscious caution that shields one from what is forbidden.
4.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a group ('you all'). The -ū ending directs the order to a masculine plural 'you.' Built on a reflexive pattern (Form VIII), it conveys 'protect yourselves / be on guard.'

5.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
5.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

6.meaning: A command, 'and seek / strive after / desire.' To pursue something earnestly, to look for and aim at it with effort.
6.grammar: A command verb (form VIII, an intensive of 'to want/seek'), addressed to a masculine-plural 'you' by the -ū ending; as a command it drops the final -na. The leading alif is a helping vowel pronounced when starting the word. Wa- means 'and.'
6.root: ب-غ-ي (b-gh-y) — to seek, desire, strive for

7.meaning: 'To Him' or 'toward Him' — the preposition expressing direction or endpoint ('to / toward') combined with a pronoun referring to a single masculine person, indicating motion or attention directed at him.
7.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base 'ilā shifts to 'ilay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -hi is the third-person masculine singular object of a preposition, 'him'; its -i vowel is the form the pronoun takes after the 'ay' sound.

8.meaning: "the means of approach / that which brings one near" — a noun for an avenue, link, or instrument by which one seeks nearness to something or someone (especially nearness to Allah).
8.grammar: A definite feminine noun ("the means"). The "al-" prefix is the definite article "the"; the "-ta" (taʾ marbūṭa pronounced as "t") marks it as feminine, and the final "-a" is the accusative ending, typically marking the object of a verb or the goal that is sought.
8.root: و-س-ل (w-s-l) — to draw near, seek connection, a means of approach

9.meaning: "and strive! / and struggle hard! " — a command to a group to exert utmost effort, struggle, and persevere in a cause, opening with the connector "and."
9.grammar: An imperative (command) verb in the masculine plural, opened by the connector "and." It is from the intensive/reciprocal pattern (form III) that conveys earnest, sustained effort against resistance. The "-ū" ending marks the plural addressee ("you all").
9.root: ج-ه-د (j-h-d) — to exert effort, strive, struggle

10.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
10.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

11.meaning: "His way / His path" — the noun for a road, path, or way, here carrying the attached pronoun "His" (referring to Allah); idiomatically, the path or cause of Allah.
11.grammar: A masculine noun with the attached possessive pronoun "-hi" ("his/His"). The pronoun appears in its "-hi" form (with the "i" vowel), which is used when the noun is in the genitive — i.e., after a preposition or when linked in an "of"-type relation to a preceding word.

12.meaning: 'so that you may…,' 'in the hope that you…' — a particle expressing purpose, expectation, or hopeful anticipation, fused with 'you (plural).' It introduces a hoped-for or intended outcome; when used of Allah it conveys the desired result rather than uncertainty.

parts.en: so that / perhaps / in hope that

12.grammar: An emphatic particle of hope/purpose belonging to the 'inna' family, which attaches a pronoun as its subject. The particle's fixed form ends in '-a,' and the suffix '-kum' is 'you (plural),' giving 'so that you (all) may…'

13.meaning: You attain success / prosper / flourish. To achieve true success and lasting well-being — winning what is sought and being saved from loss.
13.grammar: A present-tense verb for the second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The tu- prefix (from the fourth verb pattern) signals a 'you' subject, and the -ūna ending marks the masculine plural in the indicative mood, stating it as an ongoing or factual reality.
13.root: ف-ل-ح (f-l-ḥ) — to succeed, prosper, thrive (originally to till/cultivate)

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
3.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

4.meaning: A conditional particle introducing a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact supposition: 'if (it were the case that…)'. It typically presents a condition that is unfulfilled or merely imagined, often implying the result did not or would not happen.
4.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case ending). It signals a hypothetical 'if': it sets up a supposed condition whose consequence is then stated, frequently with the sense 'if X were so, then Y would be so' — often where X is contrary to fact.

5.meaning: An emphatic particle meaning 'that' (as in 'I know that...') or 'indeed/surely.' It introduces a statement and gives it certainty and emphasis, presenting what follows as an established fact.
5.grammar: An emphatic particle that introduces a noun-clause ('that...'). It puts the following noun into the accusative case and lends the whole statement a sense of certainty and assertion. It typically comes after verbs of knowing, saying, or informing.

6.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
6.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

7.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
7.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.
7.root: — (particle; no root)

8.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
8.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

9.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
9.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

10.meaning: A word meaning 'all together', 'all of them', or 'the whole lot' — emphasising that no one and nothing is left out of a group.
10.grammar: A noun meaning 'all/entirety' carrying the -an ending: accusative case with tanwīn (the indefinite '-n'). This accusative form is typical of a word that comes alongside another to specify it as 'all of them, every one', describing the manner or extent.

11.meaning: "and the like of it / and its equal" — the noun "like, equal, counterpart" joined by "and" and carrying the attached pronoun "it," i.e., something matching or equal to it.
11.grammar: A masculine noun ("a like/equal") opened by the connector "and" and carrying the attached pronoun "-hu" ("it/its"). The stem vowel "-a" (mithla) is the accusative ending, typically marking it as the object of a verb or governed by a preceding word; the pronoun appears as "-hu" because the preceding vowel is "a."

12.meaning: Together with him; in his company or alongside him.
12.grammar: An adverb of accompaniment, 'with', joined to the attached pronoun -hu 'him'. Together they mean 'with him / in his company'.
12.root: — (no triliteral root; adverb of accompaniment)

13.meaning: "so that they may ransom themselves / in order to redeem themselves" — a verb of ransoming or buying oneself free, prefixed with "so that / in order to."
13.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ("they"), in the subjunctive mood after the particle "li-" ("so that / in order to"), which expresses purpose. The "ya-" prefix marks "they/he"; the plural ending's final "-na" is dropped to "-ū" because the subjunctive is required after "li-." The form (VIII) is reflexive: to ransom/redeem oneself.
13.root: ف-د-ي (f-d-y) — to ransom, redeem, pay to free

14.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
14.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

15.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
15.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
15.root: — (preposition)

16.meaning: ʿAdhāb — punishment, torment, suffering inflicted as a penalty; severe chastisement.
16.grammar: A noun. The final -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a following noun ('… of …') or follows a preposition or oath particle. The word names painful punishment and torment.

17.meaning: 'Day' — a span of time. It denotes a day or a definite point/period of time; it links to a following word to specify which day (e.g., 'the day of …').
17.grammar: A masculine noun. Its final -i vowel is the genitive case: it typically appears after a preposition or when the word is linked to a following noun in an 'of …' relationship (as in 'the day OF …').

18.meaning: "the Resurrection" — the standing-up of all people from death to be judged; literally the act of rising or standing up.
18.grammar: The al- prefix means "the." The -i ending (on the feminine -t) is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ("the … OF this") or follows a preposition.
18.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise

19.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
19.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

20.meaning: "it was accepted / it was received favorably" — a completed-action passive verb meaning something was accepted or received (especially of a deed or offering being accepted).

parts.en: it was accepted (Form V passive verb)

20.grammar: A past-tense passive verb, third-person masculine singular ("it/he was accepted"). It is the passive of the Form V verb (تَفَعَّلَ; active "taqabbala," to accept/receive), built by doubling the middle radical and prefixing "ta-." In the passive past, the vowels shift to "u" throughout the prefix and stem with "i" before the last radical (tu-qubbi-la); this internal vowelling — not any separable prefix — is what marks the passive. The initial "tu-" is an inseparable part of the Form V stem, not a detachable passive marker. The final "-a" is the standard past-tense singular ending.
20.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to accept, receive, face toward

21.meaning: From them / among them — the preposition min ('from, out of, part of') joined to the pronoun 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group).
21.grammar: The preposition min ('from / among / part of') with the attached third-person masculine plural pronoun -hum ('them'). Pronouns after a preposition are in the genitive; the combination expresses origin, partition ('some of them'), or belonging to that group.
21.root: — (preposition with pronoun, no root)

22.meaning: 'And for them / and they have.' A combination expressing possession or entitlement belonging to a group of males: 'and to/for them (belongs).' The particle li- conveys 'for' or 'belonging to,' and the attached pronoun refers to 'them.'
22.grammar: A possessive/benefactive phrase: the preposition li- ('for, belonging to') with the attached object pronoun -hum ('them,' masculine plural). Such 'for X' phrases commonly express that something belongs to or is owed to that party.
22.root: — (particle plus pronoun; no root)

23.meaning: Painful punishment, torment, or chastisement — suffering imposed as a penalty.
23.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The ending -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and in the nominative case, typically used for the subject or for the thing said to exist.
23.root: ع-ذ-ب (ʿ-dh-b) — to punish, torment, chastise

24.meaning: Painful, agonizing, deeply hurtful. An intensive adjective describing something that inflicts severe, grievous pain.
24.grammar: A masculine singular adjective on the intensive pattern faʿīl, conveying a strong, abiding quality ('truly painful'). The -un ending (tanwīn ḍamm) marks the nominative case (the case of a subject or of a noun's basic naming form), and the nunation shows it is indefinite.

1.meaning: they want / they intend — to will, desire, or purpose something. The verb conveys an active, ongoing intention or wish on the part of a group.
1.grammar: A present-tense Form IV verb (arāda, 'to will/intend'). The yu- prefix marks a third-person subject, and the ending -ūna marks masculine plural plus the indicative mood (a plain statement: 'they want'). The -na would drop under a particle that changes the mood.

2.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
2.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

3.meaning: They go out / depart / exit: to leave a place, to come or go forth from within.
3.grammar: A present/subjunctive verb of Form I, third-person masculine plural ('they go out'). The ya- prefix marks a third-person subject and the -ū ending marks a plural of males. The normally-final -na is dropped, signalling the subjunctive or jussive mood that follows certain particles.
3.root: خ-ر-ج (kh-r-j) — to go out, to exit, to emerge

4.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
4.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

5.meaning: 'The Fire' — fire, flame; in religious usage often the Fire of Hell, the blazing punishment of the Hereafter.
5.grammar: The definite article 'al-' ('the') plus the feminine noun 'nār' ('fire'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (so it is pronounced 'an-nār'). The '-i' ending is genitive, the case used after a preposition or to link the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the Fire').

6.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
6.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

7.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (referring to a group of males, or a mixed group). Because it stands on its own rather than being attached to a verb or noun, it often adds emphasis, singling out or stressing the subject ('they themselves', 'it is they who').
7.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It does not take case endings; the fixed -m simply marks the plural 'they'. Standing alone, it commonly serves to emphasise or isolate the subject.

8.meaning: "(by no means) coming out / going forth / departing" — the active participle "ones who come out," describing those who exit or leave, prefixed with "bi-" (commonly used to reinforce a negation, "not at all coming out").
8.grammar: An active participle ("ones who come out") in the masculine plural, prefixed by "bi-." The "-īna" ending is the masculine sound plural in its genitive/accusative form; here the "bi-" prefix governs the genitive. The participle names the doer of the action of "coming out."
8.root: خ-ر-ج (kh-r-j) — to go out, come forth, exit, depart

9.meaning: "from it / out of it" — the preposition "from/out of" with an attached pronoun "it" referring to a feminine noun.
9.grammar: A preposition ("from/out of") fused with the attached pronoun "-hā" ("it/her"), which refers back to a feminine or grammatically feminine noun. Prepositions like this place their following pronoun in the genitive; the pronoun itself does not change shape for case.

10.meaning: 'And for them / and they have.' A combination expressing possession or entitlement belonging to a group of males: 'and to/for them (belongs).' The particle li- conveys 'for' or 'belonging to,' and the attached pronoun refers to 'them.'
10.grammar: A possessive/benefactive phrase: the preposition li- ('for, belonging to') with the attached object pronoun -hum ('them,' masculine plural). Such 'for X' phrases commonly express that something belongs to or is owed to that party.

11.meaning: Painful punishment, torment, or chastisement — suffering imposed as a penalty.
11.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The ending -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and in the nominative case, typically used for the subject or for the thing said to exist.

12.meaning: "lasting, enduring, permanent, abiding" — an active participle describing something that stays in place, persists, or is established and ongoing.
12.grammar: An active participle (form IV) functioning as an adjective/noun ("one that stays, abiding"). The "mu-" prefix marks the doer/agent of the action. The final "-un" (tanwīn ḍamma) is the indefinite nominative ending, marking the word as indefinite ("a lasting one") and as a subject or predicate rather than an object.
12.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise, remain, establish

1.meaning: "and the (male) thief" — the noun/active participle "the one who steals" (masculine), preceded by the connector "and" and made definite by "the."
1.grammar: A definite active participle used as a noun ("the thief"), masculine singular, opened by the connector "and." The "al-" is the definite article "the" (its "l" assimilates into the following "s," hence "as-sāriq"). The final "-u" is the nominative ending, typically marking the word as a subject or topic.

2.meaning: "and the (female) thief" — the feminine form of "the one who steals," preceded by "and" and made definite by "the."
2.grammar: A definite active participle used as a noun, marked feminine ("the female thief"), opened by "and." The "al-" is the definite article "the" (its "l" assimilates into "s"). The "-at-" (taʾ marbūṭa) marks the feminine, and the final "-u" is the nominative ending, typically marking a subject or topic.

3.meaning: "then cut off! / so sever!" — a command to a group to cut or sever something, introduced by the connector "then/so."
3.grammar: An imperative (command) verb addressed to a group of males, prefixed by "fa-" ("then/so"), linking it as a consequence to what precedes. The "-ū" ending marks the plural addressee ("you all"); the imperative takes a helping initial vowel in place of the present-tense prefix.
3.root: ق-ط-ع (q-ṭ-ʿ) — to cut, sever, cut off

4.meaning: "the hands of the two of them / their two hands" — the plural noun "hands" carrying the attached dual pronoun "of the two of them."
4.grammar: A plural noun ("hands," the broken plural of "yad") with the attached dual pronoun "-humā" ("the two of them"). The stem vowel "-a" (aydiya-) is the accusative ending, typically marking the noun as the object of a verb. The dual pronoun specifies exactly two possessors.

5.meaning: "as a recompense / requital / repayment" — a noun denoting the return or payment given for a deed, whether reward or penalty.
5.grammar: A masculine noun. The final "-an" (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative ending; on a word like this it commonly functions adverbially, expressing the cause, purpose, or manner — i.e., "(done) as a recompense."
5.root: ج-ز-ي (j-z-y) — to recompense, requite, repay, reward or punish

6.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
6.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

7.meaning: "the two of them earned / acquired / committed" — a completed-action verb of gaining or bringing upon oneself, with two people as the doers.
7.grammar: A past-tense verb with a dual subject ("the two of them"). The final "-ā" ending marks exactly two doers. The verb denotes earning or acquiring, and is often used for actions one brings upon oneself, including the gaining of sin or its consequences.
7.root: ك-س-ب (k-s-b) — to earn, acquire, gain (good or bad)

8.meaning: "as an exemplary punishment / a deterrent penalty" — a noun for a punishment meant to make an example and warn others off.
8.grammar: A masculine noun. The final "-an" (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative ending; on this word it commonly functions adverbially to express purpose or manner — i.e., "(imposed) as a deterrent punishment."
8.root: ن-ك-ل (n-k-l) — to restrain, hold back; an exemplary punishment that deters

9.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
9.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

10.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
10.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

11.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
11.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
11.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

12.meaning: Mighty, invincible, and supremely honoured; one who possesses overwhelming power and dignity such that none can overcome or resist Him. As a divine descriptor it conveys unassailable might joined with exalted worth.
12.grammar: A descriptive noun (adjective) on an intensive pattern, conveying a deep, enduring quality. The -un ending is indefinite and nominative: it typically marks the word as a subject or as a predicate describing something ("is mighty").
12.root: ع-ز-ز (ʿ-z-z) — might, honour, strength

13.meaning: All-Wise: possessing perfect wisdom — placing everything in its right place with flawless knowledge, judgment, and purpose. As a divine attribute it denotes Allah's consummate wisdom.
13.grammar: A masculine singular adjective/intensive noun on the faʿīl pattern, expressing a deep, settled quality of wisdom. The final -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite and nominative — the case used for a subject or, very often, a predicate describing the doer ('[He is] All-Wise').
13.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge, to be wise

1.meaning: A compound meaning 'then whoever' or 'so whoever'. It combines 'then/so' with the conditional/relative 'who', introducing whatever person meets a stated condition.
1.grammar: The connector fa- ('then/so', often answering or following a condition) joined to man ('whoever / the one who'), which refers to people and introduces a condition: 'whoever does X…'. man does not change its ending; the clause after it supplies the rest of the meaning.

2.meaning: "he turned back (in repentance) / repented" — a completed-action verb of turning away from wrongdoing and returning (to Allah); when said of Allah toward a person, it means He turned to them in mercy and accepted their repentance.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ("he/it"). The final "-a" is the standard past-tense ending for a single male doer. The hollow root's middle weak letter appears as a long "ā" in this form.
2.root: ت-و-ب (t-w-b) — to turn back, repent, return

3.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
3.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

4.meaning: A noun/adverb meaning 'after' — the time or position following something; 'afterward', 'following'.
4.grammar: An adverb of time functioning as a noun, here in the genitive case marked by the final -i. The genitive ending typically appears after a preposition or as the second term of a construct ('after THE …'), linking 'after' to a following noun to specify what it comes after.
4.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — to be after, to follow, distance in place or time

5.meaning: "his wrongdoing / his injustice / his oppression" — the noun "wrongdoing, injustice, putting something out of its rightful place," carrying the attached pronoun "his."
5.grammar: A masculine verbal noun with the attached possessive pronoun "-hi" ("his"). The pronoun appears in its "-hi" form (with the "i" vowel), used when the noun is in the genitive — i.e., after a preposition or in an "of"-type linkage to a preceding word.
5.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — wrongdoing, injustice, oppression; putting a thing where it does not belong

6.meaning: "and he set right / reformed / made amends" — a completed-action verb of putting things right, correcting, or acting righteously, opening with the connector "and."
6.grammar: A past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ("he/it"), opened by the connector "and." It is from the causative pattern (form IV), meaning to make something sound/right or to put it in order. The final "-a" is the standard past-tense ending for a single male doer.
6.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — to be sound, right, good; to set right, reform

7.meaning: A two-part connector meaning 'so/then, indeed…'. It joins fa- ('so', 'then', marking a result or consequence) to inna, an emphatic particle that strongly affirms the statement that follows ('truly', 'verily').
7.grammar: fa- is a connective prefix signaling that what follows is a consequence or next step. inna is an emphatic particle that introduces a nominal sentence, puts its following noun in the accusative, and strengthens the assertion; it does not itself take a case ending.

8.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
8.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

9.meaning: 'He/it turns in relenting / accepts repentance' — from tāba; of Allah it means He relents toward and accepts the return of a servant; of a person, he turns back to Allah.
9.grammar: A present/ongoing verb. The ya- prefix marks a masculine singular subject, 'he/it.' The final -u ending is the ordinary present-tense (indicative) marker, indicating an action that is happening or customary.
9.root: ت-و-ب (t-w-b) — to turn back, repent, return

10.meaning: A preposition fused with a pronoun, meaning 'upon him', 'on him', or 'toward him'. It marks the one to whom an action is directed or upon whom something rests.
10.grammar: The preposition 'upon/on' with an attached object pronoun -hi ('him', third-person masculine singular); its -i vowel is the regular form the pronoun takes after the 'y' sound. Paired with a verb of turning, this 'upon/toward him' marks the person the action reaches.

11.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
11.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

12.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
12.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.
12.root: — (proper name)

13.meaning: An intensive adjective/name meaning 'much-forgiving, ever-ready to forgive, one who veils and pardons faults again and again'. The form stresses abundance, so it conveys forgiveness as a constant, far-reaching quality.
13.grammar: An intensive adjective (the ghafūr 'doer-in-abundance' pattern), used as a divine attribute of Allah. The -un ending is nunation in the nominative case: it marks the word as indefinite and in the nominative, the case typically used for the subject or for a predicate that describes the subject.
13.root: غ-ف-ر (gh-f-r) — to cover, veil, forgive

14.meaning: Most merciful, ever-merciful; one whose mercy is constant and abundant. As a divine attribute it denotes Allah's enduring, all-embracing compassion toward His creation.
14.grammar: An intensive adjective on the form faʿīl ('abundantly/constantly merciful'). The ending -un (tanwīn) is the nominative case with indefiniteness, the form typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing it ('[He] is most merciful').
14.root: ر-ح-م (r-ḥ-m) — mercy, compassion, womb-like tenderness

1.meaning: 'Did not…?' — a particle combining a question with negation, used to ask 'Have I/has he not…?', often expecting agreement or serving as a gentle reminder.
1.grammar: An interrogative prefix 'a-' ('?') joined to the negation 'lam'. 'lam' negates a verb and places it firmly in the past ('did not'), and grammatically puts the following present-tense verb into the jussive (clipped) form. Together they form a rhetorical or confirming question.

2.meaning: You know, you come to know, you are aware — to possess knowledge or to realise/recognise something.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb in the 'you' (masculine singular) form. The ta- prefix marks a second-person singular subject ('you'). The bare ending (no final -u) is the jussive/conditional mood, the shortened form used after conditional or command-type particles rather than as a plain statement.

3.meaning: An emphatic particle meaning 'that' (as in 'I know that...') or 'indeed/surely.' It introduces a statement and gives it certainty and emphasis, presenting what follows as an established fact.
3.grammar: An emphatic particle that introduces a noun-clause ('that...'). It puts the following noun into the accusative case and lends the whole statement a sense of certainty and assertion. It typically comes after verbs of knowing, saying, or informing.

4.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
4.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

5.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
5.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

6.meaning: Kingdom, dominion, sovereign rule — full ownership and authority over a realm; the right and power to command and dispose.
6.grammar: A singular noun. The final -u marks the nominative case, used when the noun is the subject of a sentence or the thing being identified ('the dominion is …'). The absence of nunation here points to its being made definite by a following possessor in a genitive link.
6.root: م-ل-ك (m-l-k) — to own, rule; kingship, dominion

7.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
7.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.
7.root: س-م-و (s-m-w) — height, sky

8.meaning: 'And the earth' — the connective 'and' joined to 'the earth', meaning the ground, land, or the world beneath the sky.
8.grammar: The connective 'wa-' ('and') with the definite feminine noun 'al-arḍ' ('the earth'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the earth') or follows a preposition, here matching the case of what it is joined to.

9.meaning: 'and He punishes / chastises' — to inflict painful penalty. The leading 'wa' joins it to what comes before ('and …').
9.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'), from the intensive (doubled-middle) pattern conveying forceful action, joined by 'wa' ('and'). The separate final -u is the indicative ending, marking a plain, ongoing statement ('he punishes').

10.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
10.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

11.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'he wills, he wishes, he chooses' — to want or intend something by one's own decision.
11.grammar: A present/ongoing action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular, and the final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact ('he wills'), as opposed to a command or a verb governed by 'that.'
11.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — willing, wishing; the root behind 'thing' (shayʾ)

12.meaning: 'And He forgives / and He pardons.' The verb denotes covering over and wiping away sins; ghafr is forgiveness that both conceals the fault and remits its punishment. Prefixed with 'and'.
12.grammar: The wa- prefix means 'and' (sometimes 'but'). The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'). The final -u vowel marks the indicative, the ordinary present-tense form expressing an ongoing or habitual action ('He forgives').
12.root: غ-ف-ر (gh-f-r) — to forgive, to cover over (sin)

13.meaning: 'for whoever / to the one who' — the preposition 'for/to' joined with the relative word 'who', introducing the person(s) about whom something is said.
13.grammar: A preposition ('for/to') combined with the relative/interrogative word 'man' ('who, whoever'). Together they single out a person or group as the focus ('for the one(s) who...').

14.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'he wills, he wishes, he chooses' — to want or intend something by one's own decision.
14.grammar: A present/ongoing action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular, and the final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact ('he wills'), as opposed to a command or a verb governed by 'that.'
14.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — willing, wishing; the root behind 'thing' (shayʾ)

15.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
15.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
15.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

16.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
16.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

17.meaning: 'every,' 'each,' or 'all' — a word expressing totality or completeness. It indicates the entirety of something: when joined to a singular indefinite noun it means 'every (single) one,' and when joined to a definite noun it can mean 'all of' or 'the whole of.'
17.grammar: A noun of totality. The final '-i' ending is genitive (the 'of/possession' case): it marks the word as governed by a preceding preposition or as the first term of a possessive link to a following noun, so it typically reads 'of every…' or 'every…' leading into what follows.

18.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
18.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
18.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

19.meaning: All-powerful, fully able, ever-capable — possessing complete and effective power to do whatever is willed; one whose ability never falls short.
19.grammar: An intensive adjective on the faʿīl pattern, which stresses a deep, abiding quality ('thoroughly able'). The final -un is the indefinite nominative (nunation) — the doubled-n shows no 'the', and the -u base vowel marks the nominative case, used when the word is a subject or a predicate ('… is all-powerful').
19.root: ق-د-ر (q-d-r) — power, ability, measure, decree

1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: 'The Messenger' — one sent with a message; in religious usage, a prophet commissioned by Allah to deliver revelation to people.
2.grammar: 'al-' is the definite article 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the following r, doubling it). 'rasūl' is a noun meaning 'one who is sent, an envoy/messenger'. The final -u is the nominative ending, the case typically marking the subject of a sentence or a word simply being named.

3.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
3.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

4.meaning: A verb meaning 'it grieves you' or 'it makes you sad' — to cause sorrow, distress, or anxiety to a single addressee.
4.grammar: A present/future-tense verb with a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it') marked by the 'ya-' prefix. The vowel-less (jussive) ending on the stem shows it follows a governing particle such as a negative or conditional. The attached '-ka' is the object 'you' (one male).

5.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
5.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

6.meaning: A verb meaning 'they race', 'they hasten', or 'they vie with one another' — to hurry eagerly, often in competition; the form suggests striving and mutual rivalry toward something.

parts.en: hasten / race / compete (Form III verb stem)

6.grammar: A present/future-tense Form III (fāʿala) verb — the long 'ā' after the first root letter often conveys mutual or reciprocal action, here 'to vie/race with one another'. The 'yu-' prefix plus '-ūna' ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject in the indicative mood, used for plain statements of ongoing action (the retained final 'n' shows no particle is governing it).

7.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
7.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
7.root: — (particle)

8.meaning: A noun meaning 'disbelief' or 'rejection of faith' — the deliberate covering over or denial of truth and of Allah; from a root whose core sense is to cover or conceal.
8.grammar: A definite verbal noun ('the disbelief') with the definite article 'al-' and the genitive '-i' ending. The genitive case typically follows a preposition or links this noun to a preceding noun in an 'of/in' relationship. The original root sense is 'to cover', since disbelief covers or hides the truth.
8.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; hence to deny, disbelieve, be ungrateful

9.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
9.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

10.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
10.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

11.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
11.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

12.meaning: We have believed; we have come to faith and trust — to affirm belief, give one's trust, and feel secure in that conviction, stated by a group about themselves.
12.grammar: A past-tense verb on the form-IV pattern (āmana, 'to believe / to have faith'). The ending -nā (a single morpheme, نَا) attached to a past verb marks the subject as 'we'. The doubled 'n' heard in 'āmannā' comes from the verb stem's final 'n' meeting the 'n' that begins the -nā ending.
12.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, security, trust, faith

13.meaning: With their mouths — by means of what they utter or speak aloud (often contrasted with what their hearts truly hold).
13.grammar: A noun preceded by 'bi-' ('with/by') with an attached possessive pronoun. 'Afwāh' is the broken (irregular) plural 'mouths.' The '-i' ending is genitive after the preposition 'bi-'; the suffix '-him' means 'their,' so the whole reads 'with their mouths.'
13.root: ف-و-ه (f-w-h) — mouth, opening; utterance

14.meaning: 'And not' — the conjunction wa- ('and') joined to lam, a particle that negates a verb and pushes its meaning into the completed past ('did not …').
14.grammar: A connector wa- ('and') plus the negative particle lam. Lam negates a following present-tense verb but turns its sense into the past: 'has not / did not …'. It also causes that verb to take the jussive (clipped) ending.

15.meaning: A verb meaning 'to believe', 'to have faith', or 'to place one's trust and security'. Its core sense unites inward faith with the granting of safety and trust.
15.grammar: A present-tense verb with the 'tu-' prefix marking a second-person masculine singular subject ('you'); the 'u' vowel belongs to this verb's pattern (the form used for 'to believe'). The vowel-less ending (jussive) is the shape the verb takes after a negating or questioning particle such as 'lam'.
15.root: ا-م-ن / ء-م-ن (’-m-n) — safety, trust, faith

16.meaning: 'Their hearts' — the hearts belonging to a masculine plural group. In Qur'anic usage the 'heart' is the seat of understanding, intention, feeling, and faith, not merely the physical organ.
16.grammar: A plural noun ('hearts') in the nominative, shown by the -u before the pronoun, which typically marks it as the subject of a sentence. The attached 'hum' means 'their' (a group of males or mixed group), giving 'their hearts.'
16.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — heart; to turn over, fluctuate

17.meaning: A connector meaning 'and', joined to the preposition 'from / of', introducing a portion or origin — 'and from' or 'and among'.
17.grammar: Two particles: wa- ('and') plus the preposition min ('from, of, among'). Min normally appears as 'min', but its final vowel shifts to 'mina' when the next word begins with the definite article, simply to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

18.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
18.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

19.meaning: 'They became Jews / adopted Judaism', or in the verb's wider sense 'they turned (back) in repentance'. A completed act by a group of taking on the way of the Jewish community.

parts.en: became Jews / turned back (past, masc. plural)

19.grammar: A past-tense verb from a hollow root. The whole form hādū is already 3rd-person masculine plural ('they turned/became Jews'): the long ū plus the final silent alif are the plural marker, so no separate ending is split off. The action is presented as completed; the root carries the idea of turning toward or returning, from which the sense 'to follow Judaism' derives.
19.root: ه-و-د (h-w-d) — turning back, returning; hence following Judaism

20.meaning: An emphatic plural describing people who are habitual, eager listeners — ones who constantly give ear and lend attention. The intensive pattern conveys not mere occasional hearing but a persistent, characteristic inclination toward listening.
20.grammar: An intensive noun-of-agent (faʿʿāl pattern) made plural with the -ūna ending. The -ūna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the nominative (subject) case, signalling that these are the doers/describees of an action. The doubled middle consonant (faʿʿāl) intensifies the meaning to 'one who listens much/eagerly.'
20.root: س-م-ع (s-m-ʿ) — hearing, listening

21.meaning: A prepositional phrase meaning 'to/for falsehood, for the sake of a lie.' It denotes deliberate untruth — fabricated, false speech — with the particle conveying purpose or direction toward it.
21.grammar: A noun preceded by the preposition 'li-' ('to/for') with the definite article 'al-'. The preposition forces the noun into the genitive case, which the -i ending marks. The -i ending here is the case required after a preposition; it indicates the noun is the object of 'li-', expressing purpose, recipient, or direction.
21.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — lying, falsehood

22.meaning: An emphatic plural describing people who are habitual, eager listeners — ones who constantly give ear and lend attention. The intensive pattern conveys not mere occasional hearing but a persistent, characteristic inclination toward listening.
22.grammar: An intensive noun-of-agent (faʿʿāl pattern) made plural with the -ūna ending. The -ūna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the nominative (subject) case, signalling that these are the doers/describees of an action. The doubled middle consonant (faʿʿāl) intensifies the meaning to 'one who listens much/eagerly.'
22.root: س-م-ع (s-m-ʿ) — hearing, listening

23.meaning: 'For a people / for a folk' — directed toward a community or group of human beings considered collectively.
23.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('for/to') joined to a noun 'people.' Because it follows a preposition, the noun takes the genitive, and the tanwīn (the -in ending) marks it as indefinite ('a people'). The whole phrase means 'for a people,' directing something toward that group.
23.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand/rise; a people, community

24.meaning: Others / other ones — additional people distinct from those already mentioned (masculine plural of 'other').
24.grammar: A masculine plural adjective/noun meaning 'others.' The -īna ending is the accusative/genitive form of the masculine plural (its nominative counterpart would be -ūna). This ending typically marks the word as a direct object of a verb or as following a preposition.
24.root: أ-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to come later, to be other/last

25.meaning: A negating particle, 'not', used specifically to deny that an action happened in the past, even though it attaches to a present-tense verb form. It turns 'you do X' into 'you did not do X'.

parts.en: did not (negation of a completed act)

25.grammar: An indeclinable particle that governs the verb after it, putting that verb into the jussive (clipped) mood and giving it past-time meaning. In short: lam + a present-form verb = 'did not [verb]'.

26.meaning: A verb meaning 'they come to you' — an act of approaching or arriving at a second person (masculine singular), with the 'you' built into the word as the goal of the coming.
26.grammar: A present/imperfect verb. The ya-…-ū frame marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). The attached -ka is a pronoun meaning 'you' (one male) and serves as the goal/object of the coming. The verb stands in the jussive (the mood after a conditional particle), where the final 'n' of the indicative plural ending -ūna drops, leaving just -ū.
26.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — coming, arriving

27.meaning: 'They alter, distort, twist, tamper with' — an intensive verb describing deliberately shifting words or meanings away from their correct sense. It is said of a group (third person, 'they') acting repeatedly.

parts.en: he / they — third-person present-tense subject marker

27.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb in an intensive (form II) pattern that adds force or deliberateness to 'distort'. The yu- prefix plus the -ūna ending mark a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). The retained final nūn (-ūna) marks the indicative mood — a plain ongoing statement of fact.
27.root: ح-ر-ف (ḥ-r-f) — edge, to turn aside, to distort

28.meaning: 'The word(s), speech, utterance' — a collective noun for words or statements taken as speech, especially weighty or revealed words.
28.grammar: A definite collective noun ('the words/speech'); the al- prefix means 'the'. The final -a is the accusative ending, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon).
28.root: ك-ل-م (k-l-m) — speech, word, to speak

29.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
29.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

30.meaning: A noun/adverb meaning 'after' — the time or position following something; 'afterward', 'following'.
30.grammar: An adverb of time functioning as a noun, here in the genitive case marked by the final -i. The genitive ending typically appears after a preposition or as the second term of a construct ('after THE …'), linking 'after' to a following noun to specify what it comes after.
30.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — to be after, to follow, distance in place or time

31.meaning: A noun (plural) with an attached possessive 'its/his,' meaning 'its proper places' or 'its rightful positions' — the locations or settings where something belongs. The base word denotes a place where a thing is set down or situated.
31.grammar: A plural noun of place (mafʿil pattern, here broken-plural mawāḍiʿ) with the possessive pronoun '-hi' ('its/his'). The -i ending before the pronoun shows the genitive case (typical when the noun follows a preposition or is possessed). The pronoun '-hi' takes the 'i'-vowel form because it follows that genitive -i sound.

32.meaning: 'They say / they keep saying' — a present-tense verb of speaking: to say, utter, or assert in words.
32.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they'), from a hollow (middle-vowel) root. The ya- prefix marks the 'they/he' class, the -ū marks the masculine plural subject, and the -na ending signals the ordinary (indicative) present, 'they are saying.'

33.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
33.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

34.meaning: You (plural) were given / have been granted — the passive sense that 'you all' received something bestowed, without naming the giver.
34.grammar: A completed (past-tense) passive verb ('were given' rather than 'gave'). The '-tum' ending marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all'). As a passive, the subject is the receiver of what was granted, not the giver.
34.root: ء-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; to bring, to give

35.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
35.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

36.meaning: A command meaning 'so take it / then seize it,' addressed to a group. The leading particle adds a sense of 'so/then,' linking the order to something preceding as its consequence, and 'it' is built in as the thing to be taken.
36.grammar: An imperative (command) verb. The 'fa-' prefix means 'so/then,' marking what follows as a result or consequence. The -ū ending directs the command to a masculine plural 'you all.' The attached '-hu' is the object pronoun 'it/him.' The verb 'khudh' is an irregular imperative whose initial root letter is dropped in the command.

37.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
37.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

38.meaning: The particle 'lam', a negating word used to push a verb into the past: it means 'did not' / 'has not'. Though it sits before a present-tense verb form, it negates the action as something that did not happen.
38.grammar: 'lam' is a negating particle that governs a following present-tense verb but gives it past meaning ('did not …'). It also puts that verb into the shortened (jussive) form. 'lam' itself carries no ending.

39.meaning: A passive verb meaning 'you are given it' — to have something handed or granted to you. The subject receives rather than acts, and 'it' is the thing bestowed.
39.grammar: A present-tense passive verb. The 'tu-' prefix with the 'u-a' vowelling marks the passive voice ('are given' rather than 'give') and a second-person 'you' subject. Because the final root letter is weak, the passive plural appears as the vowel sequence -aw- (in the full form tūtawna) rather than the active plural -ūna; it is the passive-voice plural morpheme, not an active subject marker. A governing particle puts the verb in the jussive, and the attached '-hu' is the object 'it,' the thing given.

40.meaning: A command meaning 'so beware! / then be on your guard!,' addressed to a group. It urges caution and wariness, with the leading particle marking it as a consequence ('so/then').
40.grammar: An imperative (command) verb with the connective prefix 'fa-' ('so/then'), which presents the order as a result of what came before.
