The stem carries a helping initial vowel (the written 'i'). The -ū ending addresses a masculine plural 'you all'; the silent alif after it is a spelling convention for the plural imperative.

41.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
41.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

42.meaning: A verb meaning '(if) He/it intends, wills, or desires' — to purpose or aim at something. The form IV (causative) pattern denotes deliberate volition, the directing of one's will toward an outcome.

parts.en: helping vowel (jussive, before a following word)

42.grammar: A present-tense verb (form IV, 'to will/intend') with a third-person masculine singular 'he' subject shown by the 'yu-' prefix. Its base jussive form would end in a silent (sukūn) consonant; the final -i here is a 'helping vowel' added only to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a cluster, and does not change the verb's jussive (conditional) status. The triliteral root is most commonly given as ر-و-د (r-w-d), though some grammarians treat the root of this verb as disputed.
42.root: ر-و-د (r-w-d) — seeking, willing, intending (root sometimes treated as disputed)

43.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
43.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

44.meaning: A noun with an attached 'his/its,' meaning 'his trial' or 'his testing/temptation.' The base word denotes a trial, affliction, or seductive test that probes and tries a person — sometimes through hardship, sometimes through allure or discord.
44.grammar: A feminine noun carrying the possessive pronoun '-hu' ('his/its'). The -a ending before the pronoun marks the accusative case, the form a noun takes when it is the direct object of a verb. The feminine ending (tāʾ marbūṭa) is pronounced 't' when a suffix is attached.

45.meaning: So never / then never — a connector 'so/then' joined to an emphatic particle of negation that denies a future action absolutely: 'will never (at all)'.
45.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector meaning 'so/then', linking to what precedes. 'lan' negates a following present-tense verb and casts it into the future with emphatic force ('will never'); it also puts that verb into the subjunctive, which shows up as a final '-a' on the verb.

46.meaning: A verb meaning 'you own / you have power over / you control' — to possess and have command of something, whether property or the ability to bring it about. It conveys ownership joined with effective authority.
46.grammar: A present-tense verb with the 'ta-' prefix marking a second-person masculine singular 'you' subject. The final -a ending is the subjunctive, used when the verb follows certain particles (such as those meaning 'that,' 'so that,' or 'never will'); it typically expresses a non-factual, dependent, or future-negated action rather than a plain statement.

47.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
47.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

48.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
48.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

49.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
49.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

50.meaning: A thing; something or anything. With a negation it commonly amounts to 'nothing at all.'
50.grammar: A singular masculine noun, indefinite ('a thing'). The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative, often used here as an object or an adverbial 'in any respect / at all.'

51.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'those' — pointing to people or things that are distant or already known. It singles out a group ('those ones', 'it is those who').
51.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those'. It is fixed in form (no case endings). The -ka element signals distance/remoteness, pointing to something far off or notable. It can refer to people of either gender.

52.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
52.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

53.meaning: A negating particle, 'not', used specifically to deny that an action happened in the past, even though it attaches to a present-tense verb form. It turns 'you do X' into 'you did not do X'.

parts.en: did not (negation of a completed act)

53.grammar: An indeclinable particle that governs the verb after it, putting that verb into the jussive (clipped) mood and giving it past-time meaning. In short: lam + a present-form verb = 'did not [verb]'.

54.meaning: A verb meaning '(if) He/it intends, wills, or desires' — to purpose or aim deliberately at an outcome. The form IV (causative) pattern expresses the directing of one's will toward a thing.

parts.en: helping vowel (jussive, before a following word)

54.grammar: A present-tense verb (form IV) with a third-person masculine singular 'he' subject marked by the 'yu-' prefix. Its jussive form would normally end in a silent consonant; the -i is a 'helping vowel' added solely to smooth the join with a following word that begins with a consonant cluster, and does not alter the verb's jussive (conditional) state. The triliteral root is most commonly given as ر-و-د (r-w-d), though some grammarians treat the root of this verb as disputed.
54.root: ر-و-د (r-w-d) — seeking, willing, intending (root sometimes treated as disputed)

55.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
55.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

56.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
56.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

57.meaning: A verb meaning 'He purifies / cleanses / makes pure' — to remove impurity, sin, or defilement and render something clean, wholesome, and free of taint. The doubled-consonant form gives it a thorough, effective sense.
57.grammar: A present-tense intensive verb (form II, with a doubled middle root letter) meaning 'to purify thoroughly.' The 'yu-' prefix marks a third-person masculine singular 'he' subject. The -a ending is the subjunctive, used after particles meaning 'that / so that'; it marks the action as dependent or purposed rather than a standalone statement.

58.meaning: 'Their hearts.' The noun denotes the heart as the inner seat of feeling, understanding, and intention; its very name evokes turning and fluctuation, since the heart is what shifts and changes.
58.grammar: A plural noun ('hearts') with the attached possessive -hum ('their'). The -a vowel on the noun is the accusative ending, which typically marks the word as the object of a verb (the thing being acted upon).
58.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — to turn over, change; hence the heart, which turns

59.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
59.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

60.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
60.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

61.meaning: 'The nearer (life) / this world' — literally 'the nearest/lowest,' a name for the present worldly life as opposed to the Hereafter.
61.grammar: The definite article al- with dunyā, a feminine superlative/elative adjective ('the nearest, the lowest') used as a name for the present world. Its ending (alif maqṣūra) is invariable — it does not change for case — and it commonly describes 'the [worldly] life.'
61.root: د-ن-و (d-n-w) — nearness, being close or low; hence the 'near' present world

62.meaning: 'Disgrace / humiliation / shame' — a state of public abasement and dishonour.
62.grammar: A verbal noun, masculine singular. The -un (tanwīn ḍamm) ending is nominative and indefinite, typical of a subject or predicate ('[there is] a disgrace'). It names the condition of being shamed and humiliated.
62.root: خ-ز-ي (kh-z-y) — disgrace, humiliation, being put to shame

63.meaning: A connector meaning 'and', joined to a phrase 'for them' or 'they have' — literally 'and to/for them', expressing that something belongs to or is owed to a group.
63.grammar: Two prefixes on a pronoun: wa- means 'and', and the preposition la- means 'for/to'. The pronoun -hum means 'them', a group of males or a mixed group. The preposition la- attached to a pronoun commonly conveys possession or entitlement — 'they have' or 'for them (belongs) …'.

64.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
64.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

65.meaning: The Hereafter — the final, lasting life that comes after death and the present world; literally 'the last/latter (abode or life)', as opposed to the first, nearer life.
65.grammar: A feminine adjective used as a noun, with 'the'. The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF …'), or follows a preposition or oath particle.
65.root: ء-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to be last, to come after, end

66.meaning: Painful punishment, torment, or chastisement — suffering imposed as a penalty.
66.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The ending -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and in the nominative case, typically used for the subject or for the thing said to exist.

67.meaning: Great, immense, mighty — vast in magnitude or importance. Describes something tremendous, whether in size, weight, or gravity.
67.grammar: An adjective on the intensive 'faʿīl' pattern, conveying a strong, established quality. The '-un' ending marks it nominative and indefinite; as an adjective it typically agrees with and describes an indefinite noun ('a great …').

1.meaning: An emphatic plural describing people who are habitual, eager listeners — ones who constantly give ear and lend attention. The intensive pattern conveys not mere occasional hearing but a persistent, characteristic inclination toward listening.
1.grammar: An intensive noun-of-agent (faʿʿāl pattern) made plural with the -ūna ending. The -ūna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the nominative (subject) case, signalling that these are the doers/describees of an action. The doubled middle consonant (faʿʿāl) intensifies the meaning to 'one who listens much/eagerly.'

2.meaning: A prepositional phrase meaning 'to/for falsehood, for the sake of a lie.' It denotes deliberate untruth — fabricated, false speech — with the particle conveying purpose or direction toward it.
2.grammar: A noun preceded by the preposition 'li-' ('to/for') with the definite article 'al-'. The preposition forces the noun into the genitive case, which the -i ending marks. The -i ending here is the case required after a preposition; it indicates the noun is the object of 'li-', expressing purpose, recipient, or direction.

3.meaning: An emphatic plural meaning 'voracious devourers / gluttonous consumers' — people who greedily and habitually eat up or consume. The intensive pattern stresses excess and constancy in the consuming.
3.grammar: An intensive noun-of-agent (faʿʿāl pattern, doubled middle consonant) made plural with the -ūna ending. The -ūna marks a sound masculine plural in the nominative (subject) case. The faʿʿāl pattern intensifies the meaning to 'one who eats/consumes voraciously and habitually.'

4.meaning: A prepositional phrase meaning 'of / for the unlawful gain' — denoting forbidden, ill-gotten earnings such as bribery or illicit profit. The base word signifies that which is illegitimate and, in its sense, ruinous to the one who takes it.
4.grammar: A noun with the definite article 'al-' preceded by the preposition 'li-' ('to/for/of'). The 'l' of the article assimilates into the following 's' (a 'sun letter'), shown by the doubling. The preposition puts the noun in the genitive case, which the -i ending marks; this is the case a noun takes as the object of a preposition.

5.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'fa-' ('then', 'so', 'but') drawing a consequence, joined to the conditional particle 'in' ('if'). Together: 'then if …', 'but if …'.
5.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that signals a result or transition ('then/so'). 'in' is the conditional particle 'if', introducing a supposed condition. Both are indeclinable particles with no case ending.

6.meaning: they came to you — to arrive at or approach someone. This combines the verb 'they came' with an attached 'you', i.e. they presented themselves before a single male addressee.
6.grammar: A past-tense Form I verb. The -ū ending is the masculine-plural subject ('they'), marking completed action. The attached -ka is an object pronoun, 'you' (a single male). The plural normally carries a silent trailing alif, which drops before the attached pronoun. The hamzah is the final root letter.

7.meaning: A command meaning 'so judge / then decide / then rule,' addressed to one person. It calls for rendering a verdict or governing decision. The leading particle adds 'so/then,' tying the command to what precedes as its consequence.
7.grammar: An imperative (command) verb addressed to a second-person masculine singular 'you.' The 'fa-' prefix means 'so/then,' marking the order as a result of what came before. The stem carries a written helping vowel at its start; the verb ends in a silent consonant (sukūn), which is the normal form of a singular command.
7.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — judging, ruling, wisdom

8.meaning: An adverb of place meaning 'between' or 'among', here joined to the attached pronoun 'them'; together it conveys 'between them / amongst them', signalling something situated in the midst of a group or shared among parties.
8.grammar: An adverb of place (ẓarf) ending in -a, the accusative marker typical of such adverbs, indicating a location or relationship. The attached suffix '-hum' is a possessive/object pronoun meaning 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group).
8.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies in the midst

9.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
9.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

10.meaning: A command meaning 'turn away / avert yourself / decline,' addressed to one person. It denotes deliberately turning one's face or attention aside from something, withholding engagement.

parts.en: turn away! avert! (command stem, form IV)

10.grammar: An imperative (command) verb of form IV (the 'a-' at the front is part of this pattern, meaning roughly 'to turn oneself away'). It is addressed to a second-person masculine singular 'you' and ends in a silent consonant (sukūn), the standard ending for a singular command.
10.root: ع-ر-ض (ʿ-r-ḍ) — breadth, presenting; (form IV) turning away

11.meaning: From them; away from them; concerning them. The preposition ʿan conveys moving away from, departing from, or 'on behalf of / concerning', combined with the pronoun 'them'.
11.grammar: A preposition joined to the attached pronoun -hum, 'them' (referring to a group, grammatically masculine plural). The preposition ʿan basically signals separation or removal ('away from'), and can also mean 'about/concerning' or 'on behalf of' depending on usage.

12.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
12.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

13.meaning: A verb meaning 'you turn away / you avert yourself / you decline' — to face aside from something or withhold one's attention. The form conveys a deliberate turning of oneself away.
13.grammar: A present-tense verb of form IV ('to turn away') with the 'tu-' prefix marking a second-person masculine singular 'you' subject. It ends in a silent consonant (sukūn), which marks the jussive — the form used after conditional particles (such as 'if') or commands/prohibitions, expressing a hypothetical or contingent action rather than a plain fact.
13.root: ع-ر-ض (ʿ-r-ḍ) — breadth, presenting; (form IV) turning away

14.meaning: From them; away from them; concerning them. The preposition ʿan conveys moving away from, departing from, or 'on behalf of / concerning', combined with the pronoun 'them'.
14.grammar: A preposition joined to the attached pronoun -hum, 'them' (referring to a group, grammatically masculine plural). The preposition ʿan basically signals separation or removal ('away from'), and can also mean 'about/concerning' or 'on behalf of' depending on usage.
14.root: — (a preposition; no triliteral verbal root)

15.meaning: So never / then never — a connector 'so/then' joined to an emphatic particle of negation that denies a future action absolutely: 'will never (at all)'.
15.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector meaning 'so/then', linking to what precedes. 'lan' negates a following present-tense verb and casts it into the future with emphatic force ('will never'); it also puts that verb into the subjunctive, which shows up as a final '-a' on the verb.
15.root: — (particle — no root)

16.meaning: A verb meaning 'they harm you / they injure you' — to do damage or detriment to a second person (masculine singular), with the 'you' built in as the one harmed.
16.grammar: A present-tense verb with a doubled final root letter. The ya-…-ū frame marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). The attached '-ka' is the object pronoun 'you' (one male), the one harmed. A governing particle places the verb in the jussive, where the plural's usual final 'n' drops, leaving -ū.

17.meaning: A thing; something or anything. With a negation it commonly amounts to 'nothing at all.'
17.grammar: A singular masculine noun, indefinite ('a thing'). The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative, often used here as an object or an adverbial 'in any respect / at all.'

18.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
18.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

19.meaning: A verb meaning 'you judged / you decided / you ruled' — a completed act of rendering a verdict or governing decision, performed by the person addressed.
19.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb describing a completed action. The suffix '-ta' marks the doer as second-person masculine singular 'you.' In the past tense, person and subject are shown by these endings attached after the stem rather than by a prefix.
19.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — judging, ruling, wisdom

20.meaning: A command meaning 'so judge / then decide / then rule,' addressed to one person. It calls for rendering a verdict or governing decision. The leading particle adds 'so/then,' tying the command to what precedes as its consequence.
20.grammar: An imperative (command) verb addressed to a second-person masculine singular 'you.' The 'fa-' prefix means 'so/then,' marking the order as a result of what came before. The stem carries a written helping vowel at its start; the verb ends in a silent consonant (sukūn), which is the normal form of a singular command.
20.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — judging, ruling, wisdom

21.meaning: An adverb of place meaning 'between' or 'among', here joined to the attached pronoun 'them'; together it conveys 'between them / amongst them', signalling something situated in the midst of a group or shared among parties.
21.grammar: An adverb of place (ẓarf) ending in -a, the accusative marker typical of such adverbs, indicating a location or relationship. The attached suffix '-hum' is a possessive/object pronoun meaning 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group).
21.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies in the midst

22.meaning: In/with justice and equity — 'qisṭ' is fair, balanced dealing: giving each their due in full measure, without wronging anyone.
22.grammar: A masculine noun ('justice, equity') governed by the preposition 'bi-' ('in/with') and made definite by 'al-' ('the'). The final -i ending is genitive, the case a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun in an 'of' relationship.
22.root: ق-س-ط (q-s-ṭ) — justice, equity, fair measure

23.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
23.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

24.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
24.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

25.meaning: He loves / likes / holds dear. To have affection for and approval of something or someone.
25.grammar: A present-tense verb in the fourth pattern, third-person masculine singular ('he…'). The yu- prefix signals a single masculine subject, and the final -u ending marks the indicative mood, presenting the action as an established fact or ongoing reality.
25.root: ح-ب-ب (ḥ-b-b) — love, affection; to hold dear

26.meaning: A noun (plural) meaning 'those who act justly / the equitable ones' — people who deal fairly and give everyone their due, establishing balance and justice. The form names them as doers of just dealing.

parts.en: one who acts justly (form IV agent)

26.grammar: A doer-noun (active participle, form IV — 'one who deals equitably') with the definite article 'al-,' made plural with the -īna ending. The -īna marks a sound masculine plural in the accusative/genitive case — the form used when the noun is a direct object or follows a preposition, as opposed to the -ūna form used for the subject.
26.root: ق-س-ط (q-s-ṭ) — justice, equity, fairness

1.meaning: A phrase: 'and how…' — 'how?' is a question word asking about the manner, way, or state of something; with the connector 'and' prefixed.
1.grammar: An interrogative ('how?') asking about manner or condition, preceded by the connector 'wa' ('and'). This question word is invariable — it does not change for case — and it always carries a fixed '-a' ending. It can express genuine inquiry or astonishment.

2.meaning: A verb meaning 'they make you a judge / they appoint you to arbitrate / they submit to your judgment' — a group seeking a second person (masculine singular) to rule between them. The intensive form denotes installing someone as decision-maker, with 'you' built in as the appointed one.

parts.en: they make (someone) a judge (present, form II)

2.grammar: A present-tense intensive/causative verb (form II, doubled middle root letter — 'to make someone a judge'). The 'yu-' prefix with the -ūna ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'); the full -ūna ending (with its 'n') shows the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact, not governed by a subjunctive or jussive particle. The attached '-ka' is the object 'you,' the one appointed.

3.meaning: A small phrase meaning 'and with them / while in their possession is…' — combining 'and/while' with a word denoting nearness, presence, or possession ('at, with, in the keeping of'), plus 'them.' It conveys that something is present at hand with a group.

parts.en: with, at, in the possession of

3.grammar: The connective 'wa-' ('and/while') joined to 'ʿinda,' a word of place/possession meaning 'with, at, in the keeping of.' 'ʿinda' always carries the -a ending as a fixed adverb of place (it tells where/with whom something is). The attached '-hum' ('them') takes the linking vowel 'u' (becoming '-humu') to ease pronunciation before a following word.

4.meaning: A proper noun: the Torah (al-Tawrāt) — the scripture revealed to Moses (Mūsā).
4.grammar: A definite proper noun carrying the prefix al- ('the'); its 'l' sound assimilates into the following 't'. The -u ending is the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence (e.g. the thing that 'was sent down').

5.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
5.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

6.meaning: A noun meaning 'the judgment, ruling, decree, or wisdom' — an authoritative decision or command, and by extension the sound wisdom behind it. It denotes the verdict that settles a matter or the governing rule that decides it.
6.grammar: A verbal noun (the abstract 'act/result of judging'). The -u ending marks the nominative case, the form a noun takes when it is the subject of a sentence or the thing being identified (e.g., after 'is'). It signals the word is functioning as a doer or topic rather than an object.

7.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
7.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

8.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
8.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

9.meaning: A verb meaning 'they turn away / they turn their backs / they take charge and turn aside' — a group turning themselves away from something. The form (taking-as-master) carries the sense of turning away in aversion, or alternatively of assuming control.
9.grammar: A present-tense reflexive verb (form V, 'to turn oneself away / take as a master'). The 'ya-' prefix with the plural ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). Because the verb's final root letter is weak, the plural ending appears as '-awna' rather than '-ūna'; the retained 'n' shows the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact.

10.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
10.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

11.meaning: A noun/adverb meaning 'after' — the time or position following something; 'afterward', 'following'.
11.grammar: An adverb of time functioning as a noun, here in the genitive case marked by the final -i. The genitive ending typically appears after a preposition or as the second term of a construct ('after THE …'), linking 'after' to a following noun to specify what it comes after.
11.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — to be after, to follow, distance in place or time

12.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
12.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

13.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
13.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.
13.root: — (relative pronoun / particle)

14.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'those' — pointing to people or things that are distant or already known. It singles out a group ('those ones', 'it is those who').
14.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those'. It is fixed in form (no case endings). The -ka element signals distance/remoteness, pointing to something far off or notable. It can refer to people of either gender.

15.meaning: Refers to 'the believers' — those who have faith, who trust and affirm Allah and what He has revealed. The whole word is prefixed with 'with/in/by', so it carries the sense 'with/in the believers'.
15.grammar: An active participle in the plural, made definite by 'al-' (the) and governed by the preposition 'bi' (with/in/by). The '-īna' ending marks a masculine sound plural in the non-subject (accusative/genitive) state; after a preposition like 'bi' it functions as a genitive ('with/in the believers'). The 'mu-' prefix marks it as a doer — 'one who brings about faith,' i.e. a believer.
15.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — to be secure, to trust, to have faith

1.meaning: A two-part expression: an emphatic particle that strongly affirms and confirms a statement ('truly, indeed, certainly'), fused with the attached pronoun 'we.' Together: 'truly we…' / 'indeed we…'
1.grammar: The particle inna gives strong emphasis and certainty to the clause it opens. The attached -ā is the pronoun 'we,' serving as the subject being emphasized: 'truly we…'

2.meaning: We sent down — to cause something to descend or be revealed from a higher source to a lower; classically used of revelation sent down from on high.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb of the causative (fourth) form, meaning to make something come down. The attached -nā is the subject pronoun 'we', marking the action as completed and done by a 'we' (a form of majestic/collective speech when used of Allah).
2.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, come down, be sent down

3.meaning: The Torah: the scripture revealed to the Prophet Moses. A proper name for that divinely revealed Book.
3.grammar: A proper noun (a name of a revealed Book). It carries the definite article al-, whose l (the lām of the article) assimilates into the following t sound, since t is a 'solar' letter that absorbs the article's lām. The final -a ending is accusative, the case typically used for the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or after certain particles.
3.root: — (proper name of a scripture; commonly treated as having no Arabic triliteral root)

4.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
4.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

5.meaning: Guidance — right direction, the showing of the correct way and the leading along it. The term combines pointing out the path and granting success in following it; more than mere information, it is direction toward what is right.

parts.en: indefinite (tanwin) ending on a shortened final vowel

5.grammar: An indefinite masculine singular noun. The -an (tanwin) ending marks indefiniteness — 'a guidance' rather than 'the guidance'. Because the word ends in a weak final letter, its case is not audibly distinguished, so this single form covers more than one grammatical position.

6.meaning: 'And light' — radiance or illumination; figuratively, guidance and clarity that dispel darkness. The leading 'wa' is the connector 'and'.
6.grammar: A singular masculine noun joined by 'wa' (and). The '-un' ending (nunation, tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a light' / 'light') and in the nominative state, which is the form a word takes when it is the subject or otherwise stands as a naming/predicate word rather than an object.
6.root: ن-و-ر (n-w-r) — light, to give light, illumination

7.meaning: He judges / He will judge; He decides, rules, and decrees with authority — passing a binding verdict and governing a matter wisely.
7.grammar: A present/future-tense verb, 'he judges/will judge,' describing a single male subject (or 'He,' of Allah). The ya- prefix marks the third-person masculine singular ('he'), and the final -u marks the indicative mood — an actual, ongoing, or future action.
7.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge, decide, rule; wisdom and governance

8.meaning: with it / by it — a preposition meaning 'with' or 'by means of' joined to a pronoun referring to a single feminine (or grammatically feminine) thing.
8.grammar: The bi- prefix is a preposition meaning 'with', 'by', or 'by means of'. The attached -hā is an object pronoun meaning 'it' or 'her', referring to something feminine in gender. Together they mean 'with it' or 'by means of it'.

9.meaning: 'The prophets' — those chosen by Allah to receive revelation and convey His message to humanity.
9.grammar: A definite masculine sound (regular) plural noun with the prefixed article 'al-' ('the'). The ending -ūna is the nominative case for this kind of plural, the form used when the noun is the subject or doer of a sentence ('the prophets [did/were] …').
9.root: ن-ب-ا (n-b-ʾ) — news, tidings; a prophet conveys news from Allah

10.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
10.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

11.meaning: They submitted/surrendered (to Allah): a completed act, by a group, of submitting and giving oneself over to Allah — i.e., becoming Muslim.
11.grammar: A past-tense verb of the causative pattern (Form IV) meaning 'to submit/surrender oneself (to Allah)'. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'), expressing a completed action.

12.meaning: A compound meaning 'for those who' or 'belonging to those who'. It joins the preposition 'for/to' with a masculine plural relative pronoun ('those who'), introducing a clause that describes a group of people by something they do or possess.
12.grammar: The prefix 'li-' is a preposition meaning 'for', 'to', or expressing ownership/benefit ('belonging to'). The relative pronoun is 'alladhīna' ('those who'), but when 'li-' attaches to it the connecting hamza of 'al-' drops out and the two lām sounds merge into one doubled lām, so the form is written and read 'lilladhīna' rather than 'li-alladhīna'. 'alladhīna' has a fixed shape and does not change for case.

13.meaning: 'They became Jews / adopted Judaism', or in the verb's wider sense 'they turned (back) in repentance'. A completed act by a group of taking on the way of the Jewish community.

parts.en: became Jews / turned back (past, masc. plural)

13.grammar: A past-tense verb from a hollow root. The whole form hādū is already 3rd-person masculine plural ('they turned/became Jews'): the long ū plus the final silent alif are the plural marker, so no separate ending is split off. The action is presented as completed; the root carries the idea of turning toward or returning, from which the sense 'to follow Judaism' derives.
13.root: ه-و-د (h-w-d) — turning back, returning; hence following Judaism

14.meaning: 'The rabbis' — devout religious teachers and masters of the divine law; learned men devoted to nurturing others in religion. The leading 'wa' is 'and'.
14.grammar: A masculine sound plural made definite by 'al-' (the) and joined by 'wa' (and). The '-ūna' ending marks the plural in the subject (nominative) state — the form used when the word is the doer or the thing being named. The pattern is a relational/adjectival noun built on 'rabb' (lord/master), denoting men dedicated to the Lord and to mastery of religion.
14.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, master, be lord over

15.meaning: 'The scholars' — learned religious authorities, especially expert jurists and keepers of the Scripture. The leading 'wa' is 'and'.
15.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of 'ḥabr' (a learned man, a religious scholar), made definite by 'al-' (the) and joined by 'wa' (and). The final '-u' marks the nominative — the state a noun takes when it is the subject or the thing being named.
15.root: ح-ب-ر (ḥ-b-r) — learning, scholarship, fine adornment

16.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
16.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

17.meaning: 'They were entrusted / made to safeguard' — they were given something into their keeping to guard and preserve. The form conveys that the safeguarding was assigned to them by another.

parts.en: were entrusted to keep / made to guard

17.grammar: A past-tense verb in the passive voice ('were entrusted/made to safeguard'), built on the 'ist-' (Form X) pattern. In its active sense Form X often carries the idea of seeking or asking for something, but here the verb is passive: the 'u-i' vowel pattern (us-tuḥ-fiẓū) makes the subject the receiver of the action — they did not seek the trust but were charged with it. The '-ū' ending means 'they' (a masculine plural group).
17.root: ح-ف-ظ (ḥ-f-ẓ) — to guard, keep, preserve, protect

18.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
18.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
18.root: — (preposition)

19.meaning: A scripture or book; in particular a written revelation. The word denotes something written down and consigned to record — a 'Book' in the sense of a divinely sent, recorded scripture, also carrying the broader sense of a binding decree or anything set down in writing.
19.grammar: A masculine singular noun. The final -i ending is genitive (the 'of' case): it typically marks the word as linked to a following noun ('… OF …'), or as governed by a preceding preposition or oath particle.
19.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — writing, inscribing, recording

20.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
20.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

21.meaning: A compound meaning 'and they were' or 'and they used to' — it sets a state or habit in the past. The verb 'to be/become' here establishes an ongoing past condition, often paired with a following verb to express habitual action.
21.grammar: A past-tense verb ('to be') in the third-person masculine plural — the -ū ending means 'they' did/were. It commonly conveys a continued past state or habit, especially when followed by another verb. The wa- prefix means 'and.'
21.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to come into being

22.meaning: A preposition fused with a pronoun, meaning 'upon him', 'on him', or 'toward him'. It marks the one to whom an action is directed or upon whom something rests.
22.grammar: The preposition 'upon/on' with an attached object pronoun -hi ('him', third-person masculine singular); its -i vowel is the regular form the pronoun takes after the 'y' sound. Paired with a verb of turning, this 'upon/toward him' marks the person the action reaches.

23.meaning: Witnesses — those present who observe and can testify to what they saw; can also carry the sense of those who bear witness. Plural.
23.grammar: A broken plural on the fuʿalāʾ (فُعَلَاء) pattern, which is a diptote: it takes the -a ending for BOTH the accusative and the genitive and never takes tanwīn (the final 'n'). Because of this, the -a alone does not tell you the case — the word could be a direct object (accusative) or governed by a preposition ('of/among', genitive). Only when made definite or put into construct would it take the ordinary -i in the genitive.
23.root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d) — to witness, observe, testify, be present

24.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
24.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

25.meaning: 'You (all) fear / stand in awe of' — to dread or hold in reverent awe, especially the kind of fear mixed with reverence before something mighty.
25.grammar: A present/imperfect verb addressed to a second person. The 'ta-' prefix marks second person but does not by itself fix the number; the '-ū' ending supplies the plural, so the prefix and suffix together mean 'you all' (do the action). The bare, vowel-shortened ending (rather than the full 'tafʿalūna') shows the verb is in a 'cut-short' state — the form it takes after certain particles (such as those giving a command, a prohibition, or 'so that'). At root it conveys fear blended with reverence.
25.root: خ-ش-ي (kh-sh-y) — to fear, dread, stand in awe

26.meaning: Mankind, humanity, people in general — the collective of human beings.
26.grammar: A definite noun ('the people') with the attached 'al-' ('the'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (a sun letter), which is why the 'n' is doubled — this is a pronunciation effect, not a separate piece. The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the one being acted upon) or the subject of certain particles.
26.root: ن-و-س (n-w-s) — to move/sway; by extension, people

27.meaning: And fear Me: a command to hold reverent awe and dread — to be wary of and revere — directed toward the speaker (Allah), with 'Me' as the object of that fearful reverence.
27.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a masculine plural 'you', joined to the conjunction wa- ('and/but'), with the attached -ni standing for 'Me' as the object. The plural-imperative subject marker is the suffix -ū (a wāw); its alif normally drops when a pronoun is attached, leaving the wāw alone before -ni. So the whole means '(you all) stand in awe of Me'.
27.root: خ-ش-ي (kh-sh-y) — to fear with reverence, to dread, to be in awe

28.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
28.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

29.meaning: You (all) buy, sell, or trade — to exchange one thing for another, giving up something to obtain something else.
29.grammar: A present/non-past verb in a reflexive-exchange (ifta'ala) pattern for masculine plural 'you'. The ta- prefix means 'you', and the -ū ending marks a plural subject; the missing final nūn shows a subjunctive/jussive mood (as after a governing particle).
29.root: ش-ر-ي (sh-r-y) — to buy, sell, barter, exchange

30.meaning: With / by My signs — 'sign(s)' (āyāt: tokens, proofs, communicated verses) joined to a preposition and the possessive 'my'.
30.grammar: The preposition bi- joined to the feminine plural noun 'signs', followed by the possessive ending 'my'. The plural noun is in the genitive after the preposition, and the -ī suffix attributes the signs to the speaker ('my signs').
30.root: أ-ي-ي (ʾ-y-y) — a sign, mark, token

31.meaning: A price, a payment, the value or sum given in exchange for something.
31.grammar: An indefinite noun. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative, commonly marking the noun as the direct object of a verb ('a price').

32.meaning: 'A little / a small amount' — an adjective/noun meaning small in quantity, few, scant, or trifling.
32.grammar: A noun/adjective 'little' in the accusative case with indefinite marking (the -an ending, tanwīn). The accusative commonly marks an object or specifies amount/manner; the doubled -n sound marks it as indefinite, 'a little.'
32.root: ق-ل-ل (q-l-l) — fewness; being little, scant, or small in amount

33.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
33.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

34.meaning: The particle 'lam', a negating word used to push a verb into the past: it means 'did not' / 'has not'. Though it sits before a present-tense verb form, it negates the action as something that did not happen.
34.grammar: 'lam' is a negating particle that governs a following present-tense verb but gives it past meaning ('did not …'). It also puts that verb into the shortened (jussive) form. 'lam' itself carries no ending.

35.meaning: 'He judges / decides / governs' — to give a ruling, pass judgment, or rule with authority over a matter.
35.grammar: A present/imperfect verb with the 'ya-' prefix meaning 'he'. The vowel-less final consonant (a quiescent ending rather than '-kumu') shows it is in the 'cut-short' (jussive) state — the form a verb takes after particles that command, forbid, or set a condition. Its core sense is to render an authoritative decision or ruling.
35.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge, decide, rule with wisdom

36.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
36.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

37.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'he sent down, he caused to descend, he revealed' — used especially of Allah sending down revelation, rain, or blessings from above.
37.grammar: A completed (past) action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the -a ending marks third-person masculine singular. The form IV (causative) pattern means 'to make something come down,' i.e., to send it down.

38.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
38.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

39.meaning: So those / then those are the ones — a connector 'so/then' joined to a demonstrative pointing to a distant or already-mentioned group: 'those people, they (are the ones who)…'.
39.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector meaning 'so/then', often introducing a result or consequence. 'ulā'ika' is a plural demonstrative ('those') pointing to people, typically picking up a previously described group and setting them up as the subject. It is fixed in form and does not change for case.

40.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (masculine plural). Standing on its own, it typically adds emphasis or marks the group out as the focus ('they, specifically', 'it is they who').
40.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It takes no case endings; the base is hum, and the final vowel appears as -u (humu) as a connecting vowel to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a definite article. Standing alone, it commonly emphasises or isolates the subject.

41.meaning: Definite plural noun/participle: 'the disbelievers, those who reject faith' — those who cover over and deny the truth. The pattern names a whole group defined by this attribute.
41.grammar: A definite active participle ('the rejecters'). The '-ūna' ending is the masculine sound plural in the nominative (subject) case — the form a word takes when it is the doer of an action or the subject of a sentence ('the disbelievers [are/do]…').
41.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover over, reject, disbelieve

1.meaning: 'And We decreed / prescribed / wrote down' — to ordain or set down as a binding ruling. At root 'kataba' is 'to write,' and by extension to make something obligatory or fixed. The leading 'wa' is 'and'.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb joined by 'wa' (and). The '-nā' ending attached to a past verb means 'we' did the action. Beyond literal writing, this verb commonly means to prescribe or make binding — to 'write down' something as a decree.
1.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — to write, inscribe, prescribe, ordain

2.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
2.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
2.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

3.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
3.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

4.meaning: An emphatic particle meaning 'that' (as in 'I know that...') or 'indeed/surely.' It introduces a statement and gives it certainty and emphasis, presenting what follows as an established fact.
4.grammar: An emphatic particle that introduces a noun-clause ('that...'). It puts the following noun into the accusative case and lends the whole statement a sense of certainty and assertion. It typically comes after verbs of knowing, saying, or informing.

5.meaning: 'The soul / self / life' — the living person or inner self; by extension a human life.
5.grammar: A singular feminine noun made definite by 'al-' (the); the 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (a 'sun letter'), which is why the 'n' is doubled in pronunciation (an-nafs). The final '-a' marks the accusative — the state a noun takes when it is the object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or otherwise governed into that case. It denotes the self, the soul, or a living person.

6.meaning: 'For / in return for the soul (self, life)' — the living person or life, here governed by the preposition 'bi', which can carry the sense of exchange or recompense ('for, in return for').
6.grammar: The noun 'soul/self/life' made definite by 'al-' (the) and governed by the preposition 'bi'; the 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (a 'sun letter'), so the 'n' is doubled in pronunciation (bin-nafs). The '-i' ending is genitive: the state a noun takes after a preposition such as 'bi' (or when linked to a following noun as '… of …'). With 'bi', the sense is often exchange or compensation — 'for / in return for.'

7.meaning: 'And the eye' — the organ of sight. The leading 'wa' is 'and'.
7.grammar: A singular feminine noun made definite by 'al-' (the) and joined by 'wa' (and). The final '-a' marks the accusative — the state a noun takes when it is the object of a verb or otherwise governed into that case. The word 'ʿayn' also bears wider senses (spring, source), but its core meaning here is the eye.
7.root: ع-ي-ن (ʿ-y-n) — eye, spring, source

8.meaning: 'For / in return for the eye' — the organ of sight, governed by 'bi', which can carry the sense of exchange or recompense.
8.grammar: The noun 'eye' made definite by 'al-' (the) and governed by the preposition 'bi'. The '-i' ending is genitive — the state required after a preposition like 'bi' (or when a noun is linked to a following one as '… of …'). With 'bi' the sense is often exchange or compensation, 'for / in return for.'

9.meaning: 'And the nose' — the organ of smell. The leading 'wa' is 'and'.
9.grammar: A singular masculine noun made definite by 'al-' (the) and joined by 'wa' (and). The final '-a' marks the accusative — the state a noun takes when it is the object of a verb or otherwise governed into that case.
9.root: ء-ن-ف (ʾ-n-f) — nose; by extension pride, anew

10.meaning: 'For / in return for the nose' — the organ of smell, governed by 'bi', which can carry the sense of exchange or recompense.
10.grammar: The noun 'nose' made definite by 'al-' (the) and governed by the preposition 'bi'. The '-i' ending is genitive — the state required after a preposition such as 'bi' (or when a noun links to a following one as '… of …'). With 'bi' the sense is often exchange or compensation, 'for / in return for.'
10.root: ء-ن-ف (ʾ-n-f) — nose; by extension pride, anew

11.meaning: 'And the ear' — the organ of hearing. The leading 'wa' is 'and'.
11.grammar: A singular feminine noun made definite by 'al-' (the) and joined by 'wa' (and). The final '-a' marks the accusative — the state a noun takes when it is the object of a verb or otherwise governed into that case.
11.root: ء-ذ-ن (ʾ-dh-n) — ear; to hear, give heed, give permission

12.meaning: 'For / in return for the ear' — the organ of hearing, governed by 'bi', which can carry the sense of exchange or recompense.
12.grammar: The noun 'ear' made definite by 'al-' (the) and governed by the preposition 'bi'. The '-i' ending is genitive — the state required after a preposition like 'bi' (or when a noun links to a following one as '… of …'). With 'bi' the sense is often exchange or compensation, 'for / in return for.'
12.root: ء-ذ-ن (ʾ-dh-n) — ear; to hear, give heed, give permission

13.meaning: 'And the tooth' — a tooth. The leading 'wa' is 'and'.
13.grammar: A singular feminine noun made definite by 'al-' (the) and joined by 'wa' (and). The 's' is a 'sun letter,' so the 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into it and the 's' is doubled in pronunciation (as-sinn). The final root letter 'n' itself carries a shadda (gemination), so the stem is 'sinn' with a doubled 'n' — reflecting the doubled middle/final letter of the root s-n-n. The final '-a' marks the accusative — the state a noun takes when it is the object of a verb or otherwise governed into that case. By extension the same word can mean 'age' (years of one's life).
13.root: س-ن-ن (s-n-n) — tooth; age; to sharpen, to establish a way

14.meaning: 'For / in return for the tooth' — a tooth, governed by 'bi', which can carry the sense of exchange or recompense.
14.grammar: The noun 'tooth' made definite by 'al-' (the) and governed by the preposition 'bi'. The 's' is a 'sun letter,' so the 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into it and the 's' is doubled in pronunciation (bis-sinn). The final root letter 'n' carries a shadda (gemination), so the stem is 'sinn' with a doubled 'n,' giving 'bis-sinni' with the genitive ending. The '-i' ending is genitive — the state required after a preposition such as 'bi' (or when a noun links to a following one as '… of …'). With 'bi' the sense is often exchange or compensation, 'for / in return for.'
14.root: س-ن-ن (s-n-n) — tooth; age; to sharpen, to establish a way

15.meaning: 'And the wounds' — injuries or cuts to the body. The leading 'wa' is 'and'.
15.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of 'jurḥ' (a wound), made definite by 'al-' (the) and joined by 'wa' (and). The final '-a' marks the accusative — the state a noun takes when it is the object of a verb or otherwise governed into that case.
15.root: ج-ر-ح (j-r-ḥ) — to wound, injure, cut

16.meaning: A noun meaning 'retaliation, equal requital, just retribution' — a like-for-like response in which the penalty matches the offence, following one another in due correspondence.
16.grammar: An indefinite noun. The final -un (nominative with tanwīn/'nunation') marks it as indefinite ('a/some…') and typically as the subject or predicate of a sentence (often 'there is …' or 'X is …').
16.root: ق-ص-ص (q-ṣ-ṣ) — to follow/track, recount; to requite in kind

17.meaning: A compound meaning 'then whoever' or 'so whoever'. It combines 'then/so' with the conditional/relative 'who', introducing whatever person meets a stated condition.
17.grammar: The connector fa- ('then/so', often answering or following a condition) joined to man ('whoever / the one who'), which refers to people and introduces a condition: 'whoever does X…'. man does not change its ending; the clause after it supplies the rest of the meaning.

18.meaning: 'He gave freely / waived as charity / remitted' — to give something up generously as an act of charity, including forgoing one's own due. The form intensifies the root sense of charitable giving.
18.grammar: A past-tense verb in a reflexive/intensive pattern (the 'ta-' shape with a doubled middle root letter), conveying that one takes the act upon oneself — to give as charity or to graciously forgo a right. The final '-a' is the bare past-tense ending meaning 'he' did it.
18.root: ص-د-ق (ṣ-d-q) — truth, sincerity; hence charity given sincerely

19.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
19.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

20.meaning: A two-part phrase: the connector 'then / so' plus the standalone pronoun 'he / it,' used to point back and resume with 'then he…' or 'so it…'
20.grammar: The connector 'fa' ('then/so') plus the detached subject pronoun 'huwa' ('he/it'), 3rd-person masculine singular. Both are indeclinable, with no case ending; the pronoun typically begins or emphasizes a statement about 'he/it.'

21.meaning: 'An expiation / atonement' — something that covers over and makes amends for a wrong or a broken obligation, wiping away its penalty.
21.grammar: A singular feminine noun in an intensive pattern denoting a means of covering or blotting out. The '-un' ending (nunation, tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('an expiation') and in the nominative — the state a noun takes when it is the subject or the thing being named. At root the idea is 'covering over' a sin so as to neutralize it.
21.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; hence to cover over / atone for a sin

22.meaning: A two-part phrase 'for Him' or 'to Him belongs,' expressing possession, ownership, or that something is due to one masculine being.
22.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('for/to/belonging to') with its vowel shifted to 'la-' before the pronoun. The attached -hu means 'Him', so the whole means 'for Him' or 'His'; the preposition signals possession or that something is owed or directed to that person.

23.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
23.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.
23.root: — (pronoun/particle; no triliteral root)

24.meaning: The particle 'lam', a negating word used to push a verb into the past: it means 'did not' / 'has not'. Though it sits before a present-tense verb form, it negates the action as something that did not happen.
24.grammar: 'lam' is a negating particle that governs a following present-tense verb but gives it past meaning ('did not …'). It also puts that verb into the shortened (jussive) form. 'lam' itself carries no ending.

25.meaning: 'He judges / decides / governs' — to give a ruling, pass judgment, or rule with authority over a matter.
25.grammar: A present/imperfect verb with the 'ya-' prefix meaning 'he'. The vowel-less final consonant (a quiescent ending rather than '-kumu') shows it is in the 'cut-short' (jussive) state — the form a verb takes after particles that command, forbid, or set a condition. Its core sense is to render an authoritative decision or ruling.
25.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge, decide, rule with wisdom

26.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
26.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.
26.root: — (particle + relative pronoun)

27.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'he sent down, he caused to descend, he revealed' — used especially of Allah sending down revelation, rain, or blessings from above.
27.grammar: A completed (past) action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the -a ending marks third-person masculine singular. The form IV (causative) pattern means 'to make something come down,' i.e., to send it down.

28.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
28.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
28.root: — (proper divine name)

29.meaning: So those / then those are the ones — a connector 'so/then' joined to a demonstrative pointing to a distant or already-mentioned group: 'those people, they (are the ones who)…'.
29.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector meaning 'so/then', often introducing a result or consequence. 'ulā'ika' is a plural demonstrative ('those') pointing to people, typically picking up a previously described group and setting them up as the subject. It is fixed in form and does not change for case.

30.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (masculine plural). Standing on its own, it typically adds emphasis or marks the group out as the focus ('they, specifically', 'it is they who').
30.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It takes no case endings; the base is hum, and the final vowel appears as -u (humu) as a connecting vowel to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a definite article. Standing alone, it commonly emphasises or isolates the subject.

31.meaning: The wrongdoers; those who do wrong, act unjustly, or place things where they do not belong. The underlying image is one who oppresses, transgresses limits, and deals unjustly with others or with themselves.
31.grammar: An active participle (the doer of the action) made definite by the prefix al- ('the'). The -ūna ending marks a masculine plural in the nominative (subject) case, the form used when the word functions as the doer of a verb or the subject of a sentence.

1.meaning: "and We caused to follow / sent in succession" — to make one thing come right after another, sending a series so each follows on the heels of the one before.
1.grammar: The wa- prefix is "and." This is a past-tense verb of the intensive (doubled) form. The -nā ending marks a first-person plural subject ("we") who completed the action.
1.root: ق-ف-و (q-f-w) — to follow behind, come after

2.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on, upon, over,' and by extension 'against' or 'incumbent upon.' It can mark something resting on top of, an obligation laid on someone, or being set over/above something.
2.grammar: An indeclinable preposition (its form never changes). It governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case, and conveys location 'on/upon,' or figuratively duty or opposition ('against').

3.meaning: 'Their traces / footsteps / tracks' — the marks, footprints, or after-effects left behind by someone; 'their' refers to a group of males. The core noun means a trace or vestige that follows after a thing.
3.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of 'athar' (a trace, track, mark) with the attached pronoun '-him' meaning 'their' (a masculine plural group). The '-i' vowel before the pronoun is genitive — the state a noun takes when it follows a preposition or is possessed; the possessive pronoun itself puts the noun into that linked, possessed state ('the traces of them' = 'their traces').
3.root: ء-ث-ر (ʾ-th-r) — trace, track, mark, vestige; to transmit

4.meaning: The proper name 'ʿĪsā' (Jesus), a prophet and messenger. The leading 'bi' is the preposition 'with / by / through.'
4.grammar: A proper name governed by the preposition 'bi' (with/by/through). The name ends in a fixed long 'ā' (written with the 'broken' alif) and is indeclinable — its ending does not change for case — so although 'bi' calls for the genitive state, the form itself stays the same.
4.root: — (proper name; no Arabic triliteral root — of non-Arabic origin)

5.meaning: 'Son (of)' — a male child or descendant; commonly used to link a person to their father or lineage.
5.grammar: A singular masculine noun meaning 'son.' The '-i' ending is genitive — the state a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a following noun ('son OF …'). This word characteristically stands between two names, joining a person to his father in a chain of descent.
5.root: ب-ن-و / ب-ن-ي (b-n-w / b-n-y) — son, offspring; to build

6.meaning: "Maryam" — the personal name Mary, the mother of the prophet Jesus.

7.root: ص-د-ق (ṣ-d-q) — truth, sincerity

8.meaning: To / for that which — a preposition 'to, for' joined to a relative word meaning 'what' or 'that which'.
8.grammar: A combination of the preposition li- ('to, for') with the relative pronoun mā ('that which'). Together they introduce something toward or for which an action is directed; mā itself does not change for case.

9.meaning: Between; in the midst of two things. An adverb of place marking the space separating or lying among parties or points.
9.grammar: An adverb of place ('between'). It always ends in -a and grammatically governs what follows it, putting the following noun(s) into the genitive 'of' relationship. It does not change to show 'the' or a case of its own; the fixed -a is simply how this word is formed.
9.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies between

10.meaning: 'His two hands' — literally a dual 'two hands' with 'his' attached. Often used idiomatically for what lies 'in front of' or 'before' someone (i.e. between his hands).
10.grammar: The noun 'yad' (hand) in its dual form 'two hands'. The -ay ending is the dual in the genitive/accusative state (as opposed to -ā for the subject case), used after prepositions or in possessive links. The attached 'hi' means 'his' (the -i vowel of 'hi' harmonizing after the -ay). In construct, the dual's final -n drops before the pronoun.

11.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
11.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

12.meaning: The Torah — the revealed Scripture given through the prophet Moses, treated in Arabic as a definite, named book of divine guidance. The form carries the definite article 'the', marking it as that specific, well-known revelation.
12.grammar: A definite proper noun (the name of a Scripture) carrying the article al- ('the'). The final -i is the genitive case ending, which typically marks the word as following a preposition or oath particle, or as being linked to a preceding noun in an 'of …' relationship. The l- of the article assimilates into the following 't' sound (shown by the doubling).
12.root: — (a proper name, borrowed from Hebrew; no Arabic triliteral root)

13.meaning: 'And We gave/granted him' — a verb of bestowing or handing over something, with 'We' as the giver and 'him' as the recipient. The root conveys the act of bringing or delivering a thing to someone so that they come to possess it.
13.grammar: A past-tense verb in the causative pattern (afʿala: 'to give/bring to'). The suffix -nā is the subject 'we' (the doers of the giving). The attached -hu is the object pronoun 'him/it' (the one given to). So the form packs subject and object into one word: 'we-gave-him'.
13.root: ء-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; in this causative form, to bring/give

14.meaning: The Gospel (Injīl) — the revealed Scripture associated with the prophet Jesus, treated as a definite, named book. The definite article marks it as that specific, recognized revelation.
14.grammar: A definite proper noun (the name of a Scripture) with the article al- ('the'). The final -a is the accusative case ending, which generally marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or the target of certain particles.
14.root: — (a proper name, of Greek/Aramaic origin; no Arabic triliteral root)

15.meaning: 'In it / in him' — the preposition 'in, inside, within' joined to a pronoun referring to a single masculine or neuter thing. It locates something inside or as part of that referent.
15.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The pronoun -hi refers to one masculine (or grammatically masculine) thing and stands as the object of the preposition; its vowel is -i because attached pronouns take that shape after the long -i of fi. Together they answer 'in what?' or 'in whom?'.

16.meaning: Guidance — right direction, the showing of the correct way and the leading along it. The term combines pointing out the path and granting success in following it; more than mere information, it is direction toward what is right.

parts.en: indefinite (tanwin) ending on a shortened final vowel

16.grammar: An indefinite masculine singular noun. The -an (tanwin) ending marks indefiniteness — 'a guidance' rather than 'the guidance'. Because the word ends in a weak final letter, its case is not audibly distinguished, so this single form covers more than one grammatical position.

17.meaning: 'And light' — radiance or illumination; figuratively, guidance and clarity that dispel darkness. The leading 'wa' is the connector 'and'.
17.grammar: A singular masculine noun joined by 'wa' (and). The '-un' ending (nunation, tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a light' / 'light') and in the nominative state, which is the form a word takes when it is the subject or otherwise stands as a naming/predicate word rather than an object.
17.root: ن-و-ر (n-w-r) — light, to give light, illumination

18.meaning: 'And confirming / verifying as true' — an active participle describing someone or something that affirms and corroborates a prior message, declaring it authentic and in agreement with what came before.

The ending -an is the indefinite accusative ('a confirming one'): the doubled final n (tanwīn) marks indefiniteness, and the -a marks the accusative case, which commonly signals a circumstantial state ('as something …') or a direct object.
18.root: ص-د-ق (ṣ-d-q) — truth, truthfulness, sincerity
