5.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
5.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

6.meaning: They swore, took a solemn oath, vowed emphatically. The root meaning of 'dividing/apportioning' underlies the idea of an oath as a binding, weighty declaration.
6.grammar: A past-tense Form IV verb for a masculine plural 'they'. The opening hamza is the Form IV stem marker. The -ū ending marks the doers as a male/mixed group who completed the act of swearing in the past. The final silent alif is a spelling convention after this plural ending.
6.root: ق-س-م (q-s-m) — to divide, apportion; hence to swear an oath

7.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
7.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
7.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

8.meaning: Utmost effort, the full extent or strength of something; with 'oaths' it means the most solemn, strenuous oaths one can swear. The word denotes exertion pushed to its limit.
8.grammar: A noun in the accusative state (final -a). This case is taken by an object of a verb or, as often with this word, by a noun used adverbially or in a binding (genitive) construction with what follows — conveying 'with the utmost of …'.
8.root: ج-ه-د (j-h-d) — to strive, exert utmost effort

9.meaning: Their oaths; the solemn sworn pledges belonging to them. (The same plural form also serves the unrelated sense 'right hands', from which the oath sense derives, since oaths were sealed with the right hand.)
9.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural joined to the possessive pronoun -him ('their'). The -i vowel before the pronoun reflects the genitive state — the form taken when the noun follows a preposition or is bound to a preceding noun ('… of …'); -him marks the owners as a male/mixed group.
9.root: ي-م-ن (y-m-n) — right hand; hence oath, and good fortune

10.meaning: 'Indeed they' — the emphatic particle 'inna' ('truly, indeed') joined to the pronoun 'them/they', strongly affirming a statement about a group.
10.grammar: The emphatic particle inna ('indeed / truly'), which strengthens and affirms a sentence, with the attached pronoun -hum ('they'). Inna places its attached noun or pronoun in the accusative, so -hum here functions as 'they' serving as the subject of the emphasized statement ('indeed they...').

11.meaning: An emphatic assertion meaning roughly "are indeed with you" or "were certainly with you." It combines an emphatic particle "la-" (truly/indeed) with the adverb of accompaniment "maʿa" (with, alongside, in the company of) and an attached pronoun "you (plural)." It stresses togetherness or being in someone's company.
11.grammar: The "la-" prefix is the particle of emphasis, adding the force of "surely/indeed." The core "maʿa" is an adverb of accompaniment whose fixed "-a" ending it carries inherently. The suffix "-kum" is the attached pronoun for a group of people being addressed ("you all"), and it sits in the possessive/genitive slot governed by "maʿa."
11.root: — (maʿa is a particle/adverb of accompaniment with no triliteral verbal root)

12.meaning: It came to nothing / became void / was wasted — of deeds, to be rendered worthless and to lose all reward.

parts.en: to come to nothing / be nullified

12.grammar: A past-tense verb describing a completed event. The -at ending marks a feminine singular subject ('it/she'), used because the thing that becomes void (e.g. 'deeds') is grammatically feminine. The root pictures effort that swells up and then bursts into nothing.
12.root: ح-ب-ط (ḥ-b-ṭ) — coming to nothing, nullification of works

13.meaning: Their deeds / works / actions — the things they have done.
13.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of 'deed', meaning 'deeds/works'. The attached -hum means 'their' (masculine plural), forming a possessive link. The -u before the pronoun is nominative, marking the whole phrase ('their deeds') as a subject. The -hum form keeps its u-vowel after this nominative ending.
13.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — working, doing, action

14.meaning: "And they came to be / and they became," from a verb that originally means "to enter upon the morning" and by extension "to end up in a certain state / to become." It describes a group transitioning into a new condition.
14.grammar: The "fa-" prefix means "so" or "and then," marking a result or sequence. The verb is in the completed (past) tense; the "-ū" ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ("they"). As one of the "sisters of kāna," this verb links a subject to a predicate state, hence "they became (something)."
14.root: ص-ب-ح (ṣ-b-ḥ) — morning / the coming of daybreak; by extension, to come to be in a state

15.meaning: Losers — those who suffer loss and ruin, ending up with a deficit. A 'khāsir' is one whose venture or final account comes out at a loss.
15.grammar: An active participle (one in the state of the action) in the masculine plural. The -īna ending marks the accusative/genitive plural — used for a direct object, after a preposition, or (as often here) describing a state, e.g. 'as losers'.
15.root: خ-س-ر (kh-s-r) — loss, ruin, falling short

1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
4.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

5.meaning: "Turns back / apostatizes," from a verb meaning to revert, retreat, or turn away from something one had embraced — often used of abandoning one's faith.
5.grammar: The "ya-" prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ("he/it") in the present-future tense. With the geminate "-dd-" kept intact and the final short "-a", the verb is in the subjunctive (manṣūb) mood — the form triggered by certain governing particles. (The jussive of this verb would instead break the doubled consonant, giving "yartadid.") The pattern (Form VIII, iftaʿala) often carries a reflexive sense — the action turning back upon the doer.
5.root: ر-د-د (r-d-d) — to return, send back, turn away

6.meaning: A combination meaning 'from among you' or 'of you' — singling out a part or some individuals out of a larger group being addressed.
6.grammar: The preposition min ('from, among, some of') with the attached pronoun -kum, which means 'you' for a group of two or more (grammatically masculine plural). Because the pronoun follows a preposition, it is in the object form; the whole expression partitions or draws out individuals from the addressed group.
6.root: — (min is a particle/preposition; -kum is a pronoun)

7.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on behalf of,' 'for,' 'about,' or 'away from.' It often conveys removing a burden from someone or acting in their place.

parts.en: on behalf of / for / away from

7.grammar: A preposition (a linking particle). It governs the noun that follows it, putting that noun into the genitive case. It does not change form.

8.meaning: His religion / way of life — his binding way of belief, worship and obedience owed to Allah; the whole 'path' one follows.
8.grammar: The stem 'dīn' is a complete way of life: creed, worship, obedience and recompense. The attached -hi means 'his/its' and forms a possessive link, so the noun shows the genitive -i before it ('the religion of him'). The -hi form (with the i-vowel) is the regular shape after a genitive ending.

9.meaning: A two-part marker meaning 'then/so' plus 'shall/will.' It announces something forthcoming as a consequence: the particle sawfa points to the future, generally a more remote or emphatic future than the shorter prefix sa-.
9.grammar: A linking particle fa- ('then/so,' signalling result or sequence) joined to the future particle sawfa, which is placed before a present-tense verb to throw its action into the future ('will/shall …').

10.meaning: he brings / he comes with — a third-person verb meaning to bring something forward or cause it to come, often by fetching or producing it.
10.grammar: A present/future tense verb. The ya- prefix marks a third-person singular masculine doer ('he/it'). Built on a weak root ending in a long vowel, it carries the sense of bringing or coming forth. The form expresses an ongoing or habitual action.

11.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
11.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

12.meaning: "With/by a people," combining the preposition "bi-" (with, by means of) and the noun "qawm," meaning a people, folk, nation, or community — typically a body of men or a tribe bound together.
12.grammar: The "bi-" prefix is a preposition meaning "with" or "by means of." The "-in" ending (tanwīn) is the genitive case combined with indefiniteness, giving "a people"; this genitive is exactly what a preposition like "bi-" requires of the noun that follows it.
12.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; relatedly, a group that stands together as a community

13.meaning: "He loves them," expressing affection, fondness, and devoted attachment toward a group, with the lover being a single "he."
13.grammar: The "yu-" prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ("he") in the present-future tense, in the causative (Form IV) pattern fitting for "to love." The suffix "-hum" is the attached object pronoun "them" (a group), receiving the action of the verb.
13.root: ح-ب-ب (ḥ-b-b) — love, affection, to hold dear

14.meaning: "And they love Him," expressing the affection and devoted attachment of a group toward a single male object of love.
14.grammar: The "wa-" prefix means "and." The "yu-…-ūna" frame marks a third-person masculine plural subject ("they") in the present-future tense; the full "-ūna" ending signals the indicative mood (a plain, ongoing statement, not subjunctive or jussive). The final "-hu" is the attached object pronoun "him."
14.root: ح-ب-ب (ḥ-b-b) — love, affection, to hold dear

15.meaning: "Humble / lowly / gentle (ones)," a plural describing people who are meek, soft, and undemanding toward others — the opposite of haughty or harsh.

parts.en: plural pattern ending + indefinite genitive ("… ones, of")

15.grammar: This is a broken plural on the "afʿila(t)" pattern (أَفْعِلَة), in which the tāʾ marbūṭa is part of the pattern itself. The "-in" tanwīn ending marks the word as indefinite and in the genitive case — the case used after prepositions or when a word is linked to a preceding noun in an "… of …" relationship.
15.root: ذ-ل-ل (dh-l-l) — lowliness, humility, being meek or submissive

16.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
16.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
16.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

17.meaning: A plural noun meaning 'the believers' — those who have faith, who inwardly trust and affirm. The Form IV participle denotes one who brings about belief and security within.
17.grammar: A definite plural active participle of Form IV (āmana 'to believe'). The -īna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) state. The prefixed mu- marks it as a Form IV participle ('one who has/gives faith').

18.meaning: "Mighty / stern / firm (ones)," a plural describing those who are strong, dignified, and unyielding — formidable and resistant rather than soft.

parts.en: plural pattern ending + indefinite genitive ("… ones, of")

18.grammar: This is a broken plural on the "afʿila(t)" pattern (أَفْعِلَة), in which the tāʾ marbūṭa is part of the pattern itself. The "-in" tanwīn ending marks it as indefinite and genitive — the case taken after a preposition or in an "… of …" link to a preceding word.
18.root: ع-ز-ز (ʿ-z-z) — might, strength, honor, being mighty and unconquerable

19.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
19.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
19.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

20.meaning: "The disbelievers," those who reject faith and cover over or deny the truth; the active participle in plural, "the ones who disbelieve / are ungrateful."
20.grammar: The "al-" prefix is the definite article "the." The "-īna" ending is the sound masculine plural in the accusative or genitive case — the form used when the plural is a direct object or follows a preposition or a preceding noun. The base "kāfir" is an active participle: "one who does the act of disbelieving/covering."
20.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; hence to deny or be ungrateful for truth

21.meaning: "They strive / struggle / wage jihād," expending utmost effort and exertion against an obstacle or enemy, often in a sustained, mutual struggle.
21.grammar: The "yu-…-ūna" frame marks a third-person masculine plural subject ("they") in the present-future tense, with the full "-ūna" ending signaling the indicative mood (a plain ongoing statement). The verb is the Form III (fāʿala) pattern, which conveys mutual or strenuous effort directed at another party.
21.root: ج-ه-د (j-h-d) — to exert effort, strive, struggle to one's utmost

22.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
22.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
22.root: — (particle)

23.meaning: 'path, way, road' — a route or course; figuratively a cause or way of life one travels along. In construct ('the way OF ...').
23.grammar: A singular noun with the '-i' (genitive) ending, which typically links it to a following noun ('the way OF ...') or follows a preposition. It marks the word as connected to or possessed by what comes after.
23.root: س-ب-ل (s-b-l) — way, path, road

24.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
24.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

25.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
25.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

26.meaning: They fear: to be afraid of, to hold in awe or dread. Often used of reverent fear of Allah as well as ordinary fear of danger.
26.grammar: A present-tense verb of Form I (with a weak middle letter, giving the long ā), third-person masculine plural ('they fear'). The ya- prefix marks a third-person subject; the full -ūna ending (with its final -na intact) marks a plural of males in the indicative mood, used for a plain, ongoing statement of fact.
26.root: خ-و-ف (kh-w-f) — fear, fright, dread

27.meaning: "Blame / censure / reproach," a noun denoting a single instance or act of finding fault with someone and rebuking them.

parts.en: single-instance noun ending + accusative ("a [single act of] …")

27.grammar: The base is a verbal noun "blame." The added "-at-" gives a noun of a single instance (one act of blaming). The final "-a" ending is the accusative case, the form a noun takes as the direct object of a verb or when it is the first term of a possessive "… of …" pairing.

28.meaning: "A blamer / one who censures / a fault-finder," the active participle naming a person who reproaches and criticizes others.
28.grammar: This is an active participle (fāʿil pattern): "one who does the blaming." The "-in" tanwīn ending marks it as indefinite and genitive — the case used after a preposition or as the second term in an "… of …" construction with a preceding noun.
28.root: ل-و-م (l-w-m) — to blame, censure, reproach

29.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
29.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

30.meaning: "Bounty / grace / favour / excellence" — faḍl is overflowing generosity, favour, and grace; the surplus good that one freely bestows beyond what is owed.
30.grammar: A masculine singular noun. The final -u is the nominative case ending, typically marking the word as the subject of a sentence or the thing being asserted.
30.root: ف-ض-ل (f-ḍ-l) — to be in excess / surpass / show favour

31.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
31.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

32.meaning: He gives it to him / bestows it on him — a subject grants something to a recipient; the verb takes two objects (a thing given and a person given to), and the attached pronoun here is the recipient, 'him'.
32.grammar: A present/future-tense verb meaning 'to give/bestow' (a doubly-transitive verb that takes both a thing given and a person given to). The 'yu-' prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'). The attached '-hi' is the indirect object — the recipient, 'him' (the one given TO), not the thing given.
32.root: ء-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; to bring, to give

33.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
33.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

34.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'he wills, he wishes, he chooses' — to want or intend something by one's own decision.
34.grammar: A present/ongoing action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular, and the final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact ('he wills'), as opposed to a command or a verb governed by 'that.'
34.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — willing, wishing; the root behind 'thing' (shayʾ)

35.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
35.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
35.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

36.meaning: An adjective meaning 'vast, ample, all-embracing, boundless' — wide in capacity, encompassing; of Allah it conveys limitless reach in knowledge, mercy, and bounty.
36.grammar: An active participle ('one who is vast/encompassing') used adjectivally. The ending '-un' is the indefinite nominative (tanwīn), marking it as 'a vast one' and as a subject or predicate.
36.root: و-س-ع (w-s-ʿ) — breadth, capacity, amplitude, to encompass

37.meaning: An intensive adjective/name meaning 'All-Knowing / fully aware' — one whose knowledge is complete, deep, and all-encompassing; as a divine attribute it denotes Allah's perfect knowledge.
37.grammar: An intensive adjective (the pattern faʿīl conveys 'thoroughly, abundantly'). The ending -un is the indefinite nominative — the nominative case marks it as the subject or the quality being affirmed, and the -n (nunation) signals 'a / an', i.e. indefinite. So it reads '(is) all-knowing'.

1.meaning: 'Only / nothing but' — a restrictive particle that limits and emphasizes, asserting that the matter is exclusively so and no other ('it is only...'). It combines the emphatic 'inna' with the restricting 'mā'.
1.grammar: A compound particle formed from the emphatic inna ('indeed') and mā, which together work as a tool of restriction meaning 'only / nothing but'. It both stresses and confines the statement that follows to a single truth, excluding all alternatives.

2.meaning: "Your protector / guardian / ally," from "walī" — one who is close, who stands by another as friend, patron, protector, and guardian — here belonging to a group ("your," plural).
2.grammar: The base "waliyy" is a noun meaning protecting friend or guardian. The suffix "-kum" is the attached possessive pronoun for a group ("your," addressing many); its vowel appears here as "-kumu" to ease pronunciation before a following word. As the possessor, this pronoun sits in the genitive slot.
2.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — nearness, alliance; to be close, to befriend, to take charge of

3.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
3.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

4.meaning: "And His Messenger," the one sent with a message; "rasūl" denotes an envoy or apostle commissioned to deliver something, here belonging to "Him."
4.grammar: The "wa-" prefix means "and." The base "rasūl" is a noun of the faʿūl pattern meaning "one who is sent." The suffix "-hu" is the attached possessive pronoun "his," placing the noun in a possessive "messenger of Him" relationship; the pronoun occupies the genitive slot.
4.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; a message or the one sent with it

5.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
5.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

6.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
6.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

7.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
7.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

8.meaning: "They establish / set up / keep up," from a verb meaning to make something stand firm and upright — used for performing and maintaining something properly and steadfastly (as with prayer).
8.grammar: The "yu-…-ūna" frame marks a third-person masculine plural subject ("they") in the present-future tense, with the full "-ūna" ending showing the indicative mood (a plain ongoing statement). The verb is the causative (Form IV) pattern: "to make stand / cause to be upright," hence "to establish."
8.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise, be upright; causatively, to set up or establish

9.meaning: The ritual prayer (ṣalāh): the prescribed formal worship of standing, bowing, and prostrating before Allah at appointed times. As a verbal noun it also carries the underlying sense of calling upon, supplicating, and blessing.
9.grammar: A definite feminine noun. The -a ending is accusative: it generally marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon, e.g. that which is established or performed), or the object of certain particles.

10.meaning: "And they give / they bring," from a verb meaning to hand over, bestow, or bring something to someone — to render what is due, such as giving alms.
10.grammar: The "wa-" prefix means "and." The "yu-…-ūna" frame marks a third-person masculine plural subject ("they") in the present-future tense, with the full "-ūna" ending signaling the indicative mood. The verb is the causative (Form IV) pattern, conveying "to cause to come / to give over."
10.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; causatively, to bring or give

11.meaning: The purifying alms (zakāt) — the obligatory portion given from one's wealth that purifies it and causes it to grow; an act of worship and social due.
11.grammar: A definite feminine noun (the tied tā' marks the feminine). The final -a is the accusative ending, typically marking the noun as the direct object of a verb ('the alms').
11.root: ز-ك-و (z-k-w) — to be pure; to grow, increase, be blessed

12.meaning: 'While they / and they' — the word 'wa' (here 'while' or 'and') joined to the standalone pronoun 'hum' ('they'), referring to a masculine plural group.
12.grammar: A connective 'wa' — often circumstantial 'while' — plus the independent subject pronoun 'hum' ('they'), used for a masculine plural group. As an independent pronoun it usually stands as the subject of a following statement.

13.meaning: "Those who bow down / bowing ones," the active participle in plural describing people in the posture of bowing — bending in reverence and submission, as in prayer.
13.grammar: The base "rākiʿ" is an active participle: "one who is bowing." The "-ūna" ending is the sound masculine plural in the nominative case — the form used when the plural is the subject or is otherwise the "doer/described" rather than an object.
13.root: ر-ك-ع (r-k-ʿ) — to bow, bend the torso (the bowing of prayer)

1.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
1.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

2.meaning: "He takes as an ally / turns to in alliance," or simply "turns away," from a verb meaning to turn toward something and befriend/ally with it — or, with the opposite nuance, to turn one's back on it.

parts.en: take as ally / turn to (or away)

2.grammar: The "ya-" prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ("he") in the present-future tense. With the weak final letter dropped (leaving a short "-a"), the verb is in the jussive/subjunctive mood, the form triggered by certain conditional or governing particles. The verb is the reflexive Form V (tafaʿʿala), "to turn oneself toward / take for oneself as ally."
2.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — nearness, alliance; to turn toward, befriend, take charge (or, turn away)

3.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
3.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

4.meaning: 'And His Messenger' — the one sent with a message, an envoy or apostle, here joined by 'and' and tagged with 'His' (referring to Allah).
4.grammar: Connective 'and' + a masculine noun + the attached pronoun 'his'. The -a ending is accusative, marking the noun as an object of a verb; the suffix -hu ('his') links it in possession to a male referent.

5.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
5.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

6.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
6.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

7.meaning: A two-part connector meaning 'so/then, indeed…'. It joins fa- ('so', 'then', marking a result or consequence) to inna, an emphatic particle that strongly affirms the statement that follows ('truly', 'verily').
7.grammar: fa- is a connective prefix signaling that what follows is a consequence or next step. inna is an emphatic particle that introduces a nominal sentence, puts its following noun in the accusative, and strengthens the assertion; it does not itself take a case ending.

8.meaning: "Party / faction / band," the noun "ḥizb" denoting a group, company, or partisan body of people united by a common cause or allegiance.
8.grammar: This is a singular noun. The final "-a" ending is the accusative case, taken by a noun when it is the direct object of a verb or the first term ("the party of …") of a possessive pairing with a following noun.
8.root: ح-ز-ب (ḥ-z-b) — a group, party, or faction; a band of people

9.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
9.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

10.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (masculine plural). Standing on its own, it typically adds emphasis or marks the group out as the focus ('they, specifically', 'it is they who').
10.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It takes no case endings; the base is hum, and the final vowel appears as -u (humu) as a connecting vowel to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a definite article. Standing alone, it commonly emphasises or isolates the subject.

11.meaning: "The victorious / the prevailing ones," the active participle in plural describing those who overcome, dominate, and gain the upper hand.
11.grammar: The "al-" prefix is the definite article "the." The base "ghālib" is an active participle, "one who overcomes." The "-ūna" ending is the sound masculine plural in the nominative case — the form used when the plural is the subject or the predicate ("the … ones are").
11.root: غ-ل-ب (gh-l-b) — to overcome, prevail, conquer, gain the upper hand

1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
4.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

5.meaning: That you take, that you adopt — a present-tense verb (form VIII) meaning to take for oneself, to choose or adopt something. Addressed to a group ('you all'), and in a form used after particles meaning 'that' or 'to'.
5.grammar: A present-tense verb in the reflexive (form VIII) pattern, 'to take for oneself'. The ta- prefix with the plural ending means 'you all'. The ending is -ū (the final 'n' of -ūna has dropped), which marks the subjunctive or jussive mood — the form used after particles like 'that', 'to', or 'not'.

6.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
6.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

7.meaning: Past-tense verb (reflexive form), third person plural: 'they took for themselves, adopted, chose.' A completed act of taking something on as one's own.
7.grammar: A completed-action (past) verb in a reflexive pattern (taking something for oneself). The '-ū' ending (with silent trailing alif) marks the subject as 'they' (masculine plural). The opening 'i-' is a helping vowel that lets the cluster of consonants be pronounced.
7.root: أ-خ-ذ (ʾ-kh-dh) — to take, seize, grasp

8.meaning: Your religion / way of life — the system of belief, worship, obedience, and accountability one lives by; 'dīn' carries the sense of a binding way to which one submits and for which one is recompensed.
8.grammar: A singular noun carrying the accusative '-a' ending, which typically marks it as the direct object of a verb. The attached '-kum' is a possessive pronoun meaning 'your' for a plural addressee ('you all').
8.root: د-ي-ن (d-y-n) — religion, way; obedience, requital, accountability

9.meaning: Mockery, ridicule, a laughing-stock — the act of deriding, or an object treated as a joke. Huzuw is scornful jesting that belittles.
9.grammar: An indefinite verbal noun in the accusative ('an' written with tanwīn on a final alif). The accusative here is typical for the object of a verb or for stating what something is taken/treated 'as'. 'Indefinite' means 'mockery / a mockery' rather than 'the mockery'.
9.root: ه-ز-و (h-z-w) — to mock, ridicule, scoff at; a wāw-final variant of the related root ه-ز-أ (h-z-ʾ), this written form ending in wāw

10.meaning: "And amusement / play / sport," the noun "laʿib" denoting idle play, frivolous fun, and games — activity pursued for diversion rather than serious purpose.
10.grammar: The "wa-" prefix means "and." The "-an" tanwīn ending marks the noun as indefinite and in the accusative case — the case used for a direct object of a verb or other complement within a sentence.
10.root: ل-ع-ب (l-ʿ-b) — to play; play, sport, amusement

11.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
11.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

12.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
12.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

13.meaning: They were given / granted — the passive past tense of the verb 'to give/bring' (form IV of ʾ-t-y), where a plural group receives something without the giver being named.
13.grammar: Passive past tense. The internal vowelling (u-...-u) marks it as passive — the subject receives the action rather than doing it. The '-ū' ending means 'they', giving 'they were given' (the giver left unmentioned).
13.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (form IV) to bring or give

14.meaning: The Book, the Scripture — a written revelation; the term for a divinely revealed text.
14.grammar: A definite noun ('the Book') with attached 'al-' ('the'). The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb.
14.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — to write; a writing, book

15.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
15.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
15.root: — (preposition)

16.meaning: 'before you,' 'prior to you' — an expression of precedence in time or place, here relating that precedence to 'you (plural).' The core word denotes the 'before' side, what comes earlier or in front.
16.grammar: An adverb of time/place ('before') joined to the pronoun '-kum' ('you, plural'). The '-i' ending is genitive: such words of place/time regularly take this case, especially after a preposition, and the attached pronoun completes the sense as 'before you.'

17.meaning: "And the disbelievers / the staunch deniers," "kuffār" being an intensive plural for those who persistently reject faith and cover over the truth — often connoting obstinate or ungrateful denial.
17.grammar: The "wa-" prefix means "and" and "al-" is the definite article "the." The base "kuffār" is an intensive/broken plural (fuʿʿāl pattern) stressing the depth or persistence of the trait. The final "-a" ending is the accusative case, the form taken as a direct object or other sentence complement.
17.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; hence to deny or be ungrateful for truth

18.meaning: Allies, protectors, intimate friends — those taken as close supporters, patrons, or guardians, with whom one stands in mutual loyalty (plural of walī).
18.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of 'walī.' Being a 'diptote' (a noun that resists the usual full set of endings), it takes a single final '-a' here for the accusative case, which commonly marks the direct object of a verb or signals 'as / being' something — and notably without the usual '-n' (no nunation).
18.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — nearness, allegiance, guardianship

19.meaning: A command addressed to a group: 'guard yourselves / be mindful and on your guard.' The verb conveys taqwā — protecting oneself by being conscious of Allah and shielding oneself from wrongdoing and its consequences.
19.grammar: An imperative (command) verb addressed to a plural 'you (all).' The -ū ending marks the masculine plural addressees ('you all'). The pattern (form VIII, from waqā 'to protect') gives the sense of taking protective care for oneself.
19.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to guard, shield, protect oneself

20.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
20.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.
20.root: — (proper name)

21.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
21.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

22.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
22.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
22.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

23.meaning: 'Believers / faithful ones' — the plural of muʾmin, one who has faith and trust in Allah and grants assent to the truth.

parts.en: believers (form IV participle, oblique masculine sound plural)

23.grammar: An active participle ('one who believes') from the form IV pattern, here a masculine sound plural. The single suffix -īna is the oblique (accusative/genitive) form of the masculine plural — used for a direct object or after a preposition — as opposed to the -ūna form used for the subject. Its nūn is part of the one ending and is not a separable morpheme.
23.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — security, trust; hence faith and belief

1.meaning: 'And when...' — a linking phrase joining 'and' to 'when', used to introduce a circumstance or a recurring situation: 'and whenever / and at the time that...'.
1.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to idhā ('when'). Idhā is a particle pointing to a time or condition, generally referring to something expected or recurring in the future ('when / whenever' it happens), and it normally introduces a following clause that states what occurs at that time.

2.meaning: "You called out / you made a call," from a verb meaning to call to, summon, or proclaim aloud to someone, with the callers being a group ("you all").
2.grammar: This verb is in the completed (past) tense. The suffix "-tum" marks a second-person masculine plural subject — a group being addressed as "you all" who performed the action. The verb is the Form III (fāʿala) pattern, fitting for calling out toward another party.
2.root: ن-د-و / ن-د-ي (n-d-w / n-d-y) — to call out, summon, proclaim

3.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
3.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

4.meaning: The ritual Prayer — the formal worship of standing, bowing, and prostrating before Allah at appointed times. More broadly the root conveys connection, supplication, and reaching out to the divine; it is the central act of Islamic devotion.
4.grammar: A definite feminine noun ('the prayer'). The article al- means 'the.' The -i ending (on the feminine tā') is the genitive case: it typically links the word to a preceding preposition or to another noun in an 'of' relationship (e.g. 'of the prayer / to the prayer').

5.meaning: "They took it / adopted it," from a verb meaning to take, seize, or adopt something for oneself — to acquire it and make it one's own; the object "it" is feminine.
5.grammar: The verb is in the completed (past) tense; the "-ū" ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ("they"). The suffix "-hā" is the attached object pronoun "it/her," referring to a grammatically feminine thing receiving the action. The verb is the reflexive Form VIII (iftaʿala), "to take for oneself / adopt."
5.root: أ-خ-ذ (ʾ-kh-dh) — to take, seize, grasp; to adopt or acquire

6.meaning: Mockery, ridicule, a laughing-stock — the act of deriding, or an object treated as a joke. Huzuw is scornful jesting that belittles.
6.grammar: An indefinite verbal noun in the accusative ('an' written with tanwīn on a final alif). The accusative here is typical for the object of a verb or for stating what something is taken/treated 'as'. 'Indefinite' means 'mockery / a mockery' rather than 'the mockery'.
6.root: ه-ز-و (h-z-w) — to mock, ridicule, scoff at; a wāw-final variant of the related root ه-ز-أ (h-z-ʾ), this written form ending in wāw

7.meaning: "And amusement / play / sport," the noun "laʿib" denoting idle play, frivolous fun, and games — activity pursued for diversion rather than serious purpose.
7.grammar: The "wa-" prefix means "and." The "-an" tanwīn ending marks the noun as indefinite and in the accusative case — the case used for a direct object of a verb or other complement within a sentence.
7.root: ل-ع-ب (l-ʿ-b) — to play; play, sport, amusement

8.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
8.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

9.meaning: A connector meaning 'because they…' or 'by reason that they…'. It fuses the preposition bi- (here giving a cause, 'because of') with anna ('that', an emphatic particle introducing a fact) and the attached pronoun -hum ('they').
9.grammar: bi- here gives a causal sense ('because of'). anna is an emphatic particle meaning 'that' which introduces a statement of fact and takes a following noun or pronoun in the accusative; the attached -hum is that pronoun, a masculine plural 'they'. Together they give a reason: 'because they …'.

10.meaning: 'A people / folk / community' — a group of people bound together, often by kinship, tribe, or shared identity.
10.grammar: An indefinite collective noun ('a people'), grammatically singular but referring to a group. The -un ending is indefinite ('a') and nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence.
10.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a group that stands together

11.meaning: 'Not' — a particle of negation. Depending on context it denies a present fact, forbids an action, or rules something out ('do not / there is no').
11.grammar: A negating particle, 'not / no'. It is used to deny or prohibit — negating present-tense statements, expressing 'there is no...', or, with a command form, forbidding an action ('do not...').

12.meaning: 'They understand / use reason.' To comprehend, reason, and grasp things with the intellect — to 'tie down' meaning with the mind, to think rationally and exercise sound judgment.
12.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya-…-ūna frame means 'they [do]' for a group of males or a mixed group. The full -ūna ending (with the final -na intact) marks the indicative mood, i.e. a plain factual statement. The root sense is binding/restraining, hence using the mind to 'hold' meaning.
12.root: ع-ق-ل (ʿ-q-l) — to bind, restrain; intellect, reason

1.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
1.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

2.meaning: 'O people of… / O folk of…' — a vocative call ('O!') addressed to the 'people' or 'folk' belonging to something (such as the people of a household, place, or scripture).
2.grammar: The vocative particle ya ('O') used to address or call out, plus the noun 'people/folk'. The -a ending is accusative, which is the case a called-upon noun takes when it is attached to a following word ('O people OF …'). It denotes those who belong to or are associated with something.
2.root: ا-ه-ل (ʾ-h-l) — family, folk, those belonging to

3.meaning: 'The Book / the Scripture' — a written record or revealed scripture; literally that which is written.
3.grammar: The definite article al- with the noun kitāb ('book, scripture'), itself a verbal noun from 'to write.' The -i ending is genitive, typically marking the word as following a preposition or standing in an 'of' relationship to a preceding noun.

4.meaning: An interrogative particle that turns a statement into a yes/no question, roughly "is it that…?" or "do…?". It can also carry a rhetorical or expectant tone rather than a literal request for information.
4.grammar: A question particle placed before a sentence to ask whether something is the case. It has no case ending and does not change form; it simply marks the words that follow as a yes/no question.

5.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'you (plural) find fault with, hold a grudge against, or take vengeance on' — to disapprove of or resent something so strongly that one wishes to punish or retaliate. The underlying sense is finding something blameworthy and reacting against it.

parts.en: find fault with / resent / take vengeance

5.grammar: A present/imperfect verb. The ta- prefix signals a second-person subject ('you'), and the -ūna ending marks it as masculine plural and indicative ('you all do/are doing'). The full pattern ta-…-ūna means 'you (men, or a mixed group) do something'.
5.root: ن-ق-م (n-q-m) — to resent, hold a grudge, exact retribution for a wrong

6.meaning: "from us" — the preposition 'from' (indicating origin, source, or starting point) fused with the attached pronoun 'us'. It can also carry a partitive sense, 'some of us / a part of us'.
6.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The base 'min' normally takes a vowelless final consonant, but before the pronoun '-nā' the nūn is doubled (assimilation), giving 'minnā'. The suffix '-nā' is the first-person plural object/possessive pronoun meaning 'us' or 'our'.
6.root: — (preposition; the pronoun has no triliteral root)

7.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
7.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.
7.root: — (particle)

8.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
8.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

9.meaning: We have believed; we have come to faith and trust — to affirm belief, give one's trust, and feel secure in that conviction, stated by a group about themselves.
9.grammar: A past-tense verb on the form-IV pattern (āmana, 'to believe / to have faith'). The ending -nā (a single morpheme, نَا) attached to a past verb marks the subject as 'we'. The doubled 'n' heard in 'āmannā' comes from the verb stem's final 'n' meeting the 'n' that begins the -nā ending.

10.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
10.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
10.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

11.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
11.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

12.meaning: 'It was sent down / revealed': the act of being caused to descend, used especially of revelation brought down from Allah. The passive form puts the focus on the thing sent down rather than on the sender.
12.grammar: A past-tense passive verb in Form IV (anzala 'to send down' → unzila 'was sent down'). The prefix is only the u- vowel carried on the connecting hamza; the nūn that follows is the first root letter (of ن-ز-ل), not part of the prefix. The internal vowel pattern u–i marks it as passive ('was/were sent down'), with no named doer. The final -a marks the subject as 'he/it', a single masculine thing, and signals completed action.
12.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, come down; (Form IV) to send down

13.meaning: 'To us / toward us' — the preposition 'to/toward' joined to the pronoun 'us,' expressing direction or motion toward the speakers.
13.grammar: Preposition 'ilā' (to/toward), which shifts to the form 'ilay-' before a pronoun, plus the attached pronoun -nā, 'us.' Pronouns after a preposition stand in the genitive (object-of-preposition) role; -nā is a fixed form and does not change shape.
13.root: — (preposition + pronoun)

14.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
14.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.
14.root: — (relative pronoun / particle)

15.meaning: 'It was sent down / revealed': the act of being caused to descend, used especially of revelation brought down from Allah. The passive form puts the focus on the thing sent down rather than on the sender.
15.grammar: A past-tense passive verb in Form IV (anzala 'to send down' → unzila 'was sent down'). The prefix is only the u- vowel carried on the connecting hamza; the nūn that follows is the first root letter (of ن-ز-ل), not part of the prefix. The internal vowel pattern u–i marks it as passive ('was/were sent down'), with no named doer. The final -a marks the subject as 'he/it', a single masculine thing, and signals completed action.
15.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, come down; (Form IV) to send down

16.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
16.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

17.meaning: An adverb of time meaning 'before / beforehand / previously,' pointing to a moment or state that precedes something else in time. When used with the final vowel -u (qablu), it stands cut off from an explicit following noun, conveying 'before(hand)' or 'previously' in an absolute sense — the thing it is 'before' is understood rather than stated.
17.grammar: An adverb of time. The final -u ending here is the indeclinable (mabnī) form taken when the word is severed from a following genitive: rather than 'before X,' it means 'before(hand)' on its own, with the reference point left implicit.
17.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to come before, precede, be in front; to receive/accept

18.meaning: And that — a linking expression introducing a fact or clause ('and that …'); it combines 'and' with a particle that sets up and emphasises the statement that follows.
18.grammar: A connective made of wa- ('and') plus anna ('that'). Anna introduces a noun clause — a fact being asserted — and gives it emphasis, roughly 'and (it is the case) that …'. As a governing particle, anna puts the noun right after it into the accusative case.

19.meaning: 'Most of you' / 'the greater number of you' — the comparative/elative noun 'greater part, majority' joined to the pronoun 'you all'. It denotes the larger portion of a group.
19.grammar: An elative noun (the 'most/greatest' form) with the suffixed pronoun -kum ('you', masculine plural) functioning like a possessive: 'the most of you.' The -a vowel before the pronoun is an accusative/object ending, the case typically taken when the word is the object of a verb or otherwise governed in that position.
19.root: ك-ث-ر (k-th-r) — to be much, many, abundant

20.meaning: 'Ones who are defiantly disobedient, transgressors' — those who break out of obedience to Allah and overstep the bounds of His law. The root sense is of something departing from its proper place or rind; the term denotes deliberate rebellion against the sacred order.
20.grammar: An active participle ('one who transgresses') in the masculine plural. The -ūna ending marks masculine plural in the nominative case — the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or the predicate ('they are transgressors').
20.root: ف-س-ق (f-s-q) — to forsake obedience, deviate from the right path

1.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
1.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

2.meaning: An interrogative particle that turns a statement into a yes/no question, roughly "is it that…?" or "do…?". It can also carry a rhetorical or expectant tone rather than a literal request for information.
2.grammar: A question particle placed before a sentence to ask whether something is the case. It has no case ending and does not change form; it simply marks the words that follow as a yes/no question.

3.meaning: 'I inform you, I give you news of' — a first-person verb meaning to announce or tell someone of something weighty or significant. The doubled middle root letter intensifies it: to convey important tidings.
3.grammar: A present/imperfect verb in an intensive (form II) pattern. The u- prefix signals a first-person singular subject ('I'), the final -u is the indicative ending (a plain statement), and the attached -kum is the object 'you (all)'. So: 'I inform you all.'

4.meaning: 'Of/with evil, with something bad' — the preposition 'with/of' joined to the noun-adjective 'evil, badness.' It refers to something bad or harmful in itself (this is the plain noun for evil, not a comparative; the comparative 'worse' would be a different form, أَشَرّ).
4.grammar: A preposition bi- ('with, of') attached to a noun/adjective meaning 'evil, badness.' The -in ending (written as nunation, an 'n' sound) marks the noun as indefinite ('an evil, some badness') and in the genitive case — the case a noun takes after a preposition like bi-. It is a plain noun, not a comparative form.

5.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
5.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

6.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
6.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

7.meaning: 'As a recompense, reward, or requital' — that which is given back in return for one's deeds. The word can denote a reward but is used of any return for conduct, good or ill.
7.grammar: A feminine noun. The -an ending (nunation, written on the tā' marbūṭa) marks it as indefinite ('a recompense') and accusative — a case often used to specify in what respect something is so ('… as a recompense', 'in terms of requital'), among other object-like roles.
7.root: ث-و-ب (th-w-b) — to return, come back; reward, requital

8.meaning: 'With / in the presence of / near' — an adverb of place and relation meaning at, by, in the sight or estimation of someone. It indicates nearness, possession, or what holds in someone's view (as in 'with Allah' = in His sight).
8.grammar: An adverb of place that is always followed by a noun it relates to. It carries a fixed -a ending; this accusative-type vowel is characteristic of such adverbs of place and shows the word is functioning to locate something ('at, near, in the presence of').

9.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
9.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

10.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
10.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

11.meaning: He cursed him — He expelled him from mercy and consigned him to being driven away and rejected. Divine cursing means removal from grace.
11.grammar: A past-tense verb. The bare -a ending (with no added subject suffix) marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'). The attached -hu is the direct object 'him'. The prefixed la- is an emphatic particle stressing the certainty of the statement ('He has indeed cursed…').
11.root: ل-ع-ن (l-ʿ-n) — to curse, to drive away from mercy

12.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
12.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
12.root: — (proper divine name)

13.meaning: 'And He grew angry / was wrathful' — a perfect verb expressing anger and displeasure, here joined by 'and'.
13.grammar: The conjunction wa- ('and') plus a perfect verb, 3rd-person masculine singular. With no prefix and the final -a, it states a completed act, 'he became angry'.
13.root: غ-ض-ب (gh-ḍ-b) — anger, wrath

14.meaning: A preposition fused with a pronoun, meaning 'upon him', 'on him', or 'toward him'. It marks the one to whom an action is directed or upon whom something rests.
14.grammar: The preposition 'upon/on' with an attached object pronoun -hi ('him', third-person masculine singular); its -i vowel is the regular form the pronoun takes after the 'y' sound. Paired with a verb of turning, this 'upon/toward him' marks the person the action reaches.

15.meaning: 'And he made / appointed / rendered' — the connector 'and' joined to a past-tense verb meaning to make something into something, to fashion or appoint it. It can mean to create, to assign, or to cause a thing to become a certain way.
15.grammar: The connective wa- ('and') prefixed to a past-tense (perfect) verb. The bare verb with its final -a vowel denotes a completed act by a third-person masculine singular subject ('he made/did').
15.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, render, appoint, place

16.meaning: 'From them / among them' (a group of males or a mixed group) — indicating origin, source, or partitive 'some of them'.
16.grammar: The preposition min ('from, of, among'). The attached pronoun -hum ('them', masculine/mixed plural) takes a helping vowel -u (becoming -humu) for ease of pronunciation before a following word. The whole means 'from/among them'.

17.meaning: 'The apes, monkeys' — the definite plural noun for apes/monkeys.
17.grammar: A noun made definite by al- ('the'). The final -a vowel marks the accusative case — the case typically taken by the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon).

18.meaning: 'And the swine, pigs' — the connector 'and' with the definite plural noun for swine/pigs.
18.grammar: The connective wa- ('and') plus the definite article al- ('the') prefixed to a plural noun. The final -a is an accusative ending; because this is a 'diptote' broken plural, it takes -a without nunation. The accusative is the case typically used for the direct object of a verb.
18.root: خ-ن-ز-ر (kh-n-z-r) — swine, pig (a quadriliteral root)

19.meaning: 'And he worshipped / served / submitted to' — the connector 'and' joined to a past-tense verb meaning to worship, to devote oneself in servitude. The root denotes the relationship of a servant to a master; worship rendered with humility and obedience.
19.grammar: The connective wa- ('and') prefixed to a past-tense (perfect) verb. The final -a vowel denotes a completed act by a third-person masculine singular subject ('he worshipped').
19.root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — to worship, serve; servitude, devotion

20.meaning: 'The false god / idol / that which is wrongly worshipped' — a term (from the root meaning 'to overstep all bounds, transgress in tyranny') for any object of worship set up beside Allah: an idol, a tyrant, a devil, or any false deity that leads people into rebellion.

parts.en: false deity / idol / object of false worship

20.grammar: A noun made definite by al- ('the'). The final -a vowel marks the accusative case — the case typically taken by the direct object of a verb (the thing worshipped/served).
20.root: ط-غ-ي (ṭ-gh-y) — to exceed all limits, be tyrannical, transgress

21.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'those' — pointing to people or things that are distant or already known. It singles out a group ('those ones', 'it is those who').
21.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those'. It is fixed in form (no case endings). The -ka element signals distance/remoteness, pointing to something far off or notable. It can refer to people of either gender.

22.meaning: Evil, bad, or harmful — that which is wicked or detrimental; can also mean 'worse' in comparison.
22.grammar: A noun (also used as a comparative, 'worse'). The ending -un is the nominative with 'tanwīn' (the -n marking an indefinite noun, 'a …'). The nominative generally marks the word as the subject or as the thing being described.
22.root: ش-ر-ر (sh-r-r) — evil, badness, wickedness

23.meaning: 'A place, position, or station' — a noun for a location or standing where something or someone is situated, literally or figuratively (rank, status).
23.grammar: A noun. The -an ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a place') and accusative — a case often used to specify in what respect something holds true ('… in position/place'), as well as for direct objects.
23.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to come to be, existence (place of being)

24.meaning: 'And more astray / further from the right path' — the connector 'and' with the comparative/elative 'more lost, more gone astray.' It denotes a greater degree of straying from the correct way.
24.grammar: The connective wa- ('and') prefixed to an elative noun (the 'more/most' form). The final -u is a nominative ending — the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate ('… is more astray').
24.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to go astray, lose the way, err

25.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on behalf of,' 'for,' 'about,' or 'away from.' It often conveys removing a burden from someone or acting in their place.

parts.en: on behalf of / for / away from

25.grammar: A preposition (a linking particle). It governs the noun that follows it, putting that noun into the genitive case. It does not change form.

26.meaning: 'Evenness, levelness, the middle/right course' — a noun meaning that which is even, balanced, or equal; by extension the straight, sound, correct way. Often paired with 'path' to mean 'the even/right way.'
26.grammar: A noun. The final -i ending marks the genitive case — the case typically used when a word is linked to a following noun ('… OF …') or follows a preposition. So it commonly attaches to a following noun in a possessive-style construction.
26.root: س-و-ي (s-w-y) — to be even, level, equal; to make straight

27.meaning: The way, road, or path — a route one travels; very often used figuratively for a course of life, conduct, or the path of religion. The attached article makes it definite: 'the way'.
27.grammar: al- is the definite article 'the' (its 'l' assimilates to the following 's', heard as 'as-sabīl'). The final -i is the genitive ending, marking the word as joined to a preceding noun ('… OF the way') or governed by a preposition.

1.meaning: 'And when...' — a linking phrase joining 'and' to 'when', used to introduce a circumstance or a recurring situation: 'and whenever / and at the time that...'.
1.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to idhā ('when'). Idhā is a particle pointing to a time or condition, generally referring to something expected or recurring in the future ('when / whenever' it happens), and it normally introduces a following clause that states what occurs at that time.

2.meaning: They came to you / they reached you — a completed act of a group arriving at or approaching addressees.
2.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'), and the attached -kum is the plural object ('you all'), so together the verb means 'they came to you'. The perfect tense presents the action as already completed.

3.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

4.meaning: We have believed; we have come to faith and trust — to affirm belief, give one's trust, and feel secure in that conviction, stated by a group about themselves.
4.grammar: A past-tense verb on the form-IV pattern (āmana, 'to believe / to have faith'). The ending -nā (a single morpheme, نَا) attached to a past verb marks the subject as 'we'. The doubled 'n' heard in 'āmannā' comes from the verb stem's final 'n' meeting the 'n' that begins the -nā ending.

5.meaning: 'And indeed / and certainly' — the connector 'and' joined to qad, a particle that, before a past-tense verb, affirms and emphasizes that the action really has happened ('indeed, certainly, already').
5.grammar: The connective wa- ('and/but') prefixed to the particle qad. Qad is an emphasis word with no ending to inflect; placed before a completed (past) verb it stresses that the act truly and definitely occurred.

6.meaning: 'They entered, went in' — a past-tense verb meaning a group went or came into a place or state.
6.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb. The -ū ending marks the subject as third-person masculine plural ('they did'). The completed action denotes that they went in.
6.root: د-خ-ل (d-kh-l) — to enter, go in, penetrate

7.meaning: To/with disbelief — 'kufr', the rejection or covering-over of faith and of Allah's truth, governed by the preposition 'bi' ('with, by, to'). 'Kufr' is the active denial of belief and ingratitude toward Allah.
7.grammar: The bi- prefix is a preposition ('with, by, to'); the l- is 'the'. The final -i is the genitive ending, which is required here because the noun follows a preposition (a noun after 'bi' takes the genitive case).
7.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; hence to deny/reject faith, to be ungrateful

8.meaning: 'While they / and they' — the word 'wa' (here 'while' or 'and') joined to the standalone pronoun 'hum' ('they'), referring to a masculine plural group.
8.grammar: A connective 'wa' — often circumstantial 'while' — plus the independent subject pronoun 'hum' ('they'), used for a masculine plural group. As an independent pronoun it usually stands as the subject of a following statement.

9.meaning: A short particle placed before a verb to emphasize or affirm it. Before a past-tense verb it means 'indeed / certainly / has already (happened)'; before a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes / may'. It sharpens and confirms the verb that follows.
9.grammar: An indeclinable particle (its form never changes). It does not take case or tense endings; its job is to color the following verb — affirming and intensifying a past action ('has indeed done') or signaling occasional possibility with a present verb.
