27.root: ا-س-و / ا-س-ى (ʾ-s-w / ʾ-s-y) — grief, sorrow, regret

28.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
28.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
28.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

29.meaning: 'The people / the folk' — a collective noun for a community, nation, or group of people regarded as a body. Often it carries the nuance of one's own people or a particular group sharing a trait.
29.grammar: A collective noun with the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The final '-i' is the genitive ending, which typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun in an 'of …' relationship.
29.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand/rise; a people, community

30.meaning: The disbelievers / the ungrateful — those who reject faith and cover over the truth; the word also carries the sense of covering up or being ungrateful for what one has been given.
30.grammar: 'al-' is 'the'. The stem is an active participle ('one who disbelieves/is ungrateful') made plural for masculine people. The -īna ending is the accusative/genitive form of the sound masculine plural: it marks the word as an object of a verb or as governed by a preposition, as opposed to the subject form -ūna.
30.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; ingratitude, disbelief

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
4.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

5.meaning: 'They became Jews / adopted Judaism', or in the verb's wider sense 'they turned (back) in repentance'. A completed act by a group of taking on the way of the Jewish community.

parts.en: became Jews / turned back (past, masc. plural)

5.grammar: A past-tense verb from a hollow root. The whole form hādū is already 3rd-person masculine plural ('they turned/became Jews'): the long ū plus the final silent alif are the plural marker, so no separate ending is split off. The action is presented as completed; the root carries the idea of turning toward or returning, from which the sense 'to follow Judaism' derives.
5.root: ه-و-د (h-w-d) — turning back, returning; hence following Judaism

6.meaning: 'And the Sabians' — a named religious community; the plural designation of the Ṣābiʾūn, joined by 'and'.
6.grammar: A connecting wa- ('and') and the definite article al- ('the') prefixed to a sound masculine plural noun. The -ūna ending marks the masculine plural in the nominative case, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence.
6.root: ص-ب-أ (ṣ-b-ʾ) — to incline toward / turn to (a religion); the basis of the community-name 'Sabians'

7.meaning: 'And the Christians' — the followers of ʿĪsā (Jesus). The word is a plural form (commonly traced to 'helpers' or to Nazareth) joined to wa- ('and') and the definite article.
7.grammar: A definite plural noun (the al- prefix means 'the') preceded by wa- ('and'). It ends in a fixed long -ā and does not change its form for case; the alif of the article assimilates in sound to the following n (an-naṣārā).
7.root: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — helping, aiding (linked to 'helpers'/Nazareth)

8.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
8.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

9.meaning: 'He believed' — he had faith, trusted, and affirmed. The basic past-tense form of the verb meaning to believe and to find security in faith.
9.grammar: A past-tense verb on the causative (Form IV) pattern, from the root for security and faith. The -a ending marks a third-person masculine singular subject, 'he (believed)', stating a completed act of coming to faith.

10.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
10.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
10.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

11.meaning: "And the Day" — a stretch of time, a day; also used for the appointed Day of Judgement and Resurrection. The opening element is the conjunction 'and'.
11.grammar: A masculine singular noun with the definite article 'the' and the conjunction 'and'. The final -i is the genitive case ending: it typically signals that the word is linked to a preceding noun ('… of …') or governed by a preposition or oath particle.

12.meaning: An adjective meaning 'the last,' 'the latter,' or 'the final' — that which comes at the end of a sequence. It is the common counterpart to 'the first,' and is often used as a name for the world or life to come (the Hereafter, the Last Day), i.e. the ultimate end of all things.
12.grammar: An active-participle-type adjective on the pattern fāʿil. It carries the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The final -i is the genitive case, signaling that the word is governed by a preceding preposition or particle, or stands as the second term of a possessive link ('… of …'). It is masculine singular.
12.root: ء-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to be last, to come after, to defer / postpone

13.meaning: "And he did / worked / acted" — to do or perform an action, to put work into effect. The opening element is the conjunction 'and'.
13.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third-person masculine singular: 'he did'. The bare -a ending with no attached pronoun marks this completed, masculine 'he' action. Prefixed with the conjunction 'and'.
13.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to work / do / act

14.meaning: "Righteous / good / sound" — an active participle describing one who or that which is upright and wholesome and acts rightly; as a description of deeds it means good, virtuous works.
14.grammar: An active participle used as a noun or adjective. The -an ending (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a righteous one / a good deed') and in the accusative case — the form used for a direct object or other complement.
14.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — to be sound / upright / righteous

15.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
15.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

16.meaning: 'Fear' — a state of being afraid, dread, or alarm; apprehension of something harmful or threatening.
16.grammar: A singular indefinite noun. The '-un' ending (nunation) marks it as nominative and indefinite — 'a fear' or simply 'fear' — and the nominative typically signals the doer or subject of a sentence, or the subject of an existential statement ('there is fear').

17.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
17.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
17.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

18.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
18.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

19.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (referring to a group of males, or a mixed group). Because it stands on its own rather than being attached to a verb or noun, it often adds emphasis, singling out or stressing the subject ('they themselves', 'it is they who').
19.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It does not take case endings; the fixed -m simply marks the plural 'they'. Standing alone, it commonly serves to emphasise or isolate the subject.

20.meaning: 'They grieve / will grieve' — to feel sorrow, sadness, or distress; to be saddened over loss or hardship.
20.grammar: A present/future-tense verb, third-person masculine plural. The 'ya-' prefix marks third person, and the '-ūna' ending marks a masculine plural subject ('they') with the verb in its full (indicative) form, describing ongoing or future action. Read together the word is 'yaḥzanūna.'
20.root: ح-ز-ن (ḥ-z-n) — grief, sorrow

1.meaning: A two-part emphasis particle meaning 'surely, indeed (already)' — 'la-' strongly affirms, and 'qad' before a past verb stresses that the action has definitely occurred.
1.grammar: Two particles fused for emphasis. 'la-' is the affirming prefix 'surely / truly.' 'qad,' when it precedes a past-tense verb, confirms and intensifies that the action really happened ('has indeed …'). Together they give a strong oath-like assurance to the statement that follows.

2.meaning: "We took / seized / received" — to take, take hold of, seize, or accept; with a pact it means to bind a party to a covenant. The form carries a 'we' subject.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb with the attached subject suffix '-nā' meaning 'we': it marks a completed action done by a group (or the royal/majestic 'We'). The '-nā' ending is what turns the bare verb into 'we did it'.

3.meaning: Covenant / solemn pact — a firm, binding agreement or treaty; a weightier, more emphatic term for a pledge that is firmly tied and ratified.
3.grammar: A noun built on a pattern denoting an instrument or firm binding (from 'to bind tightly'), hence a solemn, ratified covenant. The '-a' ending is accusative, the case that typically marks the direct object — the covenant taken or made.
3.root: و-ث-ق (w-th-q) — to bind firmly, trust, make secure

4.meaning: Sons of / children of — the plural 'sons' used in a possessive construction meaning 'the descendants or people of' someone.
4.grammar: This is the plural of 'son' in the construct (possessive) state, so it leans on a following name meaning 'the children OF …'. The -ī ending here reflects the construct form (the normal final nūn of the plural drops off when the word is joined to what follows), and it carries an oblique (accusative/genitive) sense rather than a nominative one.

5.meaning: 'Israel' — the proper name Israel, the by-name of the prophet Jacob (Yaʿqūb), and by extension his descendants.
5.grammar: A proper name of non-Arabic origin. It is grammatically 'diptote' (it does not take nunation), so it shows a single '-a' ending in places where ordinary nouns would take genitive '-i'; the '-a' here simply marks its case without the usual variation.

6.meaning: 'And We sent / dispatched' — the completed act of sending forth (such as a messenger or envoy), with 'We' as the sender.
6.grammar: A Form IV past-tense (perfect) verb with the attached subject ending -nā, meaning 'we'. The hamza prefix (a-) marks Form IV, which makes the act transitive — to send something forth. The perfect tense presents the action as completed.
6.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; (Form IV) to send forth, dispatch, commission

7.meaning: A particle-and-pronoun unit meaning 'toward them / to them' — indicating direction or the goal of a motion, attention, or address aimed at a group.
7.grammar: The preposition ilā ('to / toward'), which shifts to the form ilay- when a pronoun attaches, plus the suffix -him ('them'). The pronoun is in the genitive/oblique form required after a preposition; the whole expresses direction toward a goal.
7.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

8.meaning: 'messengers' — envoys, those sent by Allah bearing a message to people.
8.grammar: The broken (irregular) plural of rasūl ('messenger'). The -an ending is accusative with tanwīn, typically marking the word as a direct object and indefinite ('messengers').

9.meaning: 'whenever / every time' — a compound expressing that something recurs each and every time a condition is met.
9.grammar: A compound of kull ('every', in the accusative -a used adverbially) and mā ('what / the time that'). Together it works as a conditional time-word, 'each time that …', linking a repeated condition to its repeated result.

10.meaning: To come to, to arrive at someone; the act of something or someone reaching or presenting itself to a person. A core verb for arrival and the coming of events, messengers, or messages.
10.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third-person masculine singular ('he/it came') — the -a ending marks a completed act by a single masculine subject. The attached -hum is the object 'them,' the ones reached by the coming.

11.meaning: "a messenger" — one who is sent bearing a message; an envoy or apostle, here in the indefinite sense "a messenger."
11.grammar: The -un ending is nominative with nunation: the -u marks it as a subject (the doer/topic), and the final -n signals that it is indefinite ("a messenger," not "the messenger").

12.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
12.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.
12.root: — (particle + relative pronoun)

13.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
13.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

14.meaning: To incline toward, crave, or be drawn after something; the inner pull of desire or whim. The verb conveys the soul's leaning toward what it wants, often with a connotation of following caprice rather than guidance.
14.grammar: A present-tense verb in the third-person feminine singular ('she/it desires') — the ta- prefix marks the feminine (or second-person masculine) subject. The verb describes ongoing or habitual inclination and craving.
14.root: ه-و-ى (h-w-y) — to incline, fall toward, crave; whim/desire

15.meaning: Their own selves / their souls — the plural of "self" (the inner person, soul, or very being) joined to "their." It points to people's own selves, their lives, or their inner beings.
15.grammar: Plural noun "selves/souls" with the -u ending, which is nominative, typically marking the word as the subject or doer in a sentence. The attached -hum means "their," so the whole is "their selves."
15.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — soul, self, breath; the inner self and life-essence of a person

16.meaning: A group, faction, party, or portion of people — a section split off from a larger body.
16.grammar: A singular indefinite noun. The -an (tanwīn fatḥ) ending marks the accusative case with indefiniteness, typically signalling the direct object of a verb ('a group'), or an adverbial sense.

17.meaning: They denied / they cried lies; they declared (something or someone) to be false. An intensive verb meaning to reject as a lie, to disbelieve and brand untrue — directed by a plural 'they'.

parts.tr: kadhdhab (doubled dh; simplified transliterations may write 'kadhab')
parts.en: denied / branded as lies (past stem, intensive)

17.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in an intensive pattern (to treat as false, to repeatedly deny). The middle radical carries a shadda (doubling), which is exactly what marks this as the intensive form: kadhdhab- (not the simple kadhab-). The ending -ū marks the doers as 'they' — a plural, grammatically masculine group, so the whole reconstructs to kadhdhabū. Note that simplified transliterations sometimes omit the doubling and write 'kadhabū', but the doubled dh is essential to the form. The perfect tense denotes a completed action.
17.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — to lie; in this form, to call a lie, to deny as false

18.meaning: A group, party, or faction — a distinct portion of people. Joined by 'and,' it introduces a further such group, often contrasted with another previously mentioned.
18.grammar: A noun ('a group') with the -an ending, the accusative indefinite case, which typically marks the object of a verb or a fronted noun. The wa- prefix means 'and,' coordinating it with something mentioned before.
18.root: ف-ر-ق (f-r-q) — to separate, divide; a division/party

19.meaning: 'They kill / they slay' — a present/future verb describing a group taking life or putting others to death.
19.grammar: A Form I present-tense verb, 3rd person masculine plural ('they'). The ya- prefix with the -ūna ending marks the plural 'they' subject. The full -ūna (with final nūn) is the indicative, the plain ongoing present/future form used when no particle shortens it.
19.root: ق-ت-ل (q-t-l) — to kill, slay, put to death

1.meaning: 'And they reckoned / supposed / thought' — the completed act of a group believing or assuming something to be the case.
1.grammar: A connecting wa- ('and') with a Form I past-tense (perfect) verb, 3rd person masculine plural. The -ū ending marks the plural 'they' subject (the silent alif after it is spelling only). The perfect presents the act of supposing as completed.
1.root: ح-س-ب (ḥ-s-b) — to reckon, calculate; to suppose, think, deem

2.meaning: A compound particle meaning 'that … not,' 'lest,' 'so as not to.' It introduces a clause of something feared, intended-to-prevent, or negated after a verb.
2.grammar: A merging of the particle an ('that,' which introduces a verb in the subjunctive) with the negative lā ('not'); the 'n' of an assimilates into lā, giving allā. Together they mean 'that … not' and put the following verb into the subjunctive mood, often after verbs of fearing, wishing, or commanding.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'it is / it comes to be / it exists.' From kāna, the core verb of being, here in its present form expressing being or coming into a state.
3.grammar: A present/imperfect verb of being. The ta- prefix marks a third-person feminine singular subject ('it/she'). The final -a is the subjunctive ending, which typically appears after particles meaning 'that,' 'so that,' or 'until,' giving a sense of 'that it be' or 'so that it may be.'
3.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

4.meaning: A trial, test, or temptation; affliction or seduction that puts faith and character to the proof and may lead one into discord or sin.
4.grammar: A feminine singular noun (the -ah/-at ending) in the nominative case. The -un ending pairs the nominative marker -u (subject / predicate form) with nunation (-n), marking it indefinite: 'a trial'.
4.root: ف-ت-ن (f-t-n) — to test by fire, try; trial, temptation

5.meaning: 'So they became blind' — a group losing sight, often figuratively meaning they became unable or unwilling to perceive the truth; introduced by 'so/then'.
5.grammar: A linking fa- ('so/then') with a Form I past-tense (perfect) verb, 3rd person masculine plural, from a defective (weak-final) root. The plural subject 'they' is carried by the long -ū, into which the weak final root letter has merged; the trailing alif is silent (spelling only). The perfect presents the becoming-blind as a completed event.
5.root: ع-م-ي (ʿ-m-y) — to be/become blind; figuratively, to be blind to the truth

6.meaning: 'And they became deaf' — a group losing hearing, often figuratively meaning they shut themselves off from hearing or heeding; joined by 'and'.
6.grammar: A connecting wa- ('and') with a Form I past-tense (perfect) verb, 3rd person masculine plural, from a doubled (geminate) root (the doubled م shown by the shadda). The plural subject 'they' is carried by the long -ū; the trailing alif is silent (spelling only). The perfect presents the becoming-deaf as a completed event.
6.root: ص-م-م (ṣ-m-m) — to be/become deaf; to be unresponsive, closed off

7.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
7.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

8.meaning: "he turned back (in repentance) / repented" — a completed-action verb of turning away from wrongdoing and returning (to Allah); when said of Allah toward a person, it means He turned to them in mercy and accepted their repentance.
8.grammar: A past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ("he/it"). The final "-a" is the standard past-tense ending for a single male doer. The hollow root's middle weak letter appears as a long "ā" in this form.
8.root: ت-و-ب (t-w-b) — to turn back, repent, return

9.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
9.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

10.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
10.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
10.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

11.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
11.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

12.meaning: 'They became blind' — a group losing sight, often figuratively meaning they failed or refused to perceive the truth.
12.grammar: A Form I past-tense (perfect) verb, 3rd person masculine plural, from a defective (weak-final) root. The plural subject 'they' is carried by the long -ū, into which the weak final root letter has merged; the trailing alif is silent (spelling only). The perfect presents the becoming-blind as a completed event.
12.root: ع-م-ي (ʿ-m-y) — to be/become blind; figuratively, to be blind to the truth

13.meaning: 'And they became deaf' — a group losing hearing, often figuratively meaning they shut themselves off from hearing or heeding; joined by 'and'.
13.grammar: A connecting wa- ('and') with a Form I past-tense (perfect) verb, 3rd person masculine plural, from a doubled (geminate) root (the doubled م shown by the shadda). The plural subject 'they' is carried by the long -ū; the trailing alif is silent (spelling only). The perfect presents the becoming-deaf as a completed event.
13.root: ص-م-م (ṣ-m-m) — to be/become deaf; to be unresponsive, closed off

14.meaning: 'Many / numerous / much' — large in number or amount.
14.grammar: An adjective in the indefinite, nominative form: the -un ending (with nunation, the 'n' sound) marks an indefinite word in the nominative — the case used for a subject or for an adjective describing a nominative noun. It means 'a great many / much'.
14.root: ك-ث-ر (k-th-r) — to be many, abundant, numerous

15.meaning: 'Among them / from them / some of them' — the preposition 'min' ('from, of, among') joined to the attached pronoun 'hum' ('them').
15.grammar: The preposition 'min' ('from / of / among') with the attached pronoun 'hum' ('them'), referring to a masculine plural group. Together they often express 'part of them' or 'some among them'.

16.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
16.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
16.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

17.meaning: 'All-Seeing / fully observant' — one who sees clearly and with complete insight; as a divine attribute, the One who perceives all things.
17.grammar: An intensive adjective on the faʿīl pattern, denoting one who possesses sight to a high degree — 'all-seeing'. The -un ending (tanwīn) is nominative plus indefiniteness, the form used for a subject or for a predicate ('[He] is all-seeing').

18.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
18.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.
18.root: — (particle + relative pronoun)

19.meaning: 'They do / they work, they act' — a present-tense verb of doing and working, covering deeds and actions carried out by a group.
19.grammar: Present/imperfect verb. The ya-…-ūna frame marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (do).' The -ūna ending also marks the indicative mood, the plain statement form, as opposed to command or negated-future forms.
19.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deeds

1.meaning: A two-part emphasis particle meaning 'surely, indeed (already)' — 'la-' strongly affirms, and 'qad' before a past verb stresses that the action has definitely occurred.
1.grammar: Two particles fused for emphasis. 'la-' is the affirming prefix 'surely / truly.' 'qad,' when it precedes a past-tense verb, confirms and intensifies that the action really happened ('has indeed …'). Together they give a strong oath-like assurance to the statement that follows.

2.meaning: He disbelieved / rejected — to refuse faith, deny the truth, and turn away ungratefully from Allah. The root also carries the sense of covering over or being ungrateful for a blessing.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third-person masculine singular ('he disbelieved'). The final -a ending marks completed past action done by a single male. The verb denotes rejecting faith and being ungrateful, covering over the truth.
2.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover over, reject faith, be ungrateful

3.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
3.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

4.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
4.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

5.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
5.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

6.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
6.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

7.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
7.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

8.meaning: Al-Masīḥ, 'the Messiah / the Anointed One' — a title of the Prophet ʿĪsā (Jesus). It signifies one who is anointed or wiped over, traditionally linked to blessing and to his role of healing by touch.
8.grammar: A definite noun used as a title. The al- prefix means 'the', making it specific. The -u ending is nominative, the case used for the subject of a sentence or for a noun identifying who or what something is. Masīḥ has the form of a passive participle ('one who is anointed/wiped').
8.root: م-س-ح (m-s-ḥ) — to wipe, anoint, stroke over

9.meaning: 'Son' — a male child or descendant. It expresses the relationship of being the son of someone.
9.grammar: A noun. The -u ending is nominative, the case used for the subject or for a noun in apposition (a word that renames or further identifies another). The initial alif is a connecting hamza, normally elided after a preceding word, so it is read as 'bnu'. It is typically followed by the name of the father or parent ('son OF …').
9.root: ب-ن-و / ب-ن-ي (b-n-w/y) — son; to build (offspring as that which is built up)

10.meaning: "Maryam" — the personal name Mary, the mother of the prophet Jesus.
10.grammar: A proper name (feminine, foreign origin). It is diptote: it takes no -n (nunation), and in the genitive and accusative it ends in -a rather than -i, so the -a ending shown serves for both object and "of" positions.

11.meaning: 'And he said' — the act of speaking or stating, attributed to one masculine speaker, joined to what precedes by 'and.'
11.grammar: The connector 'wa-' ('and') with a past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he said.' The ending -a marks a completed action by one male, with the doer 'he' contained in the verb.

12.meaning: Al-Masīḥ, 'the Messiah / the Anointed One' — a title of the Prophet ʿĪsā (Jesus). It signifies one who is anointed or wiped over, traditionally linked to blessing and to his role of healing by touch.
12.grammar: A definite noun used as a title. The al- prefix means 'the', making it specific. The -u ending is nominative, the case used for the subject of a sentence or for a noun identifying who or what something is. Masīḥ has the form of a passive participle ('one who is anointed/wiped').
12.root: م-س-ح (m-s-ḥ) — to wipe, anoint, stroke over

13.meaning: 'O Children of … / O descendants of …' — a vocative call addressing the offspring or lineage of someone (literally 'sons of'), used to summon a people by their ancestry.
13.grammar: The vocative particle yā ('O') prefixed to the plural of 'son' in its construct (possessive-linking) form. As a construct noun it is set to be followed by a possessor ('… OF …'), giving 'O Children of …'. The -ī form here is the plural in the genitive/accusative shape used in construct.
13.root: ب-ن-ي (b-n-y) — to build; (banūn) sons, children, descendants

14.meaning: 'Israel' — the proper name Israel, the by-name of the prophet Jacob (Yaʿqūb), and by extension his descendants.
14.grammar: A proper name of non-Arabic origin. It is grammatically 'diptote' (it does not take nunation), so it shows a single '-a' ending in places where ordinary nouns would take genitive '-i'; the '-a' here simply marks its case without the usual variation.
14.root: — (proper name; no Arabic root)

15.meaning: 'Serve!,' 'worship!,' 'devote yourselves in obedience!' — a command to render worship and humble service. The underlying sense is to submit oneself wholly, in reverence and obedience, to the one served.
15.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a group. The '-ū' ending means the order is given to several people: 'you all do it!' The initial vowel is a helping prosthetic vowel that lets the word begin, since the bare command stem would otherwise start with a vowelless letter.
15.root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — to worship, to serve, devotion

16.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
16.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

17.meaning: 'My Lord' — the Master, Sustainer and Nurturer, claimed in close personal relation by the speaker.
17.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord') with the attached pronoun -ī meaning 'my'. This 'my' ending merges with the case-vowel of the noun, so a single long -ī is heard. The sense is 'the Lord who is mine'.
17.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to be lord/master, to nurture and sustain

18.meaning: 'And your Lord' — and the Lord, Master, Sustainer, and Nurturer of you all; 'Rabb' denotes the one who owns, governs, and cares for His creation, bringing it to its completion.
18.grammar: A connecting wa- ('and') with the noun 'Lord' and the possessive pronoun -kum ('your', for a group) attached. The -a vowel before the pronoun is the accusative case, typically marking the direct object of a verb.
18.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master; (Rabb) Lord, Sustainer, Owner

19.meaning: An emphasis particle fused with a pronoun, meaning 'indeed He' or 'truly He'. The particle inna strongly affirms and certifies the statement that follows ('it is certainly the case that…'), with 'He' as its subject.
19.grammar: The emphasising particle inna ('indeed/truly') with the attached pronoun -hu ('He'). inna affirms and strengthens the whole statement and grammatically takes a following noun or pronoun as its subject. The lengthened -hū is how this pronoun is pronounced after an -u vowel.

20.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
20.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.
20.root: — (pronoun)

21.meaning: An active verb: 'he associates a partner (with Allah),' i.e. he commits shirk by setting up someone or something as an equal or rival to Allah. The doer here is the one ascribing the partner.
21.grammar: A present-tense active verb. The yu- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'). The final consonant carries a silent/sukūn ending (-ik with no vowel), the jussive form that appears after conditional or negating particles (e.g. 'if he …', 'let him not …').
21.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — to share, to associate as a partner

22.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
22.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
22.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

23.meaning: A two-part connector: fa- means 'so', 'then', or 'and so', linking what follows as a result or consequence; qad before a past-tense verb intensifies it, conveying 'certainly', 'indeed', or 'already' — stressing that the action has truly and definitely occurred.
23.grammar: fa- is a connecting particle meaning 'so' or 'then', often marking a result. qad is a particle of emphasis; placed before a completed (past-tense) verb it affirms that the action has definitely or already happened. Neither part takes a case ending.

24.meaning: 'He forbade / made unlawful / declared sacredly off-limits.' To prohibit something firmly, to render it ḥarām — barred and inviolable, set outside what is permitted.
24.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) Form II verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he [did it],' a completed past action. The doubled middle root letter (Form II) gives an intensive/causative force — 'to make something forbidden/inviolable.'

25.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
25.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

26.meaning: A preposition fused with a pronoun, meaning 'upon him', 'on him', or 'toward him'. It marks the one to whom an action is directed or upon whom something rests.
26.grammar: The preposition 'upon/on' with an attached object pronoun -hi ('him', third-person masculine singular); its -i vowel is the regular form the pronoun takes after the 'y' sound. Paired with a verb of turning, this 'upon/toward him' marks the person the action reaches.

27.meaning: The Garden / Paradise — the place of lush, shaded greenery promised as the abode of bliss; literally a garden whose foliage covers the ground.
27.grammar: 'al-' is 'the'. 'janna' is a feminine noun (the tā marbūṭa ending). The final -a is accusative, the form typically marking a word as the object of a verb or, with place-nouns, the destination/location toward which an action occurs.

28.meaning: Means 'and his refuge / abode' — the place to which one ultimately resorts and where one comes to rest or dwell.
28.grammar: A place-noun (a 'place of …' form) meaning 'place of resort / dwelling.' The attached -hu is the possessive 'his / its.' The wa- prefix means 'and.' The -u vowel on the attached pronoun (hu) reflects its base form after a long vowel.
28.root: أ-و-ي (ʾ-w-y) — to take shelter, resort to, give refuge

29.meaning: The Fire — a definite noun for fire; frequently the term for the blazing punishment of the Hereafter (Hell).
29.grammar: Definite noun: 'al-' is 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the following 'n', heard as 'an-nār'). The '-u' ending is nominative, the case typically marking the subject of a sentence or the doer of an action.

30.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
30.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.
30.root: — (relative pronoun / particle)

31.meaning: A prepositional phrase, 'for/to the wrongdoers' — al-ẓālimūn being those who do wrong or injustice, who put things out of their rightful place; in religious usage especially those who wrong their own souls through disbelief or transgression.
31.grammar: A definite active participle (a 'doer' noun, 'those who wrong') in the masculine plural, governed by the preposition li- ('for, to'). The plural ending -īna is the genitive/accusative plural form, required here after the preposition. The single written lām after li- is the definite article 'the', its own letter merged into the preposition.
31.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — to do wrong, oppress; injustice

32.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
32.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

33.meaning: Helpers, supporters, defenders — those who come to one's aid and rally to one's side, particularly in a cause.
33.grammar: A broken (internally restructured) plural noun, 'helpers'. The ending -in is the indefinite genitive marker (tanwīn). The genitive typically follows a preposition or links to a preceding noun ('... of ...'); the doubled-n sound ('nunation') signals that it is indefinite ('helpers / any helpers').
33.root: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — to help, aid, give victory

1.meaning: A two-part emphasis particle meaning 'surely, indeed (already)' — 'la-' strongly affirms, and 'qad' before a past verb stresses that the action has definitely occurred.
1.grammar: Two particles fused for emphasis. 'la-' is the affirming prefix 'surely / truly.' 'qad,' when it precedes a past-tense verb, confirms and intensifies that the action really happened ('has indeed …'). Together they give a strong oath-like assurance to the statement that follows.

2.meaning: He disbelieved / rejected — to refuse faith, deny the truth, and turn away ungratefully from Allah. The root also carries the sense of covering over or being ungrateful for a blessing.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third-person masculine singular ('he disbelieved'). The final -a ending marks completed past action done by a single male. The verb denotes rejecting faith and being ungrateful, covering over the truth.
2.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover over, reject faith, be ungrateful

3.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
3.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

4.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
4.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

5.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
5.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

6.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
6.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

7.meaning: 'Third / the third' — an ordinal descriptor meaning third in a sequence; in construct it can mean 'one of three' or 'the third of three'.
7.grammar: An ordinal number, masculine singular, formed on the fāʿil template. Ordinals are their own derivational category (not active participles, even though they share that template), so this is a numeral describing rank, not the doer of a verb. The final -u is the nominative case, typically used for the subject or predicate. With no tanwīn here it stands ready to be linked to a following noun ('third OF …').
7.root: ث-ل-ث (th-l-th) — three; the basis of 'third' and 'three'

8.meaning: 'Three' — the cardinal number three; a feminine-form noun of quantity.
8.grammar: A cardinal number, feminine in form. The final -in (tanwīn) is indefinite and genitive — the case typically used after a preposition or to link the word to a preceding noun ('… OF three'). The feminine ة on '3'–'10' pairs with masculine counted nouns.

9.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
9.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

10.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
10.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

11.meaning: 'A god / a deity' — any object of worship; the general word for a deity (as opposed to the proper name Allah).
11.grammar: A singular indefinite noun 'a god'. The -in ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a/any') and in the genitive case — the form used after a preposition or in an 'of' relationship. It denotes a deity in general.
11.root: ا-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — godhood, that which is worshipped

12.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
12.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.
12.root: — (particle)

13.meaning: A god / an object of worship — a being taken as a deity and worshipped. As an indefinite noun it means 'a god' in the general sense.
13.grammar: A singular noun. The -un ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a god') and in the nominative case, typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate.
13.root: أ-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — godhood, worship, being a deity

14.meaning: One / single and unique — denoting oneness: a single individual, undivided and without partner or plurality.
14.grammar: An adjective/numeral meaning 'one.' The -un ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite and in the nominative case, the case typically used for a subject, predicate, or a descriptor agreeing with such a noun.
14.root: و-ح-د (w-ḥ-d) — oneness, singularity, uniqueness

15.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
15.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

16.meaning: The particle 'lam', a negating word used to push a verb into the past: it means 'did not' / 'has not'. Though it sits before a present-tense verb form, it negates the action as something that did not happen.
16.grammar: 'lam' is a negating particle that governs a following present-tense verb but gives it past meaning ('did not …'). It also puts that verb into the shortened (jussive) form. 'lam' itself carries no ending.

17.meaning: 'They cease / desist / refrain / come to an end' — a present/future verb describing a group stopping themselves and putting an end to an action.
17.grammar: A Form VIII present-tense verb, 3rd person masculine plural ('they'). The ya- prefix with the -ū ending marks the plural 'they' subject. The shortened ending (final nūn dropped) is the subjunctive/jussive, used after certain particles such as 'if', 'unless', or 'that'.
17.root: ن-ه-ي (n-h-y) — to forbid, restrain; (Form VIII) to desist, refrain, cease

18.meaning: 'About what' / 'of that which' — the preposition 'ʿan' ('about, concerning, away from') merged with 'mā' ('what, that which').
18.grammar: A fusion of the preposition 'ʿan' ('about, concerning') with the relative/interrogative 'mā' ('what'); the 'n' of 'ʿan' assimilates into 'mā' to give 'ʿammā'. It introduces the thing being spoken about.

19.meaning: 'They say / they keep saying' — a present-tense verb of speaking: to say, utter, or assert in words.
19.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they'), from a hollow (middle-vowel) root. The ya- prefix marks the 'they/he' class, the -ū marks the masculine plural subject, and the -na ending signals the ordinary (indicative) present, 'they are saying.'
19.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — speech; saying, uttering, asserting

20.meaning: 'He/it will surely touch / afflict / strike them' — an emphatic affirmation that something (such as a punishment) will certainly reach and befall a group.
20.grammar: A Form I present-tense verb, 3rd person masculine singular, wrapped in double emphasis: the prefix la- ('surely') and the heavy suffix -nna ('certainly'). The -nna ending fixes the verb in an emphatic future sense — 'will most certainly …'. An object pronoun ('them') is implied by the wider construction.
20.root: م-س-س (m-s-s) — to touch; to afflict, befall, strike

21.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
21.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

22.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
22.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
22.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

23.meaning: From them / among them — the preposition min ('from, out of, part of') joined to the pronoun 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group).
23.grammar: The preposition min ('from / among / part of') with the attached third-person masculine plural pronoun -hum ('them'). Pronouns after a preposition are in the genitive; the combination expresses origin, partition ('some of them'), or belonging to that group.
23.root: — (preposition with pronoun, no root)

24.meaning: Painful punishment, torment, or chastisement — suffering imposed as a penalty.
24.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The ending -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and in the nominative case, typically used for the subject or for the thing said to exist.

25.meaning: Painful, agonizing, deeply hurtful. An intensive adjective describing something that inflicts severe, grievous pain.
25.grammar: A masculine singular adjective on the intensive pattern faʿīl, conveying a strong, abiding quality ('truly painful'). The -un ending (tanwīn ḍamm) marks the nominative case (the case of a subject or of a noun's basic naming form), and the nunation shows it is indefinite.

1.meaning: 'Then will you not…?' — a rhetorical opener combining 'then/so,' a question, and a negation, used to prompt reflection ('do you then not…?').
1.grammar: A cluster of particles, not a noun or verb: the question marker 'a-' ('?'), the connector 'fa-' ('then/so'), and the negator 'lā' ('not'). Together they form a rhetorical question expecting agreement — 'will you then not…?' It has no case or tense ending of its own.

2.meaning: 'They turn back in repentance' — from tāba; describes a group repeatedly or presently returning to Allah from sin.
2.grammar: A present/ongoing verb. The ya-…-ūna frame marks a masculine-plural subject ('they') doing the action now or habitually. The full -ūna ending (rather than shortened -ū) signals the ordinary, unaltered present-tense (indicative) form.
2.root: ت-و-ب (t-w-b) — to turn back, repent, return

3.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
3.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

4.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
4.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

5.meaning: 'And they seek His forgiveness' — a present/future verb describing a group asking for pardon and the covering of sins, with 'Him' as the One whose forgiveness is sought.
5.grammar: A connecting wa- ('and') with a Form X present-tense verb, 3rd person masculine plural, plus the object pronoun -hu ('Him'). The ya- prefix and -ūna ending mark the plural 'they' subject; the full -ūna (with nūn) is the indicative, the plain ongoing present/future. Form X (ista-) carries the sense of 'seeking/asking for' the action.
5.root: غ-ف-ر (gh-f-r) — to cover, forgive; (Form X) to seek forgiveness, ask pardon

6.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
6.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
6.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

7.meaning: An intensive adjective/name meaning 'much-forgiving, ever-ready to forgive, one who veils and pardons faults again and again'. The form stresses abundance, so it conveys forgiveness as a constant, far-reaching quality.
7.grammar: An intensive adjective (the ghafūr 'doer-in-abundance' pattern), used as a divine attribute of Allah. The -un ending is nunation in the nominative case: it marks the word as indefinite and in the nominative, the case typically used for the subject or for a predicate that describes the subject.
7.root: غ-ف-ر (gh-f-r) — to cover, veil, forgive

8.meaning: Most merciful, ever-merciful; one whose mercy is constant and abundant. As a divine attribute it denotes Allah's enduring, all-embracing compassion toward His creation.
8.grammar: An intensive adjective on the form faʿīl ('abundantly/constantly merciful'). The ending -un (tanwīn) is the nominative case with indefiniteness, the form typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing it ('[He] is most merciful').

1.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
1.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

2.meaning: Al-Masīḥ, 'the Messiah / the Anointed One' — a title of the Prophet ʿĪsā (Jesus). It signifies one who is anointed or wiped over, traditionally linked to blessing and to his role of healing by touch.
2.grammar: A definite noun used as a title. The al- prefix means 'the', making it specific. The -u ending is nominative, the case used for the subject of a sentence or for a noun identifying who or what something is. Masīḥ has the form of a passive participle ('one who is anointed/wiped').
2.root: م-س-ح (m-s-ḥ) — to wipe, anoint, stroke over

3.meaning: 'Son' — a male child or descendant. It expresses the relationship of being the son of someone.
3.grammar: A noun. The -u ending is nominative, the case used for the subject or for a noun in apposition (a word that renames or further identifies another). The initial alif is a connecting hamza, normally elided after a preceding word, so it is read as 'bnu'. It is typically followed by the name of the father or parent ('son OF …').
3.root: ب-ن-و / ب-ن-ي (b-n-w/y) — son; to build (offspring as that which is built up)

4.meaning: "Maryam" — the personal name Mary, the mother of the prophet Jesus.
4.grammar: A proper name (feminine, foreign origin). It is diptote: it takes no -n (nunation), and in the genitive and accusative it ends in -a rather than -i, so the -a ending shown serves for both object and "of" positions.

5.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
5.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

6.meaning: "a messenger" — one who is sent bearing a message; an envoy or apostle, here in the indefinite sense "a messenger."
6.grammar: The -un ending is nominative with nunation: the -u marks it as a subject (the doer/topic), and the final -n signals that it is indefinite ("a messenger," not "the messenger").

7.meaning: A short particle placed before a verb to emphasize or affirm it. Before a past-tense verb it means 'indeed / certainly / has already (happened)'; before a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes / may'. It sharpens and confirms the verb that follows.
7.grammar: An indeclinable particle (its form never changes). It does not take case or tense endings; its job is to color the following verb — affirming and intensifying a past action ('has indeed done') or signaling occasional possibility with a present verb.
7.root: — (no triliteral root; an emphasizing particle)

8.meaning: 'It passed away / went by, came to an end' — said of a community, time, or era that has elapsed and is now gone. The root carries the sense of being emptied out, hence of time or people that have passed.
8.grammar: Past-tense verb. The -t (sukūn-marked -at) suffix marks a third-person feminine singular subject, 'she/it,' used here because the noun it refers to is grammatically feminine. The past tense states a completed action.
8.root: خ-ل-و (kh-l-w) — to be empty/vacant; to pass away, elapse

9.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
9.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

10.meaning: A word meaning 'before him' or 'prior to him' — combining a noun denoting that which comes earlier in time or sequence with an attached pronoun referring to a single masculine entity.
10.grammar: A noun of time ('before') carrying the genitive -i ending, with the attached pronoun -hi ('him'). The -hi form of the pronoun (rather than -hu) appears after a genitive -i vowel. Together it expresses 'before him' or 'prior to him'.
10.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to be before, to precede, to face/receive

11.meaning: "the messengers" — the definite plural of rasūl, an envoy or messenger: one sent with a message or mission. With the article it denotes 'the messengers' as a defined group.
11.grammar: A definite broken (internally formed) plural noun. The leading al- is 'the', and its 'l' assimilates into the following r- (heard as rr-). The final -u is the nominative case, the form a noun takes as the subject of a sentence.

12.meaning: And his mother — the word for a mother joined to a possessive pronoun meaning 'his', with a connecting particle meaning 'and'.
12.grammar: A noun 'mother' (umm) with the prefixed conjunction wa- ('and') and the attached pronoun -hu meaning 'his/its' (3rd-person masculine singular). The pronoun in -hu form attaches to a noun to show possession ('his ...'); its vowel shifts to -hi after an i-sound. As written here the noun carries a nominative sense, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence.
12.root: ا-م-م (ʾ-m-m) — motherhood, an origin or source from which things stem

13.meaning: An intensive description for one who is utterly truthful and faithful to the truth — habitually sincere in word and deed, never lying. The feminine form denotes such a woman of complete veracity.
13.grammar: A noun/adjective on the intensive pattern fiʿʿīl, which exaggerates the quality — not merely truthful but supremely, habitually so. The -a (tā' marbūṭa) marks the feminine. The final -un is 'nunation' (tanwīn): an indefinite ending ('a truthful one'), and its -u vowel signals the nominative, the case typically used for the subject or predicate of a sentence.
13.root: ص-د-ق (ṣ-d-q) — truthfulness, sincerity, keeping faith with reality

14.meaning: A dual past-tense verb meaning 'the two of them were' or 'they both were'. It is the verb of being applied to exactly two subjects, situating something as an existing or ongoing state in the past for a pair.
14.grammar: Past-tense verb from the family of 'to be'. The final -ā ending marks a dual subject: the action or state belongs to exactly two doers, 'the two of them'. As a verb of being, it sets up a past state or condition rather than a one-off action.
14.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

15.meaning: They both eat / consume food — a verb of eating in the present-future tense referring specifically to two persons (the dual).
15.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb. The ya- prefix marks 3rd-person and ongoing/future action ('eats / will eat'); the -āni ending makes it dual — exactly two doers — and marks the indicative mood (a plain statement of fact, as opposed to a command or a negated/subjunctive form, which would drop the final -ni).
15.root: ا-ك-ل (ʾ-k-l) — eating, consuming, taking in as food

16.meaning: The food — that which is eaten; nourishment or a meal.
16.grammar: A noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The l of al- assimilates in sound to the following ṭ (a 'sun letter'), so it is pronounced aṭ-ṭaʿām. The final -a is the accusative case, the ending typically used for the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon).
16.root: ط-ع-م (ṭ-ʿ-m) — food, taste, the act of feeding

17.meaning: A command 'look! / consider! / observe!' It directs the listener to turn their gaze or attention toward something, whether with the eye or with the mind.
17.grammar: A singular masculine imperative (command) addressed to 'you'. The helping 'u' at the start lets the cluster be pronounced, and the vowelless final consonant (-ur with sukūn) is the standard imperative ending, issuing a direct order.
17.root: ن-ظ-ر (n-ẓ-r) — to look, to see, to consider

18.meaning: An interrogative meaning 'how?' — asking about the manner, condition, or state of something ('how?', 'in what way?'). It can also express astonishment.
18.grammar: An interrogative particle (kayfa) ending in an invariable -a; it does not change for case. It asks about the manner or state of an action ('how…?') and is sometimes used rhetorically to express wonder or rebuke rather than a genuine question.
18.root: — (interrogative particle; no triliteral root)

19.meaning: We make clear / We explain plainly — a verb meaning to set something forth distinctly, to clarify and lay out evidence so it is unmistakable.
19.grammar: A present-tense verb on the intensive Form II pattern (doubled middle root letter), which carries a causative sense: 'to make something clear'. The nu- prefix means 'we'. The final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain statement ('we make clear'), as opposed to a command or subjunctive.
19.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — clarity, distinctness, separating one thing from another

20.meaning: To them / for them — the preposition li- ('to, for') joined to the pronoun 'them'. It expresses that something is directed toward, belongs to, or is for the benefit of a group.
20.grammar: The preposition li- ('to/for') combined with the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). When li- takes a pronoun its vowel becomes 'la-'. The final -u here is a connecting vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word; it carries no case meaning of its own.

21.meaning: 'The signs / the verses' — the plural of 'sign,' referring to clear indicators, proofs, miracles, or the verses of revelation that point to truth.
21.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun ('the signs'), made definite by the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The sound feminine plural takes the -i ending when it is an object of a verb or linked after a preposition or possessor — that is, when it is grammatically governed rather than serving as the subject.
21.root: ا-ي-ي (ʾ-y-y) — sign, mark, token

22.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
22.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

23.meaning: Look! / Consider! — a command to direct one's eyes or attention toward something, to observe and reflect on it.
23.grammar: A singular command (imperative) addressed to one person, 'look!'. The verb root begins with a cluster, so a helping vowel u- is prefixed to make it pronounceable. The bare stem with no ending and a vowelless final consonant (-ẓur) is the basic command form. Often paired with the preposition ilā ('look AT') or used in the sense 'reflect, consider'.
23.root: ن-ظ-ر (n-ẓ-r) — looking, seeing, regarding and reflecting

24.meaning: A particle/adverb meaning 'in whatever manner,' 'from wherever,' or 'whenever' — it asks or denotes the how, where, or when of an action in an open-ended way.
24.grammar: An invariable interrogative/conditional adverb; it has no case ending and never changes form. It introduces the manner, place, or time of an action in a general, open sense ('in what way / from where / when').

25.meaning: They are turned away / deluded — a passive verb meaning that people are diverted away from truth toward falsehood, made to deviate from what is right.
25.grammar: A present-tense verb in the passive voice — the u- prefix vowel with an a-vowel on the stem signals 'are being [acted upon]', so the subjects are the ones turned away, not the ones turning. The -ūna ending marks a 3rd-person masculine plural subject ('they') and the indicative mood (a plain statement). The sense is being led astray or deluded away from the truth.
25.root: ا-ف-ك (ʾ-f-k) — turning away, deviation, falsehood and deception

1.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
1.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

2.meaning: Do you worship / serve? — a question put to a group: 'are you worshipping?' The verb means to worship, to serve in humble devotion.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb fronted by the interrogative particle a- ('do…?'), which turns a statement into a yes/no question. The ta-…-ūna frame marks a 2nd-person masculine plural subject ('you all'), and the -ūna ending is the indicative mood (a plain statement here cast as a question). The verb denotes worship and devoted service.
2.root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — worship, servitude, humble devotion to a master

3.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
3.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

4.meaning: A noun used to mean 'besides', 'other than', 'apart from', or 'short of'. It points to something or someone set apart from, or lower/lesser than, a named party. Often used in the phrase 'besides Allah'.
4.grammar: 'dūn' functions as an adverb-like noun of place/relation. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, which appears because it follows a preposition (such as 'min', 'from') and because it links to a following noun ('other than …'). It commonly heads the construction 'besides/other than [someone]'.
4.root: د-و-ن (d-w-n) — to be low/beneath, to fall short; hence 'below, other than, besides'

5.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
5.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

6.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
6.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

7.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
7.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

8.meaning: He owns / possesses / has power over — a verb meaning to have ownership, control, or authority over something, to be able to dispose of it as one wills.
8.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya- prefix marks a 3rd-person masculine singular subject ('he') and ongoing/future action. The final -u marks the indicative mood (a plain statement). The verb spans ownership, possession, and the power or authority to control and dispose of a thing.
8.root: م-ل-ك (m-l-k) — ownership, dominion, possessing and holding sway

9.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
9.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

10.meaning: Harm / injury / hurt — that which damages or causes detriment; an affliction or adversity.
10.grammar: A noun. The final -an is 'nunation' (tanwīn) marking it as indefinite ('some harm / a harm'), and its -a vowel signals the accusative case — the ending typically used for the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon).
10.root: ض-ر-ر (ḍ-r-r) — harm, injury, damage, the opposite of benefit

11.meaning: 'And not' — a connector 'and' joined to the negative particle 'not,' negating a following statement.
11.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the negator lā ('not'). Lā commonly negates a present-tense verb or a noun. Neither particle takes case endings.

12.meaning: Benefit, profit, or advantage; something useful or gainful that brings good.
12.grammar: A singular noun marked indefinite ('benefit / some benefit'). The -an (tanwīn) combines the -a accusative case-ending — which typically marks the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon) — with the -n of indefiniteness.
12.root: ن-ف-ع (n-f-ʿ) — benefit, usefulness, profit

13.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
13.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
13.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

14.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
14.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

15.meaning: "the All-Hearing" — one who hears, perceiving all sounds completely and constantly; used as a divine name it denotes the One whose hearing is perfect and all-encompassing.
15.grammar: A definite intensive adjective/noun on the faʿīl pattern, which conveys a deep, enduring quality ('ever-hearing,' not merely 'hearing once'). The 'al-' prefix makes it definite ('the'). The final '-u' is the nominative case ending, the form a word takes when it is the subject of a sentence or a predicate/description following it.
15.root: س-م-ع (s-m-ʿ) — hearing, listening

16.meaning: The All-Knowing — one whose knowledge is complete, perfect, and all-encompassing; an intensive form stressing that knowing is an essential, constant attribute.
16.grammar: A definite noun/adjective in an intensive pattern (faʿīl) that stresses depth and permanence of the quality. The prefix 'al-' means 'the'; the final -u (ḍamma) marks the nominative case, which typically signals the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing it.

1.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
