5.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'those' — pointing to people or things that are distant or already known. It singles out a group ('those ones', 'it is those who').
5.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those'. It is fixed in form (no case endings). The -ka element signals distance/remoteness, pointing to something far off or notable. It can refer to people of either gender.

6.meaning: 'Companions / people of, dwellers, owners' — those closely associated with something, its inseparable folk, fellows, or inmates; literally the people who 'keep company with' a thing.
6.grammar: A masculine plural noun (the plural of ṣāḥib, 'companion'). The '-u' ending is nominative, typically marking the subject of a sentence; it appears here without nunation because the word is in a possessive construction ('companions OF …') with a following noun.

7.meaning: A construction meaning 'the blazing Fire / the Hellfire' — a name for the fiercely burning fire of punishment in the Hereafter.
7.grammar: The definite article al- ('the') prefixed to the noun jaḥīm ('blazing fire'), an intensive form denoting a fiercely kindled fire. The final -i ending is genitive: it typically marks the noun as the object of a preposition, or links it to a preceding noun ('… OF …').
7.root: ج-ح-م (j-ḥ-m) — intense blazing, fiercely burning fire

1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
4.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

5.meaning: A verb meaning '(that) you forbid / make unlawful' — to declare something prohibited or off-limits, or to deny it to oneself or others.
5.grammar: A present-tense (form II, intensive) verb. The tu- prefix with the plural ending marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all'). The ending is the shortened plural -ū (the 'n' of the indicative is dropped), which signals the subjunctive or jussive mood — typically used after particles such as 'do not …' or 'that …'.
5.root: ح-ر-م (ḥ-r-m) — prohibition, sanctity, that which is forbidden or sacred

6.meaning: 'Good things' — wholesome, pure, pleasant things; that which is lawful, agreeable, and beneficial, especially good foods. A feminine plural of an adjective used as a noun.
6.grammar: A sound feminine plural noun. The ending -āt marks it as a feminine plural ('good things'). The final -i vowel is the genitive case, which typically links the word to a following noun ('the good things OF…') or follows a preposition. For this plural pattern the genitive and accusative share the same -i form.

7.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
7.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

8.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'he made lawful / permitted / allowed' — to release something from prohibition and declare it permissible.
8.grammar: A past-tense (form IV) verb for a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'). It has no attached subject suffix; the bare form with its final doubled consonant carries the 'he …' meaning by itself. Form IV gives the causative sense 'to make (something) lawful'.

9.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
9.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

10.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
10.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

11.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
11.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

12.meaning: You transgress / overstep the limits / commit aggression. To exceed the bounds of what is right and just, going beyond proper limits into wrongdoing.
12.grammar: A present-tense verb in the eighth pattern for the second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The ta- prefix signals a 'you' subject; the -ū ending (with silent alif) marks the masculine plural, and the dropped final nūn shows it is in the jussive/subjunctive mood, typically governed by a preceding particle (such as a prohibition 'do not…').
12.root: ع-د-و (ʿ-d-w) — to overstep, exceed; enmity, aggression

13.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
13.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

14.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
14.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.
14.root: — (proper name)

15.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
15.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

16.meaning: He loves / likes / holds dear. To have affection for and approval of something or someone.
16.grammar: A present-tense verb in the fourth pattern, third-person masculine singular ('he…'). The yu- prefix signals a single masculine subject, and the final -u ending marks the indicative mood, presenting the action as an established fact or ongoing reality.
16.root: ح-ب-ب (ḥ-b-b) — love, affection; to hold dear

17.meaning: The transgressors / those who overstep limits / aggressors — people who habitually exceed the bounds of what is right and commit aggression.
17.grammar: An active participle (one who does the action) in the eighth pattern, masculine plural, carrying the definite article al- ('the'). The -īna ending is the masculine-plural ending used for the accusative or genitive case — typically the object of a verb or following a preposition.
17.root: ع-د-و (ʿ-d-w) — to overstep, exceed; enmity, aggression

1.meaning: A command, 'and eat.' To consume food; addressed to a group, directing them to partake.
1.grammar: A command verb ('eat!') addressed to a masculine-plural 'you,' marked by the -ū ending; as a command it has no final -na, and the original first root letter is dropped in this imperative. Wa- means 'and.'

2.meaning: From what / from that which — a fusion of the preposition 'from' with the relative 'what/which', introducing the thing or situation being referred to.
2.grammar: A merger of 'min' ('from') and 'mā' ('what/that which'); the 'n' of 'min' assimilates into the 'm' of 'mā', doubling it. The combination means 'from what ...' and typically introduces a following clause describing the thing referred to. Being particles, neither part takes a case ending.

3.meaning: A construction meaning 'He provided you / granted you sustenance' — to bestow provision (food, wealth, any good thing) upon someone. The provider is 'He'; 'you' are the recipients.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb for a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'); the final -a is the standard past-tense ending. The attached -kum ('you all') is the object; its vowel is raised to -kumu for ease before a following word beginning with the article.
3.root: ر-ز-ق (r-z-q) — provision, sustenance, bestowal of livelihood

4.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
4.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

5.meaning: Lawful, permitted, allowed — that which is sanctioned and free to be used or done, the opposite of forbidden.
5.grammar: An indefinite noun/adjective ('lawful, permitted'). The -an ending is the accusative with tanwīn (indefiniteness), generally marking the word as an object, predicate, or descriptive complement.
5.root: ح-ل-ل (ḥ-l-l) — to be lawful, permitted, loosed/untied

6.meaning: A descriptive noun/adjective meaning 'good, wholesome, pure and pleasant' — something lawful, clean, and agreeable, free of anything foul or harmful.
6.grammar: An adjective on the intensive pattern fayʿil. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative: it typically marks the word as an object of a verb, or as a describing complement of an indefinite noun ('a … good thing').

7.meaning: And be mindful of / guard yourselves against — a command addressed to a group meaning 'have taqwā': to keep a reverent, protective awareness of Allah that restrains one from wrongdoing. Often rendered 'fear,' but the sense is dutiful caution and God-consciousness rather than mere dread.
7.grammar: A plural imperative (command to more than one person). The base is the eighth-form verb ittaqā ('to be wary, to guard oneself'). The long -ū ending marks a masculine plural addressee ('you all'), telling the group to do the action. The leading wa- is the connective 'and.'
7.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to guard, shield, protect oneself

8.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
8.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

9.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
9.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

10.meaning: You — the standalone pronoun for a group of people ('you all', masculine or mixed). It is used for emphasis or as the subject standing on its own.
10.grammar: A detached subject pronoun meaning 'you all' (second-person masculine/mixed plural). Unlike pronoun endings attached to verbs or nouns, this word stands alone — typically to emphasize the subject or to begin an equational sentence ('you [are]…'). Its form is fixed and does not change for case.

11.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
11.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

12.meaning: Believers: those who have faith — people who inwardly trust and outwardly affirm Allah and what He has revealed. The active participle describes ones characterized by īmān (secure, committed belief).
12.grammar: A masculine plural active participle ('ones who believe'). The suffix -ūna (written wāw + nūn) is a single unit marking the masculine sound plural in the nominative case: it names a group performing or characterized by the action and is the form used when the word is the doer or topic of a sentence.
12.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — to be secure, to trust, to have faith

1.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
1.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

2.meaning: A verb meaning 'He calls you to account / holds you responsible (and penalizes)' — to take someone to task for what they have done. The Form III pattern conveys confronting and dealing with a person over their conduct.

parts.en: he takes to task / holds accountable

2.grammar: A present/future-tense verb of Form III (ākhādha 'to call to account'; the Form I base is akhadha 'to take/seize'), third-person masculine singular ('he holds accountable'). The indicative -u (the plain present mood) sits before the object pronoun; its vowel appears as -kumu to ease pronunciation before a following word with a connecting (waṣla) alif. The -kum is the masculine-plural object, 'you all.'

3.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
3.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

4.meaning: A phrase meaning 'for/by what is idle and unintended (in speech)' — careless, thoughtless utterance that carries no firm intent, such as an oath blurted out without resolve. The prefix marks it as the basis or cause of an action.
4.grammar: The preposition bi- ('for, by, on account of') joined to a definite noun ('the …'). The -i ending is genitive, the case required after a preposition. 'Laghw' denotes vain, purposeless, or unintended talk.
4.root: ل-غ-و (l-gh-w) — idle/vain talk, nonsense, the unintended

5.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
5.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

6.meaning: A plural noun meaning 'your oaths' — your solemn sworn statements or vows, here belonging to a plural 'you.'
6.grammar: A noun in the genitive (oblique) case, shown by the -i before the pronoun, the case used after prepositions or to link a noun to a possessor in a construct (iḍāfa). 'Aymān' is the plural of 'yamīn' (oath). The attached -kum is the masculine-plural possessive, 'your (all of you).'
6.root: ي-م-ن (y-m-n) — right hand; oath, the right side

7.meaning: 'But / however / yet' — a particle of correction and contrast that sets aside what came before and affirms something different instead.
7.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to lākin ('but / however'). Lākin is a particle of rectification: it draws a contrast with, or corrects, the preceding idea and introduces an opposing or qualifying statement ('... but rather...').

8.meaning: A verb meaning 'He calls you to account / holds you responsible (and penalizes)' — to take someone to task for what they have done. The Form III pattern conveys confronting and dealing with a person over their conduct.

parts.en: he takes to task / holds accountable

8.grammar: A present/future-tense verb of Form III (ākhādha 'to call to account'; the Form I base is akhadha 'to take/seize'), third-person masculine singular ('he holds accountable'). The final -u marks the indicative mood, the plain present used to state a fact. The attached -kum is the masculine-plural object pronoun, 'you all.'

9.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
9.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

10.meaning: You bound firmly / you knotted tightly — said of deliberately tying down and confirming a commitment, especially a solemn oath. The intensive verb conveys a firm, considered undertaking, not a careless slip of the tongue.
10.grammar: A past-tense verb in the intensive (second) form, which adds force or deliberateness to the basic 'to tie/bind.' The suffix -tum marks a completed action done by a masculine plural subject ('you all did'); the final short vowel -u is a connecting helper before a following word.
10.root: ع-ق-د (ʿ-q-d) — to tie, knot, bind, contract

11.meaning: The oaths / the sworn pledges — solemn vows in which one binds oneself, typically by invoking Allah. The plural of yamīn used for formal oaths.
11.grammar: A definite plural noun ('the oaths'). The -a ending marks the accusative case, the form a noun takes when it is the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon) — broadly, 'the [oaths] that something is done to.'
11.root: ي-م-ن (y-m-n) — right hand; by extension, an oath (sworn by clasping right hands)

12.meaning: Then its atonement / expiation is — the prescribed act that makes amends and lifts the consequence of breaking a binding pledge. Kaffāra is a covering or wiping-out of a fault through a specified penance. The attached pronoun refers back to that pledge.
12.grammar: A noun followed by an attached possessive pronoun. The -u ending is nominative, marking the word as the subject or the thing being identified. The suffix -hu means 'its/his,' linking the atonement to a previously mentioned thing. The leading fa- means 'then/so,' introducing a consequence.
12.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; here, to cover over / expiate a fault

13.meaning: Feeding / the giving of food — the act of providing meals to others. A verbal noun naming the action of nourishing people.
13.grammar: A verbal noun (the name of an action) from the fourth-form verb 'to feed.' The -u ending is nominative, the form used when the word is the subject or the thing being defined. As a verbal noun it commonly links to a following noun in the sense '… of …' (the feeding OF …).
13.root: ط-ع-م (ṭ-ʿ-m) — food, to feed, to taste

14.meaning: Ten — the cardinal number ten, used to count a quantity of things or people.
14.grammar: A number noun ('ten'). The tāʾ marbūṭa (ة) is an integral part of this base form, the shape 'ten' takes when counting masculine items (Arabic number-gender polarity); it is not a suffix. The case is shown by the final short vowel: here the kasra (-i) is genitive, marking the word as linked to a following noun in an 'of'/partitive sense ('ten OF …') or as governed by a preceding word.
14.root: ع-ش-ر (ʿ-sh-r) — ten; relating to the number ten

15.meaning: Needy people / the poor — those in want, lacking the means to meet their basic needs. A miskīn is someone reduced to humble need.
15.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun. Nouns of this pattern are 'diptote,' meaning they take a single -a ending for both the object case and the genitive/'of' relation without the usual -in. Here that -a marks it as the object of an action or as linked to a preceding number ('… of needy people').
15.root: س-ك-ن (s-k-n) — to be still, to settle; by extension, one brought low by need

16.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
16.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

17.meaning: Middling / average / most moderate — the middle point of a range, neither the highest nor the lowest. Often denotes a fair, typical, or balanced level.
17.grammar: A superlative/elative adjective ('middlemost, most moderate'). The -i ending is genitive, marking the word as linked to a following noun ('the average OF …') or as governed by a preceding word — the form used in a noun-to-noun 'of' construction or after a preposition.
17.root: و-س-ط (w-s-ṭ) — middle, center, the moderate mean

18.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
18.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

19.meaning: You feed / you provide food to — the ongoing or habitual act of giving food to others, addressed to a group.
19.grammar: A present-tense verb of the fourth (causative) form, 'to cause to eat = to feed.' The tu- prefix marks a 'you' (second-person) subject; the suffix -ūna (wāw + nūn, a single unit) marks a masculine plural doer and the indicative mood, used for an ongoing, habitual, or factual action ('you all feed / do feed').
19.root: ط-ع-م (ṭ-ʿ-m) — food, to feed, to taste

20.meaning: Your family / household — the people of one's home and kin whom one is responsible for. The attached 'your' addresses a group of owners.
20.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun. Before a pronoun ahl ('family, folk') follows the sound masculine plural pattern, whose oblique (non-subject) stem ends in -ī (a yāʾ); this -ī is that plural stem vowel, not a standalone case marker. The suffix -kum means 'your,' addressed to a masculine plural group ('you all'), marking the family as belonging to them.
20.root: ء-ه-ل (ʾ-h-l) — family, kinfolk, the people of a place

21.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
21.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

22.meaning: Their clothing — the garments provided to cover and dress them. Kiswa is a covering of clothing; the suffix points to the people being clothed.
22.grammar: A noun with an attached pronoun. The -u ending is nominative, the form used when the word is the subject or the thing being identified. The suffix -hum means 'their/them' (a masculine plural), here naming those who receive the clothing.
22.root: ك-س-و (k-s-w) — to clothe, to cover with a garment

23.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
23.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

24.meaning: Freeing / emancipating / setting free — the act of releasing someone from bondage into liberty. A verbal noun naming the deed of liberation.
24.grammar: A verbal noun (the name of an action) from the second-form verb 'to free, liberate.' The -u ending is nominative, used when the word is the subject or the thing being defined. As a verbal noun it typically links to a following noun in the sense '… of …' (the freeing OF …).
24.root: ح-ر-ر (ḥ-r-r) — to be free; to liberate, set free

25.meaning: A noun meaning 'a neck', and by extension 'a slave / bondsperson' — a person held in bondage, named figuratively by the neck.
25.grammar: Noun, feminine singular, indefinite. The final -in (tanwīn kasra) is the indefinite genitive: it typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun in an 'of …' relationship.

26.meaning: A compound meaning 'then whoever' or 'so whoever'. It combines 'then/so' with the conditional/relative 'who', introducing whatever person meets a stated condition.
26.grammar: The connector fa- ('then/so', often answering or following a condition) joined to man ('whoever / the one who'), which refers to people and introduces a condition: 'whoever does X…'. man does not change its ending; the clause after it supplies the rest of the meaning.

27.meaning: The particle 'lam', a negating word used to push a verb into the past: it means 'did not' / 'has not'. Though it sits before a present-tense verb form, it negates the action as something that did not happen.
27.grammar: 'lam' is a negating particle that governs a following present-tense verb but gives it past meaning ('did not …'). It also puts that verb into the shortened (jussive) form. 'lam' itself carries no ending.

28.meaning: He finds or obtains — to come upon, to have available, to possess the means for something.
28.grammar: A present-tense verb in the jussive mood. The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it'). The cut-short ending (a vowelless final consonant, -jid rather than -jidu) shows the jussive mood, typically triggered by a preceding particle of negation or condition such as 'does not' or 'whoever'.
28.root: و-ج-د (w-j-d) — to find, to come upon, to experience, to exist

29.meaning: Then fasting — the act of abstaining from food, drink, and other things from dawn to sunset, presented as a prescribed alternative.
29.grammar: The prefix fa- means 'then' or 'so', drawing a consequence. It is a verbal noun (naming the act of fasting) ending in -u, the nominative, which marks it as a subject or as a standalone statement ('then [there is] a fast of …').
29.root: ص-و-م (ṣ-w-m) — to fast, to abstain, to hold back

30.meaning: Three — the cardinal number 3, used in counting.
30.grammar: A number-noun. The -i ending is genitive because the word stands as the second (governed) term of a possessive construct — the 'of' phrase that completes a preceding noun, as in 'a fast of three'. In such a construct the first noun governs this one in the genitive; the genitive is therefore due to that preceding noun, not to anything that follows.
30.root: ث-ل-ث (th-l-th) — three, a third, threefold

31.meaning: Days — the plural of 'day,' periods of daylight or twenty-four-hour spans.
31.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of yawm ('day'). The ending -in (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('days') and in the genitive case, the form used in a possessive link ('… of days') or after a preposition.

32.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
32.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

33.meaning: Atonement / expiation of — the prescribed act that covers over and makes amends for a fault. Kaffāra carries the sense of wiping out a lapse through a specified penance.
33.grammar: A noun in the nominative case, shown by the -u ending — the form used when the word is the subject or the thing being identified. It commonly stands first in a noun-to-noun construction, linking to a following noun in the sense 'the expiation OF …'.
33.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; here, to cover over / expiate a fault

34.meaning: A plural noun meaning 'your oaths' — your solemn sworn statements or vows, here belonging to a plural 'you.'
34.grammar: A noun in the genitive (oblique) case, shown by the -i before the pronoun, the case used after prepositions or to link a noun to a possessor in a construct (iḍāfa). 'Aymān' is the plural of 'yamīn' (oath). The attached -kum is the masculine-plural possessive, 'your (all of you).'
34.root: ي-م-ن (y-m-n) — right hand; oath, the right side

35.meaning: 'When' — a particle introducing a time or circumstance, generally pointing to something expected or definite to come ('when/whenever it happens'). It sets up a condition or moment whose outcome then follows.
35.grammar: An indeclinable adverb/particle of time; it has no case ending and never changes form. It typically introduces a clause about a future or recurring event ('when …'), and is normally followed by a verb describing what takes place.

36.meaning: You swore / you took an oath — the completed act of making a solemn pledge, addressed to a group. To 'swear' here is to bind oneself by a vow.
36.grammar: A past-tense verb. The suffix -tum marks a completed action by a masculine plural subject ('you all did' it). Past tense presents the action as already done and finished.
36.root: ح-ل-ف (ḥ-l-f) — to swear, to take an oath

37.meaning: And keep / guard / preserve — a command to a group to safeguard something carefully, to watch over it and not let it lapse or be violated.
37.grammar: A plural imperative (command to more than one person) from the verb 'to guard, preserve.' The long -ū ending marks a masculine plural addressee ('you all'), directing the group to do the action. The leading wa- is the connective 'and.'
37.root: ح-ف-ظ (ḥ-f-ẓ) — to guard, preserve, keep watch over

38.meaning: Your oaths — the solemn pledges that belong to you (a group). The plural of yamīn with an attached 'your.'
38.grammar: A plural noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The -a before the suffix marks the accusative (object) case — the form a noun takes when it is the thing being acted upon. The suffix -kum means 'your,' addressed to a masculine plural group ('you all').
38.root: ي-م-ن (y-m-n) — right hand; by extension, an oath

39.meaning: 'Like that / thus / in this manner.' A comparison word meaning that something is done or is the case in the way just mentioned.
39.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like/as') prefixed to the demonstrative 'that'. Together they form a fixed adverbial expression, 'like that / thus', which does not change its ending with grammatical position.
39.root: — (a particle of comparison joined to a demonstrative; no root)

40.meaning: He makes clear / He explains; to set something forth plainly so that its meaning is evident.
40.grammar: A Form II present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'). The yu- prefix marks 'he', and the final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain, ongoing statement of fact (he makes clear / he is making clear).

41.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
41.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

42.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
42.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

43.meaning: 'His signs / His verses.' The plural of a word meaning a sign, token, or mark that points to a greater reality — also used for the verses of revelation — here joined to 'his'.
43.grammar: A sound feminine plural ('signs') with an attached possessive 'his'. The -i ending is the genitive case, the form this plural takes when it follows a preposition or is linked as the object of a possessor; the -hi ('his') marks ownership: 'his signs'.
43.root: أ-ي-ي (ʾ-y-y) — a sign, token, mark; a verse of revelation

44.meaning: 'so that you may…,' 'in the hope that you…' — a particle expressing purpose, expectation, or hopeful anticipation, fused with 'you (plural).' It introduces a hoped-for or intended outcome; when used of Allah it conveys the desired result rather than uncertainty.

parts.en: so that / perhaps / in hope that

44.grammar: An emphatic particle of hope/purpose belonging to the 'inna' family, which attaches a pronoun as its subject. The particle's fixed form ends in '-a,' and the suffix '-kum' is 'you (plural),' giving 'so that you (all) may…'

45.meaning: 'You (all) give thanks / are grateful'. To recognize a kindness and acknowledge it — with the heart, tongue, and deeds — toward the one who bestowed it.
45.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb. The 'ta-' prefix signals a 'you' subject, and the '-ūna' ending marks a plural masculine 'you' in the ongoing (indicative) mood — 'you all give thanks'. The retained '-na' shows the verb stands free of any negating or governing particle.

1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: 'Only / nothing but' — a restrictive particle that limits and emphasizes, asserting that the matter is exclusively so and no other ('it is only...'). It combines the emphatic 'inna' with the restricting 'mā'.
4.grammar: A compound particle formed from the emphatic inna ('indeed') and mā, which together work as a tool of restriction meaning 'only / nothing but'. It both stresses and confines the statement that follows to a single truth, excluding all alternatives.

5.meaning: Khamr: wine / intoxicants — any fermented or intoxicating drink that clouds and overcomes the intellect. The name derives from the idea of 'covering/veiling' the mind.
5.grammar: A definite noun ('the wine/intoxicant'). The -u ending is nominative, the form used when the word is the subject of a sentence or the thing being identified.
5.root: خ-م-ر (kh-m-r) — to cover, veil; hence wine, that which veils the mind

6.meaning: And gambling / games of chance — maysir: any wagering or game in which gain and loss turn on luck, dividing winners from losers without earned right.
6.grammar: A definite noun ('the gambling') preceded by the connective wa- ('and'). The -u ending is nominative, the form used when the word is the subject or the thing being identified.
6.root: ي-س-ر (y-s-r) — ease; to divide by lots, to gamble

7.meaning: And the sacrificial altar-stones — anṣāb: erected stones or altars at which offerings were slaughtered and dedicated to objects of worship other than Allah. The plural of nuṣub, 'something set up.'
7.grammar: A definite broken (irregular) plural noun preceded by wa- ('and'). The -u ending is nominative, the form used when the word is the subject or the thing being identified.
7.root: ن-ص-ب (n-ṣ-b) — to set up, erect, raise upright

8.meaning: And divining arrows — azlām: featherless arrows or lots cast to seek omens and make decisions, a form of fortune-telling. The plural of zalam.
8.grammar: A definite broken (irregular) plural noun preceded by wa- ('and'). The -u ending is nominative, the form used when the word is the subject or the thing being identified.
8.root: ز-ل-م (z-l-m) — divining arrow, lot used for seeking omens

9.meaning: An abomination / filth / defilement — rijs: something foul and impure, repugnant whether physically dirty or morally and spiritually corrupt; a thing to be shunned.
9.grammar: An indefinite noun ('a filth/abomination'). The ending -un is nominative with 'tanwīn' (the -n that marks an indefinite 'a/an'), the form used when the word is the subject or a predicate identifying what something is.
9.root: ر-ج-س (r-j-s) — filth, impurity, that which is foul

10.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
10.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

11.meaning: Work / deed / doing of — ʿamal: an action performed, a piece of work or conduct. Often used in the construction 'the work OF …,' attributing the deed to its source.
11.grammar: A noun in the genitive case, shown by the -i ending — the form a noun takes when linked to a following noun in an 'of' relation ('the work OF …') or when governed by a preceding preposition.
11.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to work, to act, to do

12.meaning: The Shayṭān — Satan, the devil: a rebellious, evil being who tempts and misleads; the term suggests one who is far removed from goodness and burning in defiance.
12.grammar: A definite masculine noun ('the Satan / the devil'). The final -i is the genitive ending, which generally links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …') or follows a preposition.
12.root: ش-ط-ن (sh-ṭ-n) — to be remote (from good/mercy); a devil

13.meaning: So shun it / avoid it / keep away from it — a command to a group to steer clear of something and stay on its far side. The attached 'it' points to the thing to be avoided.
13.grammar: A plural imperative (command to more than one person) from the eighth-form verb 'to keep away from, avoid.' The -ū ending marks a masculine plural addressee ('you all'); the attached -hu means 'it/him,' the thing acted upon. The leading fa- means 'so/then,' drawing a consequence.
13.root: ج-ن-ب (j-n-b) — side; to set aside, to keep at a distance

14.meaning: 'so that you may…,' 'in the hope that you…' — a particle expressing purpose, expectation, or hopeful anticipation, fused with 'you (plural).' It introduces a hoped-for or intended outcome; when used of Allah it conveys the desired result rather than uncertainty.

parts.en: so that / perhaps / in hope that

14.grammar: An emphatic particle of hope/purpose belonging to the 'inna' family, which attaches a pronoun as its subject. The particle's fixed form ends in '-a,' and the suffix '-kum' is 'you (plural),' giving 'so that you (all) may…'

15.meaning: You attain success / prosper / flourish. To achieve true success and lasting well-being — winning what is sought and being saved from loss.
15.grammar: A present-tense verb for the second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The tu- prefix (from the fourth verb pattern) signals a 'you' subject, and the -ūna ending marks the masculine plural in the indicative mood, stating it as an ongoing or factual reality.
15.root: ف-ل-ح (f-l-ḥ) — to succeed, prosper, thrive (originally to till/cultivate)

1.meaning: 'Only / nothing but' — a restrictive particle that limits and emphasizes, asserting that the matter is exclusively so and no other ('it is only...'). It combines the emphatic 'inna' with the restricting 'mā'.
1.grammar: A compound particle formed from the emphatic inna ('indeed') and mā, which together work as a tool of restriction meaning 'only / nothing but'. It both stresses and confines the statement that follows to a single truth, excluding all alternatives.

2.meaning: He/it wills, wants, intends, desires — to seek or aim at something purposefully.
2.grammar: A present-tense (form IV) verb, third-person masculine singular ('he wills/wants'). The ya- prefix marks 'he', and the final -u is the indicative ending, signalling an ongoing or habitual action ('does / is doing').
2.root: ر-و-د (r-w-d) — to seek, to want; (form IV) to will/intend

3.meaning: Shayṭān / Satan — a rebellious, malevolent being who incites to evil; the term denotes one that is remote from goodness and given to misleading. With 'al-', it points to the well-known devil.
3.grammar: 'al-' is 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the 'sh', doubling it). 'shayṭān' is a noun for a devil or inciter of evil. The final -u is nominative, the form a word takes as the subject or doer of an action.

4.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
4.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

5.meaning: To make something fall, drop, or take hold; to cause something to come into being, especially used of stirring up or planting enmity, discord, or strife among people.

parts.en: he/it (3rd-person masculine subject, causative form-IV imperfect prefix)
cause to fall / bring about (stem, form-IV)

5.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, 3rd-person masculine singular ('he/it'). This is a causative (form-IV) verb whose imperfect prefix is yū- (the long ū results from the prefix vowel combining with the weak first radical), giving the sense 'to make/cause to fall'. The final -a ending is the subjunctive mood, which signals that the verb is governed by a preceding particle (such as 'that' or 'so that') and expresses an intended or potential action rather than a plain fact.
5.root: و-ق-ع (w-q-ʿ) — to fall, to occur, to come to pass

6.meaning: The spatial or relational interval separating two or more parties: 'in the midst of', 'amongst', or 'in the space between'; joined to the pronoun 'you'.
6.grammar: An adverb of place, 'between/among', fixed in the accusative with an -a, here followed by the attached pronoun -kum ('you', plural). The pronoun is in the genitive position as the object of the adverb, so the whole means 'between/among you'. The final vowel appears as -u (kumu) to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a connecting vowel.
6.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, that which lies between

7.meaning: 'Enmity, hostility, open antagonism.' The noun names declared hostility — the state of treating another as a foe, from the root for transgressing and overstepping against someone.
7.grammar: A noun made definite by al- ('the'). The final -a is the accusative ending, which typically marks the word as the object of a verb (the thing acted upon). It denotes active, mutual hostility.
7.root: ع-د-و (ʿ-d-w) — to overstep, transgress; hence enmity

8.meaning: 'Hatred, intense loathing, detestation.' The noun names deep-seated aversion and ill-will — the opposite of love, from the root for finding something hateful and repugnant.
8.grammar: A noun made definite by al- ('the'). The final -a is the accusative ending, which typically marks the word as the object of a verb (the thing acted upon). This noun-form conveys an abundant, intense degree of hatred.
8.root: ب-غ-ض (b-gh-ḍ) — to hate, detest, find repugnant

9.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
9.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

10.meaning: Wine or any fermented, intoxicating drink; by extension, any intoxicant that clouds and overpowers the mind. The name literally evokes something that 'veils' the intellect.
10.grammar: A noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The final -i ending is genitive: it typically marks the word as linked to a preceding noun ('… OF …') or as following a preposition. Grammatically singular but used collectively for intoxicating drink as a class.

11.meaning: Gambling and games of chance — risking wealth on an uncertain outcome to win at another's expense. Originally a pre-Islamic game of drawing lots for portions of a slaughtered animal.
11.grammar: A noun carrying the prefix wa- ('and') and the definite article al- ('the'). The final -i ending is genitive, typically marking linkage to a preceding noun ('… OF …') or following a preposition. It is a verbal noun naming the activity of gambling.
11.root: ي-س-ر (y-s-r) — to be easy; to divide/apportion (by lot)

12.meaning: And to turn (someone) away, divert, bar, or hinder them from a path or course — to obstruct their progress toward something.
12.grammar: Begins with 'and' (wa-). The core is a present/imperfect verb, 3rd-person masculine singular ('he/it hinders/turns away'), with -kum ('you', plural) as its direct object. The final -a on the verb stem is the subjunctive mood, marking an action governed by a preceding particle and expressing purpose or possibility rather than a flat statement.
12.root: ص-د-د (ṣ-d-d) — to turn away, to bar, to avert

13.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on behalf of,' 'for,' 'about,' or 'away from.' It often conveys removing a burden from someone or acting in their place.

parts.en: on behalf of / for / away from

13.grammar: A preposition (a linking particle). It governs the noun that follows it, putting that noun into the genitive case. It does not change form.

14.meaning: Remembrance, recollection, calling to mind; also mention, invocation, or the very words by which something is brought to mind and kept present.
14.grammar: A verbal noun ('remembrance, mention'). The final -i ending is the genitive case: it typically links the word to a following noun in a possessive or 'of' relationship, or marks it as the object of a preceding preposition ('from/of remembrance').
14.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, to mention, to call to mind

15.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
15.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

16.meaning: 'And from / and away from' — the joining word 'and' combined with a preposition denoting movement or separation away from a source, point, or topic.
16.grammar: A compound of the connector 'and' (wa-) plus the preposition ʿan ('from, away from, concerning'), which conveys separation or moving away from something. Its base form is ʿan; the final vowel shows as -i (ʿani) only to smooth the join with a following word that begins with a connecting (elidable) consonant. A preposition has no case ending of its own; it puts the noun after it into the genitive.

17.meaning: The ritual Prayer — the formal worship of standing, bowing, and prostrating before Allah at appointed times. More broadly the root conveys connection, supplication, and reaching out to the divine; it is the central act of Islamic devotion.
17.grammar: A definite feminine noun ('the prayer'). The article al- means 'the.' The -i ending (on the feminine tā') is the genitive case: it typically links the word to a preceding preposition or to another noun in an 'of' relationship (e.g. 'of the prayer / to the prayer').

18.meaning: 'So/then — is it the case that…?' A linking 'then' joined to an interrogative particle that introduces a yes/no question, often carrying a sense of urging, challenge, or expectation ('will you not…?').
18.grammar: A compound of the connective fa- ('so, then', linking to what precedes) and the question particle hal, which turns a statement into a yes/no question and frequently implies expectation or exhortation. Particles like this are invariable — they take no case or mood ending.
18.root: — (particles; no triliteral root)

19.meaning: You — the standalone pronoun for a group of people ('you all', masculine or mixed). It is used for emphasis or as the subject standing on its own.
19.grammar: A detached subject pronoun meaning 'you all' (second-person masculine/mixed plural). Unlike pronoun endings attached to verbs or nouns, this word stands alone — typically to emphasize the subject or to begin an equational sentence ('you [are]…'). Its form is fixed and does not change for case.

20.meaning: Those who desist, abstain, leave off, or bring themselves to a stop — people who put an end to a course of action and refrain from it.

parts.en: desist / refrain / come to an end (stem, form-VIII)

20.grammar: An active participle ('ones who desist/refrain') in the masculine plural. The mu- prefix marks the doer of the action; the form-VIII pattern here gives a reflexive sense ('to bring oneself to a stop'). The -ūna ending marks the masculine plural in the nominative (subject) case — the form used when the word is the subject or a predicate.
20.root: ن-ه-ي (n-h-y) — to forbid, to come to an end, to desist

1.meaning: 'and obey!' — a command to a group to comply, submit to, and follow an order or authority. The leading 'wa' joins it ('and …').
1.grammar: An imperative (command) verb addressed to a masculine plural ('you all obey!'), joined by 'wa' ('and'). The '-ū' ending marks the plural addressee in commands.
1.root: ط-و-ع (ṭ-w-ʿ) — to obey, comply, submit willingly

2.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
2.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

3.meaning: 'and obey!' — a command to a group to comply, submit to, and follow an order or authority. The leading 'wa' joins it ('and …').
3.grammar: An imperative (command) verb addressed to a masculine plural ('you all obey!'), joined by 'wa' ('and'). The '-ū' ending marks the plural addressee in commands.
3.root: ط-و-ع (ṭ-w-ʿ) — to obey, comply, submit willingly

4.meaning: The messenger, envoy, or emissary: one who is sent with a message; in the Qur'an typically a prophet sent by Allah bearing revelation to a people.
4.grammar: A noun on the form faʿūl (an intensive/agent pattern, 'one sent'), prefixed with al- ('the'). The final -a ending is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb ('… the messenger') or the subject of certain particles. The 'l' of al- assimilates into the following 'r' (a 'sun letter'), pronounced ar-rasūl.

5.meaning: And be on your guard; take heed, beware, and be wary — a call to caution and watchfulness against danger or wrongdoing.
5.grammar: Begins with 'and' (wa-). The rest is a command (imperative) addressed to a group: 'beware!, be on guard!'. The -ū ending marks a command given to a masculine plural 'you'. The initial helping vowel (heard as i- after the 'and') is added only because the stem itself starts with a cluster that cannot begin a word.

6.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'fa-' ('then', 'so', 'but') drawing a consequence, joined to the conditional particle 'in' ('if'). Together: 'then if …', 'but if …'.
6.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that signals a result or transition ('then/so'). 'in' is the conditional particle 'if', introducing a supposed condition. Both are indeclinable particles with no case ending.

7.meaning: "You turned away / turned your backs / took charge" — the verb means to turn away, turn aside, or turn one's back; in another sense to take charge of or befriend. The form carries a 'you' (plural) subject.
7.grammar: A past-tense reflexive/intensive verb with the attached subject suffix '-tum' ('you all'), marking a completed action done by the plural addressees. The '-tum' ending is what makes the verb mean 'you (all) did it'.
7.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — to be near / turn toward or away / take charge

8.meaning: "then know! / so be aware!" — a command to a group to know or recognize a fact, introduced by a connector meaning "then/so."
8.grammar: An imperative (command) verb addressed to a group of males, prefixed by "fa-" ("then/so"), which links it to a preceding statement as a result or consequence. The "-ū" ending marks the plural addressee ("you all"); the imperative drops the present-tense "ta-" prefix and takes a helping initial vowel.

9.meaning: A compound particle meaning 'that …' or 'only that' — it introduces and emphasizes a fact as the content of a thought or statement; 'anna' asserts ('indeed/that') and the attached 'mā' often gives a restrictive sense ('that … is only …').
9.grammar: A combination of the emphatic particle 'anna' ('that, indeed') with 'mā'. 'Anna' introduces a noun-clause as the object of verbs like 'think' or 'know', putting the following noun in the accusative. Joined with 'mā' it frequently carries a limiting force, 'only/merely'. Particles like this do not themselves take case endings.

10.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
10.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

11.meaning: A messenger or envoy — one sent with a commission to deliver a message; bound to the pronoun 'our', i.e. a messenger belonging to and dispatched by 'us'.
11.grammar: A noun ('messenger') with the attached pronoun -nā ('our'). The -i vowel before the pronoun is the genitive case, which here marks the possessive link to the pronoun, giving 'our messenger' (literally 'messenger of us').
11.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send, to dispatch; a message or one sent

12.meaning: The conveying / the delivering (of a message): the act of passing on and communicating something so it reaches its hearers fully and clearly; a verbal noun naming that act.
12.grammar: A definite verbal noun (a noun naming an action) with the prefixed article 'al-' ('the'). The final -u is the nominative case ending, typically marking the word as the subject of a sentence or the thing being identified ('… is …').
12.root: ب-ل-غ (b-l-gh) — to reach, to arrive at; to convey

13.meaning: Clear, plain, manifest; that which makes things evident — both 'clearly apparent in itself' and 'making the truth clear to others'.
13.grammar: An active participle, 'the one that makes clear / the manifest', from a causative (form-IV) pattern, carried by the definite article al- ('the'). The final -u ending is the nominative case, the form used when the word serves as a subject or as a descriptor of such a word.
13.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — clarity, distinctness, making plain

1.meaning: A special negating verb meaning 'is not / are not'. Unlike a simple particle, it behaves like a verb (frozen in the past-tense form) and serves to deny that something is the case, cancelling an assertion of being.
1.grammar: A defective verb fixed in the 3rd-person masculine singular ('he/it is not'). The final -a is its frozen ending; it does not conjugate for tense like other verbs. Grammatically it raises its subject to the nominative and puts its predicate in the accusative, functioning to negate a state of being.

2.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
2.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
2.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

3.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
3.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

4.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
4.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

5.meaning: A two-part word: 'and' + 'they did / worked / performed.' The verb denotes doing deeds, working, putting effort into action — practical doing as opposed to mere speaking or believing.
5.grammar: A conjunction 'wa' + a past-tense verb, 3rd person masculine plural. The -ū ending marks the subject as 'they' (a group of males or a mixed group): 'and they did / worked.'

6.meaning: 'The righteous deeds / good works' — the definite plural of a word meaning that which is sound, wholesome, upright, and beneficial. As a noun it refers to good, virtuous actions that set things right.
6.grammar: A definite sound feminine plural noun ('the good deeds'). The -i ending is the oblique case used by feminine plurals to mark either the genitive ('… of …' / after a preposition) or the accusative (direct object); for this plural pattern the accusative and genitive share the same -i ending.
6.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — to be sound, good, upright, set right

7.meaning: Blame, fault, or sin incurred by an action; a moral lapse for which one is held accountable. In Qur'anic usage it most often appears in the phrase 'there is no junāḥ', i.e. no blame or wrongdoing attaches to doing something.
7.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The final -un (nominative case with nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a blame / any sin') and signals that it functions as a subject or the noun of existence ('there is a …'). The nunation (the -n sound) is the mark of indefiniteness.
7.root: ج-ن-ح (j-n-ḥ) — to incline or lean away (hence to deviate toward wrongdoing; the root also yields 'wing' and 'side')

8.meaning: A compound particle joining the preposition 'in/about' with the relative pronoun 'what', yielding 'in that which' or 'concerning what' — pointing to the matter or subject about which something is said or done.
8.grammar: A fixed combination of the preposition 'fī' and the indeclinable relative 'mā'. Being particles, neither takes a case ending; the phrase functions as 'in/about what…'.

9.meaning: They tasted or partook of food; they ate. The root sense is the act of tasting and consuming nourishment.
9.grammar: A past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine plural: 'they tasted / ate'. The -ū ending is the marker for 'they' (a group of males, or a mixed group), indicating a completed action already done.

10.meaning: 'When' — a particle introducing a time or circumstance, generally pointing to something expected or definite to come ('when/whenever it happens'). It sets up a condition or moment whose outcome then follows.
10.grammar: An indeclinable adverb/particle of time; it has no case ending and never changes form. It typically introduces a clause about a future or recurring event ('when …'), and is normally followed by a verb describing what takes place.

11.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
11.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

12.meaning: 'They were mindful of Allah / guarded themselves'. This is the act of taqwā: being conscious of Allah, guarding oneself against wrongdoing out of reverence for Him, and shielding oneself from His displeasure. Past tense, masculine plural.

parts.en: to be mindful of Allah / guard oneself

12.grammar: This is a past-tense verb of the reflexive/intensive pattern (form VIII), conveying that the subjects actively guarded and protected themselves. The '-aw' (written ـوا) ending marks a masculine plural subject acting in completed past time ('they did').
12.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to guard, protect, shield

13.meaning: And they believed / came to faith — to place trust and security in something and hold it true; here in the completed sense of having entered into belief.
13.grammar: Begins with 'and' (wa-). The core is a past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine plural ('they believed'), from a form-IV pattern meaning 'to have faith / give one's trust'. The -ū ending marks 'they' (masculine or mixed plural) and a completed action.
13.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — security, trust, faith; to be safe and to believe

14.meaning: A two-part word: 'and' + 'they did / worked / performed.' The verb denotes doing deeds, working, putting effort into action — practical doing as opposed to mere speaking or believing.
14.grammar: A conjunction 'wa' + a past-tense verb, 3rd person masculine plural. The -ū ending marks the subject as 'they' (a group of males or a mixed group): 'and they did / worked.'
14.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act

15.meaning: 'The righteous deeds / good works' — the definite plural of a word meaning that which is sound, wholesome, upright, and beneficial. As a noun it refers to good, virtuous actions that set things right.
15.grammar: A definite sound feminine plural noun ('the good deeds'). The -i ending is the oblique case used by feminine plurals to mark either the genitive ('… of …' / after a preposition) or the accusative (direct object); for this plural pattern the accusative and genitive share the same -i ending.
15.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — to be sound, good, upright, set right

16.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
16.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

17.meaning: 'They were mindful of Allah / guarded themselves'. This is the act of taqwā: being conscious of Allah, guarding oneself against wrongdoing out of reverence for Him, and shielding oneself from His displeasure. Past tense, masculine plural.

parts.en: to be mindful of Allah / guard oneself

17.grammar: This is a past-tense verb of the reflexive/intensive pattern (form VIII), conveying that the subjects actively guarded and protected themselves. The '-aw' (written ـوا) ending marks a masculine plural subject acting in completed past time ('they did').

18.meaning: And they believed / came to faith — to place trust and security in something and hold it true; here in the completed sense of having entered into belief.
18.grammar: Begins with 'and' (wa-). The core is a past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine plural ('they believed'), from a form-IV pattern meaning 'to have faith / give one's trust'. The -ū ending marks 'they' (masculine or mixed plural) and a completed action.
18.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — security, trust, faith; to be safe and to believe

19.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
19.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

20.meaning: 'They were mindful of Allah / guarded themselves'. This is the act of taqwā: being conscious of Allah, guarding oneself against wrongdoing out of reverence for Him, and shielding oneself from His displeasure. Past tense, masculine plural.

parts.en: to be mindful of Allah / guard oneself

20.grammar: This is a past-tense verb of the reflexive/intensive pattern (form VIII), conveying that the subjects actively guarded and protected themselves. The '-aw' (written ـوا) ending marks a masculine plural subject acting in completed past time ('they did').
20.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to guard, protect, shield

21.meaning: And they did good, acted excellently, or did something in the finest way — to perform a deed with beauty, mastery, and benevolence.
21.grammar: Begins with 'and' (wa-). The core is a past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine plural ('they did well / acted excellently'), from a form-IV pattern that conveys doing a thing in a good, beautiful, or beneficent manner. The -ū ending marks 'they' (masculine or mixed plural) and a completed action.
21.root: ح-س-ن (ḥ-s-n) — goodness, beauty, excellence

22.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
22.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
22.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

23.meaning: He loves / likes / holds dear. To have affection for and approval of something or someone.
23.grammar: A present-tense verb in the fourth pattern, third-person masculine singular ('he…'). The yu- prefix signals a single masculine subject, and the final -u ending marks the indicative mood, presenting the action as an established fact or ongoing reality.
23.root: ح-ب-ب (ḥ-b-b) — love, affection; to hold dear

24.meaning: The doers of good — those who act with excellence, beauty, and benevolence, doing things in the finest way and treating others kindly. 'Muḥsin' is one who practises 'iḥsān' (doing good beautifully).
24.grammar: An active participle (one who does the action) in the masculine plural. The -īna ending marks the accusative/genitive plural — the form used when the word is a direct object, follows a preposition, or is linked to a preceding noun. With 'al-' ('the'), it means 'the good-doers'.
24.root: ح-س-ن (ḥ-s-n) — beauty, goodness; here doing good with excellence

1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: He/it will most certainly test, try, and put you through a trial — to examine someone by means of an ordeal to bring out what is within them.
4.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, 3rd-person masculine singular ('he/it tests'), wrapped in a double emphasis: the prefixed la- ('surely') and the heavy suffix -nna ('most certainly') together give the strong sense 'he will assuredly test'. The attached -kum is the direct object, 'you' (plural). The final vowel shows as -u (kumu) only to smooth the join with a following word.
4.root: ب-ل-و (b-l-w) — to test, to try, to put through trial

5.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
5.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

6.meaning: 'with something / with a thing' — by means of some thing or matter; 'shay'' is the most general word for 'a thing'.
6.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the noun 'thing'. The '-in' ending marks the noun as indefinite ('a thing, something') and in the genitive case required after a preposition.
6.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — thing; to will, to want

7.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
7.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

8.meaning: 'the hunting' or 'the game' — the act of pursuing and catching wild animals, and also the prey itself that is hunted.
8.grammar: A noun carrying 'the' (the l- prefix assimilates into the following 's' sound). The -i ending is the genitive case, the form taken when a noun follows another noun in a possessive link ('… OF …') or follows a preposition.
8.root: ص-ي-د (ṣ-y-d) — to hunt, to catch game

9.meaning: It reaches it / can attain to it — the act of a thing arriving at, obtaining, or coming within reach of its target.
9.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, 3rd-person feminine singular ('it reaches/attains'), with the attached pronoun -hu ('it/him') as its object. The ta- prefix marks a feminine 'it' subject; the verb is in the indicative (plain-statement) mood, describing an actual or ongoing reaching.
9.root: ن-ي-ل (n-y-l) — to reach, to attain, to obtain

10.meaning: Your hands — the hands belonging to a group addressed as 'you'; by extension, what one's hands have done or earned.
10.grammar: The plural noun 'hands' (a broken plural of 'hand') with the attached pronoun -kum ('your,' addressing a group). The long -ī before the pronoun is part of the plural form. 'Hands' is often used figuratively for one's own deeds and doings.

11.meaning: And your spears / lances — long-shafted thrusting weapons; bound to the pronoun 'your' (plural).
11.grammar: Begins with 'and' (wa-). The core is a plural noun, 'spears/lances' (the plural of rumḥ), with the attached pronoun -kum ('your'). The -u vowel before the pronoun is the nominative case, the form used when the noun serves as a subject. The whole means 'and your spears'.

12.meaning: So that He may know / make known — that knowledge may come about or be made manifest; expressing the purpose for which something is done.
12.grammar: A purpose construction: the prefixed li- ('so that, in order that') plus a present/imperfect verb, 3rd-person masculine singular ('he knows / makes known'). Because li- expresses purpose, it puts the verb into the subjunctive mood, shown by the final -a ending, conveying an intended outcome rather than a plain fact.
12.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — knowledge, knowing, to be aware

13.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
13.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
13.root: — (proper divine name)

14.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
