7.meaning: You (all) were answered / responded to — a passive verb meaning that a reply or response was given to you.
7.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) passive verb. The -tum ending marks a second-person masculine plural subject, 'you all,' and the inner vowelling (u-i) makes it passive: 'you were answered / what response did you receive.'
7.root: ج-و-ب (j-w-b) — to answer, respond, reply

8.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
8.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

9.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
9.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

10.meaning: Knowledge; what is known with certainty — sure awareness or understanding of facts, as opposed to guesswork or conjecture.
10.grammar: A masculine noun. The final -a (fatḥa) ending marks the accusative case, which typically signals the word is the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or the subject of certain particles.

11.meaning: A combination of the preposition 'for / to' with the pronoun 'us', meaning 'for us' or 'to us / on our behalf'.
11.grammar: A preposition ('for / to') joined to the attached pronoun 'us'. The pronoun -nā always means 'us / our' regardless of position. Together they express benefit or direction toward the speakers ('for us').

12.meaning: 'Indeed you' — an emphasis particle meaning 'truly / indeed' joined to the pronoun 'you', used to open a statement with certainty and stress about the person addressed.
12.grammar: The emphasis particle 'inna' ('indeed, truly') with an attached pronoun. 'inna' adds strong assertion to a sentence and grammatically governs the following noun/pronoun in the accusative. The suffix '-ka' means 'you' (masculine singular) as its subject.

13.meaning: 'You' — the standalone, independent pronoun for addressing a single male person directly.
13.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, second-person masculine singular. Unlike attached pronoun suffixes, it stands alone and is typically used to identify or emphasize the subject ('you [yourself]').

14.meaning: Great Knower / All-Knowing — an intensive form meaning one who knows utterly and completely, especially of hidden things; a possessor of total knowledge.
14.grammar: An intensive noun of the 'faʿʿāl' pattern, expressing knowledge to the highest degree ('one who knows all things'). The final -u is the nominative case; the word commonly stands in construct with a following noun, meaning 'the All-Knower OF …'.
14.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know; knowledge

15.meaning: The unseen / the hidden things — the plural of that which is concealed or absent from perception: secrets, mysteries, all that lies beyond the reach of the senses.
15.grammar: A plural noun made definite by 'the.' The final -i is the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun in an 'of …' relationship or follows a preposition.
15.root: غ-ي-ب (gh-y-b) — to be hidden, absent, unseen

1.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
1.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

2.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
2.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

3.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
3.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

4.meaning: O ʿĪsā (Jesus) — a direct address, 'O ʿĪsā,' calling upon the prophet ʿĪsā by name.
4.grammar: A vocative phrase: the particle 'yā' ('O') used to call or address someone, attached to the proper name ʿĪsā. Being a foreign (non-Arabic) name, it does not change its ending for case.

5.meaning: "son" — a male child or descendant.
5.grammar: A noun beginning with a helping (elidable) vowel. The -a ending is accusative, which marks the word as the object of a verb or as an appositive describing a preceding accusative noun. When placed between two names, it functions as "son of …"

6.meaning: "Maryam" — the personal name Mary, the mother of the prophet Jesus.
6.grammar: A proper name (feminine, foreign origin). It is diptote: it takes no -n (nunation), and in the genitive and accusative it ends in -a rather than -i, so the -a ending shown serves for both object and "of" positions.

7.meaning: Remember! / Mention! / Call to mind! — a command to recall, bear in mind, or make mention of something.
7.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a single male: 'remember!' or 'mention!' The vowelless ending (sukūn) is the standard form for the command, and the initial vowel helps begin the word.
7.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, mention, call to mind

8.meaning: My favor; my blessing; my grace. Niʿma is a bestowed good, a bounty or kindness granted; with the attached 'my' it is a favor belonging to the speaker.
8.grammar: A feminine noun ('favor') with the first-person possessive 'my'. The base noun's final t carries the linking vowel -i before the possessive suffix -ī ('my'). Attaching a possessive pronoun puts the noun in a possessive (genitive) relationship, here meaning 'the favor that is mine'.

9.meaning: "upon you / to you / against you" — the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over') with the 'you' pronoun, carrying senses of resting upon, being directed to, or bearing upon someone.
9.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base ʿalā shifts to ʿalay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -ka means 'you' (second-person masculine singular). Prepositions themselves take no case ending.

10.meaning: A compound, 'and upon / and on / and against' — the connector 'and' joined to the preposition ʿalā ('on, over, against'). It adds a further thing onto which something rests or against which it bears.
10.grammar: The prefix wa- is the connective 'and', joining what follows to what came before. ʿalā is an indeclinable preposition that puts the following noun in the genitive case and signals 'on, over, or upon' something.

11.meaning: Your mother — 'mother / she who gave birth,' with an attached possessive 'your,' addressed to a single male.
11.grammar: A feminine noun (literally 'the female parent / bearer') with the attached possessive pronoun -ka ('your,' addressed to one male). The -i vowel before the pronoun is the genitive case, marking the noun as possessed ('the mother OF you').
11.root: و-ل-د (w-l-d) — to give birth, beget; child, parent

12.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
12.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

13.meaning: I supported you / I strengthened you / I aided you — a verb meaning to back up, reinforce, or give strength to, with 'you' as the one supported.
13.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb of Form II. The -tu ending marks a first-person singular subject, 'I,' and the attached -ka is the object pronoun 'you' (one male): 'I supported you.'
13.root: أ-ي-د (ʾ-y-d) — strength, support, reinforcement

14.meaning: "with the spirit of" — the preposition "with" joined to the noun for spirit, breath of life, or animating principle, in a possessive ("… of …") construction.
14.grammar: The bi- prefix is a preposition ("with, by"). The -i ending is genitive: required after the preposition, and it also links this noun to a following noun ("the spirit OF …").
14.root: ر-و-ح (r-w-ḥ) — spirit, breath, wind

15.meaning: The holiness / the sacredness / the holy — purity and sanctity; that which is utterly set apart from any defect. Paired with 'spirit' it denotes the Holy Spirit.
15.grammar: A noun made definite by 'the.' The final -i is the genitive case, which typically links it to a preceding noun in an 'of …' relationship (as in 'spirit OF holiness') or follows a preposition.
15.root: ق-د-س (q-d-s) — purity, holiness, sanctity

16.meaning: You speak / you talk — a verb of speaking or conversing with people, addressed to a single male.
16.grammar: A present/future (imperfect) verb of Form II. The tu- prefix marks a second-person masculine singular subject, 'you.' The final -u is the indicative mood, signalling a plain statement of ongoing or habitual action.

17.meaning: Mankind, humanity, people in general — the collective of human beings.
17.grammar: A definite noun ('the people') with the attached 'al-' ('the'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (a sun letter), which is why the 'n' is doubled — this is a pronunciation effect, not a separate piece. The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the one being acted upon) or the subject of certain particles.
17.root: ن-و-س (n-w-s) — to move/sway; by extension, people

18.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
18.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
18.root: — (particle)

19.meaning: 'The cradle' — the infant's crib or rocking-bed; by extension, the state of earliest infancy. It denotes the resting place prepared for a newborn.
19.grammar: A definite noun with the al- prefix ('the'). The -i ending is genitive, the case that typically follows a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF …'). The noun is on the faʿl pattern (mahd), a simple verbal-noun form derived from the act of smoothing/preparing a bed.
19.root: م-ه-د (m-h-d) — to spread out, smooth, prepare (a bed/resting place)

20.meaning: 'And in maturity / as a grown man' — kahl refers to a person of middle age, past youth and fully mature in his prime. With the prefixed 'and'.
20.grammar: A noun preceded by the connector wa- ('and'). The -an ending is accusative with tanwīn (nunation — the doubled 'n' sound marking an indefinite noun). The accusative here commonly expresses a circumstantial state (describing the condition or stage one is in, e.g. 'as a grown man').
20.root: ك-ه-ل (k-h-l) — to be mature / of middle age

21.meaning: 'And when / and at the time when' — the connective 'and' joined to a word that points to a past moment or circumstance ('when'), introducing the recollection of an event or situation.
21.grammar: A connective particle plus a time-word. The wa- prefix means 'and'. 'Idh' is an invariable adverb pointing to a definite time in the past ('when, at the moment that'); it has no case ending and typically introduces a clause recalling a past event.

22.meaning: I taught you — a verb meaning to instruct or impart knowledge, with 'I' as teacher and 'you' as the one taught.
22.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb of Form II (the doubled middle root letter gives a sense of careful, thorough instruction). The -tu ending marks a first-person singular subject, 'I,' and the attached -ka is the object pronoun 'you' (one male): 'I taught you.'
22.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know; knowledge, teaching

23.meaning: The Book, the Scripture — a written revelation; the term for a divinely revealed text.
23.grammar: A definite noun ('the Book') with attached 'al-' ('the'). The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb.
23.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — to write; a writing, book

24.meaning: "and the wisdom" — sound judgement and deep understanding that puts things in their right place; 'ḥikma' is wisdom: knowledge joined to right action, insight into the true nature and proper order of things.
24.grammar: A definite feminine noun ('the wisdom'); 'wa-' is 'and' and 'al-' is 'the.' The final '-a' is the accusative case ending, the form a noun takes as the direct object of a verb or when joined to another accusative noun.
24.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge, govern wisely; wisdom, sound judgement

25.meaning: At-Tawrāt, 'the Torah' — the revealed Scripture given to the Prophet Mūsā (Moses), prefixed with 'and'.
25.grammar: A definite proper noun naming a scripture, with the al- prefix ('the'); its lām assimilates into the following 'sun letter' t (heard as at-tawrāt). The word ends in tā marbūṭa, an integral part of the noun, not a detachable suffix. The accusative case vowel -a is pronounced on that tā marbūṭa (giving tawrāta), marking the noun as a direct object — the thing acted upon, e.g. that which is taught or revealed.
25.root: — (Hebrew-origin proper name; no Arabic triliteral root)

26.meaning: The Gospel (Injīl): the scripture revealed to the Prophet Jesus. A proper name for that divinely revealed Book.
26.grammar: A proper noun (a name of a revealed Book) prefixed with the connector wa- ('and') and the definite article al-. The final -a ending is accusative, the case typically marking the direct object of a verb or a word governed by certain particles.
26.root: — (proper name of a scripture; of non-Arabic origin, so no Arabic triliteral root)

27.meaning: 'And when / and at the time when' — the connective 'and' joined to a word that points to a past moment or circumstance ('when'), introducing the recollection of an event or situation.
27.grammar: A connective particle plus a time-word. The wa- prefix means 'and'. 'Idh' is an invariable adverb pointing to a definite time in the past ('when, at the moment that'); it has no case ending and typically introduces a clause recalling a past event.

28.meaning: You create / you shape / you fashion — a verb meaning to bring into form or mould something, addressed to a single male.
28.grammar: A present/future (imperfect) verb. The ta- prefix marks a second-person masculine singular subject, 'you.' The final -u is the indicative mood, signalling a plain statement of ongoing or habitual action.
28.root: خ-ل-ق (kh-l-q) — to create, shape, originate

29.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
29.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

30.meaning: Clay — wet earth or moist mud, the malleable material from which things (and, in scripture, the first human) are shaped.
30.grammar: The al- prefix means 'the'. The final -i is the genitive case, which typically follows a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of the clay' / 'from the clay'). Because the word carries 'the', it takes a single -i (not tanwīn '-in').
30.root: ط-ي-ن (ṭ-y-n) — clay, mud, moist earth

31.meaning: Like the form / like the shape — 'form, shape, or likeness' preceded by the particle 'like,' expressing resemblance to a shape.
31.grammar: A feminine noun preceded by the particle 'like/as.' The final -i is the genitive case, required after this particle; the -t- is the feminine ending (tāʾ marbūṭa) pronounced before the ending. It typically connects to a following noun ('like the shape OF …').

32.meaning: 'Birds' or 'flying creatures' — a collective term for birds as a kind.
32.grammar: A definite collective noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'); the 'l' of 'al-' assimilates in sound into the following 'ṭ' (a 'sun letter'), shown by the doubling. The '-i' ending is genitive, the case that regularly follows a preposition or links the noun to a preceding one in a possessive ('… of …') relationship.

33.meaning: By My permission / with My leave — 'permission, leave, or sanction' with the preposition 'by/with' and the possessive 'My,' meaning an act done by sanction granted by Me.
33.grammar: A noun preceded by the preposition 'by/with' and ending in the attached possessive -ī ('my'). The noun stands in the genitive case (as required after a preposition), and the -ī pronoun marks it as possessed: 'by the permission OF me.'
33.root: أ-ذ-ن (ʾ-dh-n) — to permit, allow; permission; also ear, to listen

34.meaning: Then you breathe / then you blow — the verb 'breathe / blow (air into)' joined to a connector meaning 'then' or 'so,' indicating an action that follows.
34.grammar: A present/future (imperfect) verb prefixed by 'then/so.' The ta- prefix marks a second-person masculine singular subject, 'you.' The final -u is the indicative mood, signalling a plain statement of action.
34.root: ن-ف-خ (n-f-kh) — to blow, breathe air into

35.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
35.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

36.meaning: And so it becomes / comes to be. A verb of 'being' or 'coming into a state' linked to what precedes by 'and so', expressing a result that then settles into existence.
36.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person feminine singular ('it'). The ta- prefix here marks a feminine 'it' as the subject (this prefix never marks a third-person masculine, which would take ya-). The fa- prefix marks consequence ('and so', 'then'). The final -u ending is the indicative mood, marking a plain statement of an ongoing or resulting fact. From a hollow root whose middle letter (و) shows in the long ū.

37.meaning: A bird — a flying creature; the word can denote a single bird or birds collectively.
37.grammar: The final -an (tanwīn) is the indefinite accusative: it marks the noun as 'a bird' (indefinite) and as the object of a verb or a stated outcome, rather than the subject.

38.meaning: By My permission / with My leave — 'permission, leave, or sanction' with the preposition 'by/with' and the possessive 'My,' meaning an act done by sanction granted by Me.
38.grammar: A noun preceded by the preposition 'by/with' and ending in the attached possessive -ī ('my'). The noun stands in the genitive case (as required after a preposition), and the -ī pronoun marks it as possessed: 'by the permission OF me.'
38.root: أ-ذ-ن (ʾ-dh-n) — to permit, allow; permission; also ear, to listen

39.meaning: And you heal / cure, restoring someone from illness to soundness. A causative verb: to make a sick person well.
39.grammar: Present-tense verb of the causative (Form IV) pattern, second-person masculine singular ('you'). The tu- prefix with this pattern means 'you cause to be healthy'. The final -u ending is the indicative mood, marking a plain ongoing statement. Joined by wa- ('and').

40.meaning: The one born blind — a person blind from birth (distinct from one who later loses sight).
40.grammar: The al- prefix means 'the'. This is an adjective of physical condition on the pattern 'afʿal'. The final -a is the accusative case, typically marking the word as the object of a verb. As an 'afʿal'-pattern word it is diptote, so it takes a bare -a (never tanwīn '-an').

41.meaning: And the leper — one afflicted with leprosy / a whitening skin disease (baraṣ).
41.grammar: The wa- prefix means 'and'; al- means 'the'. This is an adjective of bodily condition on the pattern 'afʿal'. The final -a is the accusative, typically marking it as the object of a verb. Being an 'afʿal'-pattern word it is diptote, taking a bare -a (no tanwīn).

42.meaning: By My permission / with My leave — 'permission, leave, or sanction' with the preposition 'by/with' and the possessive 'My,' meaning an act done by sanction granted by Me.
42.grammar: A noun preceded by the preposition 'by/with' and ending in the attached possessive -ī ('my'). The noun stands in the genitive case (as required after a preposition), and the -ī pronoun marks it as possessed: 'by the permission OF me.'
42.root: أ-ذ-ن (ʾ-dh-n) — to permit, allow; permission; also ear, to listen

43.meaning: 'And when / and at the time when' — the connective 'and' joined to a word that points to a past moment or circumstance ('when'), introducing the recollection of an event or situation.
43.grammar: A connective particle plus a time-word. The wa- prefix means 'and'. 'Idh' is an invariable adverb pointing to a definite time in the past ('when, at the moment that'); it has no case ending and typically introduces a clause recalling a past event.

44.meaning: You bring forth / draw out / cause to emerge — to make something come out from where it was.
44.grammar: Present-tense verb of the causative (Form IV) pattern, second-person masculine singular ('you'). The tu- prefix with this pattern turns 'go out' into 'cause to go out, bring forth'. The final -u ending is the indicative mood, a plain ongoing statement.

45.meaning: 'The dead' — those who have died or are without life; the lifeless, as a group.
45.grammar: A definite plural noun/adjective ('the dead'). It is of a plural pattern that ends in a fixed long -ā, so its ending does not change with grammatical position; it refers collectively to those who are dead.

46.meaning: By My permission / with My leave — 'permission, leave, or sanction' with the preposition 'by/with' and the possessive 'My,' meaning an act done by sanction granted by Me.
46.grammar: A noun preceded by the preposition 'by/with' and ending in the attached possessive -ī ('my'). The noun stands in the genitive case (as required after a preposition), and the -ī pronoun marks it as possessed: 'by the permission OF me.'
46.root: أ-ذ-ن (ʾ-dh-n) — to permit, allow; permission; also ear, to listen

47.meaning: 'And when / and at the time when' — the connective 'and' joined to a word that points to a past moment or circumstance ('when'), introducing the recollection of an event or situation.
47.grammar: A connective particle plus a time-word. The wa- prefix means 'and'. 'Idh' is an invariable adverb pointing to a definite time in the past ('when, at the moment that'); it has no case ending and typically introduces a clause recalling a past event.

48.meaning: I held back / restrained / withheld — to prevent or fend off someone or something from reaching another.
48.grammar: Past-tense (completed-action) verb, first-person singular ('I'). The suffix -tu marks that the speaker performed the action and that it is finished. The doubled middle letter resolves here into a full kafaf- form before the ending.

49.meaning: Sons of / children of — the plural 'sons' used in a possessive construction meaning 'the descendants or people of' someone.
49.grammar: This is the plural of 'son' in the construct (possessive) state, so it leans on a following name meaning 'the children OF …'. The -ī ending here reflects the construct form (the normal final nūn of the plural drops off when the word is joined to what follows), and it carries an oblique (accusative/genitive) sense rather than a nominative one.

50.meaning: 'Israel' — the proper name Israel, the by-name of the prophet Jacob (Yaʿqūb), and by extension his descendants.
50.grammar: A proper name of non-Arabic origin. It is grammatically 'diptote' (it does not take nunation), so it shows a single '-a' ending in places where ordinary nouns would take genitive '-i'; the '-a' here simply marks its case without the usual variation.

51.meaning: With you / about you / from you — the preposition ʿan ('away from, about, concerning') joined to 'you' (one male); after a verb of being pleased it carries the sense 'pleased WITH you'.
51.grammar: A preposition plus an attached pronoun. ʿan basically means moving away from, or 'about/concerning' a topic; paired with a verb of contentment it yields 'pleased with'. The suffix -ka is the second-person masculine singular object ('you', one male). Together: 'with you / concerning you'.

52.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
52.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

53.meaning: You came to them / brought (something) to them — arrival or bringing, directed toward a group.
53.grammar: Past-tense (completed-action) verb, second-person masculine singular ('you'), with an attached object pronoun 'them'. The -ta ending marks the doer as 'you'; -hum is the people the action reached. The root carries hamza as a root letter (not a weak middle letter), which surfaces here in ji'-.

54.meaning: 'With the clear proofs / evident signs' — bayyināt are plain, self-evident demonstrations that make the truth manifest, leaving no doubt.
54.grammar: Built from 'bi-' ('with/by means of') + 'al-' ('the') + a feminine plural noun meaning 'clear proofs.' The -i ending is the genitive case, required after the preposition 'bi-'; the feminine sound plural '-āt' takes -i (not -a) in this case. The whole phrase means 'with the clear proofs.'

55.meaning: 'Then he said / so he said' — the past-tense verb 'he said,' introduced by a connector meaning 'then / so,' marking what follows as the next or resulting step.
55.grammar: The prefix fa- means 'then / so,' linking this to what came before and often implying sequence or consequence. The verb is past-tense, third-person masculine singular ('he'); the final -a is the base vowel of the 3rd-person masculine singular past form, marking that a single masculine subject performed the action.

56.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
56.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

57.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
57.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
57.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

58.meaning: From them / among them — the preposition min ('from, out of, part of') joined to the pronoun 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group).
58.grammar: The preposition min ('from / among / part of') with the attached third-person masculine plural pronoun -hum ('them'). Pronouns after a preposition are in the genitive; the combination expresses origin, partition ('some of them'), or belonging to that group.

59.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
59.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

60.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
60.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

61.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
61.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

62.meaning: Magic / sorcery — the working of illusions or hidden powers to deceive perception or affect people; by extension, anything dazzling that distorts how things truly are.
62.grammar: A singular noun. The final -un (nunation/tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a/some magic') and in the nominative case — the form a noun takes as the subject of a sentence or after the verb 'to be'.

63.meaning: Clear, plain, and self-evident; that which makes things manifest. The form carries an active sense: not merely 'clear in itself' but 'making clear,' something that openly displays its nature and leaves no ambiguity.
63.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' word) on the form mufʿil, meaning 'one who/that which makes [something] clear.' The final -un is the indefinite nominative ending ('a …'), the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing it.

1.meaning: 'And when / and at the time when' — the connective 'and' joined to a word that points to a past moment or circumstance ('when'), introducing the recollection of an event or situation.
1.grammar: A connective particle plus a time-word. The wa- prefix means 'and'. 'Idh' is an invariable adverb pointing to a definite time in the past ('when, at the moment that'); it has no case ending and typically introduces a clause recalling a past event.

2.meaning: I inspired / revealed / put (something) into the heart — to convey a message or prompting swiftly and privately, especially divine inspiration.
2.grammar: Past-tense (completed-action) verb of the causative (Form IV) pattern, first-person singular ('I'). The opening a- belongs to that pattern; the suffix -tu marks the speaker as the doer and the action as finished. The final root letter (ي) shows as -ay-.

3.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
3.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

4.meaning: The disciples / devoted helpers — sincere, chosen supporters who aid a prophet's cause; classically the close companions of Jesus.
4.grammar: A masculine sound plural noun with the definite article 'the'. The ending -īna marks the plural in the accusative/genitive case — the form used for the object of a verb or after a preposition, equivalent to '…s' as objects.

5.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
5.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

6.meaning: 'Believe!' — a command to a group: have faith, trust, and affirm. Built on the verb meaning to attain security and to believe, it calls people to embrace faith.
6.grammar: A command (imperative) verb on the causative (Form IV) pattern, from the verb meaning 'to believe / to have faith'. The -ū ending directs the command to a second-person masculine plural audience, 'you all — believe!'.

7.meaning: 'In me / with me.' A preposition fused with the first-person singular pronoun, expressing attachment, belief, or trust directed toward the speaker ('me').
7.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') joined to the attached pronoun -ī ('me'). The -ī here is the first-person singular object that always follows a preposition or noun; it does not change for case. Combined sense: 'in me' or 'with me.'
7.root: — (preposition with pronoun; no root)

8.meaning: And in / by My Messenger — belief or trust placed in the one sent by Allah, here marked as belonging to the speaker ('My').
8.grammar: A noun ('messenger') governed by the preposition bi- ('in/by'), with the possessive ending -ī ('my'). The preposition would normally call for a genitive ending, but the attached 'my' takes its place. Joined by wa- ('and').

9.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
9.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

10.meaning: We have believed; we have come to faith and trust — to affirm belief, give one's trust, and feel secure in that conviction, stated by a group about themselves.
10.grammar: A past-tense verb on the form-IV pattern (āmana, 'to believe / to have faith'). The ending -nā (a single morpheme, نَا) attached to a past verb marks the subject as 'we'. The doubled 'n' heard in 'āmannā' comes from the verb stem's final 'n' meeting the 'n' that begins the -nā ending.

11.meaning: 'And bear witness / and testify' — a command to one addressee to observe, affirm, and give testimony to something.
11.grammar: wa- is 'and'. The stem is a command (imperative) verb addressed to a single person; the bare ending with no added vowel or suffix marks the masculine singular addressee ('you bear witness'). The opening vowel a/i is a helping vowel for pronunciation.
11.root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d) — to witness, to testify, to be present

12.meaning: That indeed we … — a connector affirming and emphasizing a statement about 'us': 'that we truly/certainly …'. Combines the preposition 'in/with', the emphatic particle 'indeed', and 'we'.
12.grammar: A particle cluster, not a verb. anna is an emphatic 'that' that strongly affirms the clause it introduces and grammatically puts its subject in the accusative; the attached -nā is that subject, 'we/us'. The leading bi- ('with/in') links the whole clause to what comes before.

13.meaning: 'Ones who submit / those who surrender themselves to Allah' — the plural of the active participle 'muslim,' i.e. one who willingly submits and devotes himself in obedience to Allah.
13.grammar: A masculine plural active participle (a doer-noun). The -ūna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the nominative case, the form used when the word stands as the subject or as the predicate naming who/what the subject is.
13.root: س-ل-م (s-l-m) — peace, safety, submission/surrender

1.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
1.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

2.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
2.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

3.meaning: 'The disciples' — devoted, sincere followers and close supporters; specifically the term used for the loyal companions of the prophet ʿĪsā (Jesus).
3.grammar: al- is 'the'. The noun ḥawāriyy ('disciple') takes the sound masculine plural ending -ūna, which both makes it plural ('disciples') and marks the nominative case, typically signaling the subject of a sentence.
3.root: ح-و-ر (ḥ-w-r) — whiteness/purity; to return; sincere devotion

4.meaning: O ʿĪsā (Jesus) — a direct address, 'O ʿĪsā,' calling upon the prophet ʿĪsā by name.
4.grammar: A vocative phrase: the particle 'yā' ('O') used to call or address someone, attached to the proper name ʿĪsā. Being a foreign (non-Arabic) name, it does not change its ending for case.

5.meaning: "son" — a male child or descendant.
5.grammar: A noun beginning with a helping (elidable) vowel. The -a ending is accusative, which marks the word as the object of a verb or as an appositive describing a preceding accusative noun. When placed between two names, it functions as "son of …"

6.meaning: "Maryam" — the personal name Mary, the mother of the prophet Jesus.
6.grammar: A proper name (feminine, foreign origin). It is diptote: it takes no -n (nunation), and in the genitive and accusative it ends in -a rather than -i, so the -a ending shown serves for both object and "of" positions.

7.meaning: An interrogative particle that turns a statement into a yes/no question, roughly "is it that…?" or "do…?". It can also carry a rhetorical or expectant tone rather than a literal request for information.
7.grammar: A question particle placed before a sentence to ask whether something is the case. It has no case ending and does not change form; it simply marks the words that follow as a yes/no question.

8.meaning: A verb meaning 'he is able / capable', 'he has the power to' — possessing the ability or capacity to do something. (Form X of the root, conveying 'to be able'.)

parts.en: is able / has the capacity (verb stem)

8.grammar: A present/imperfect verb of the seeking/capacity pattern (Form X istafʿala), 3rd person masculine singular. The ya- prefix means 'he'; the final -u is the indicative ending, marking a plain factual statement ('he is able / he can').
8.root: ط-و-ع (ṭ-w-ʿ) — willing obedience, capacity, being able

9.meaning: 'Your Lord / your Master' — the word for 'Lord' (one who owns, sustains, nurtures and has authority over) combined with 'your' (a single addressee); rabb carries the layered sense of master, sustainer, and the one who brings to maturity.
9.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The -u ending is the nominative case — the basic 'subject' state, used for the doer of an action or the topic of a sentence. The suffix -ka means 'your', addressed to a single masculine person. 'Rabb' bundles ownership, lordship, nurturing care, and sustaining authority into one term.

10.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
10.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

11.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'he sends down (gradually/repeatedly), he bestows' — the intensive form often implying sending down in stages or in abundance, used of revelation or grace.
11.grammar: A present-tense verb with a single masculine subject ('he'); the yu- prefix marks third-person masculine singular, and the final -a shows the subjunctive mood — used after particles like 'that' or 'so that.' The doubled middle letter (form II) intensifies the action, suggesting sending down little by little or copiously.

12.meaning: 'Upon us' / 'over us' / 'against us' — the preposition ʿalā ('on, over, upon') with an attached 'us'. It conveys something resting on, incumbent upon, or bearing against the group.
12.grammar: A preposition (ʿalā, 'upon/over') with an attached pronoun, first person plural (-nā, 'us'). When a pronoun is attached, ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay-. Such prepositional phrases put their pronoun in the object/genitive role.

13.meaning: A table spread (with food) / a laden feast — a set dinner-table, especially one bearing provisions.
13.grammar: A feminine singular noun. The final -tan (nunation on the feminine -t) marks it as indefinite ('a table-spread') and in the accusative case — the form used for the object of a verb.
13.root: م-ي-د (m-y-d) — swaying; providing a laden table

14.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
14.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

15.meaning: The sky or heaven — the canopy overhead; the expanse above the earth, also that which is elevated or raised over something. With the definite article it means 'the sky / the heaven'.
15.grammar: A noun with the definite article al- ('the'), in the genitive marked by the -i ending. (The 'l' of al- assimilates in sound into the following 's', a 'sun letter', though it is still written.) The genitive -i ending typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …').
15.root: س-م-و (s-m-w) — height, loftiness; sky, heaven

16.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
16.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

17.meaning: Be mindful and wary of — guard yourselves by placing a protective barrier between yourselves and harm or wrongdoing. This is the verb of taqwā: God-conscious caution that shields one from what is forbidden.
17.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a group ('you all'). The -ū ending directs the order to a masculine plural 'you.' Built on a reflexive pattern (Form VIII), it conveys 'protect yourselves / be on guard.'

18.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
18.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.
18.root: — (proper name)

19.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
19.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

20.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
20.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
20.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

21.meaning: 'Believers / faithful ones' — the plural of muʾmin, one who has faith and trust in Allah and grants assent to the truth.

parts.en: believers (form IV participle, oblique masculine sound plural)

21.grammar: An active participle ('one who believes') from the form IV pattern, here a masculine sound plural. The single suffix -īna is the oblique (accusative/genitive) form of the masculine plural — used for a direct object or after a preposition — as opposed to the -ūna form used for the subject. Its nūn is part of the one ending and is not a separable morpheme.
21.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — security, trust; hence faith and belief

1.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

2.meaning: We want / wish / intend — to desire and purpose something, with an inclination of the will toward it.
2.grammar: Present-tense verb of the Form IV pattern, first-person plural ('we'). Form IV here is not causative in meaning; the verb simply means 'to want / to intend'. The nu- prefix means 'we'. The final -u ending is the indicative mood, marking a plain ongoing statement. From a hollow root whose middle letter surfaces as the long ī.

3.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
3.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

4.meaning: That we may eat / so we eat — the act of eating, here in a form that expresses purpose or possibility ('that we eat').
4.grammar: Present-tense verb, first-person plural ('we'). The na- prefix means 'we'. The final -a ending is the subjunctive mood, used after words like 'that/so that' to express purpose or a hoped-for outcome ('that we may eat'), rather than a plain fact.

5.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'min' ('from / out of / some of') joined to the pronoun 'it' (feminine). Together: 'from it / out of it / of it,' indicating a source or a portion taken from a feminine thing.
5.grammar: A preposition 'min' with the attached pronoun '-hā' ('it/her'), referring to a feminine noun. 'Min' indicates origin, source, or a part taken from a whole; the attached pronoun is in the object form required after a preposition.

6.meaning: And that … may be set at ease / reassured — for the heart to grow calm and tranquil, its doubt or unrest settling into certainty.
6.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person feminine singular ('it', e.g. a heart). The ta- prefix here marks a feminine 'it' as the subject. The final -a (on the doubled stem ending) is the subjunctive mood, used after 'that/so that' to express a desired result. Joined by wa- ('and').
6.root: ط-م-أ-ن (ṭ-m-ʾ-n) — tranquillity, reassurance, settling of the heart (quadriliteral root)

7.meaning: Hearts — the seat of understanding, feeling, intention, and faith in a person. In Qur'anic usage the heart is the organ of comprehension and moral life, not merely the source of emotion.
7.grammar: A plural noun ('hearts') with the -u nominative ending, marking it as a subject. The attached -nā means 'our,' showing the hearts belong to the speakers.
7.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — to turn over; the heart

8.meaning: And that we may know — to come to know or gain sure knowledge of something.
8.grammar: Present-tense verb, first-person plural ('we'). The na- prefix means 'we'. The final -a ending is the subjunctive mood, used after 'that/so that' to express purpose ('that we may know'). Joined by wa- ('and').

9.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
9.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

10.meaning: A short particle placed before a verb to emphasize or affirm it. Before a past-tense verb it means 'indeed / certainly / has already (happened)'; before a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes / may'. It sharpens and confirms the verb that follows.
10.grammar: An indeclinable particle (its form never changes). It does not take case or tense endings; its job is to color the following verb — affirming and intensifying a past action ('has indeed done') or signaling occasional possibility with a present verb.

11.meaning: You spoke the truth to us / were truthful with us — confirming that what someone said matches reality, addressed to 'us'.
11.grammar: Past-tense (completed-action) verb, second-person masculine singular ('you'), with an attached object pronoun 'us'. The -ta ending marks the doer as 'you'; the -nā is the people addressed, 'us'.

12.meaning: And that we may be / become — a verb of 'being' expressing entering or settling into a state, in a purpose-form ('that we be').
12.grammar: Present-tense verb, first-person plural ('we'), from a hollow root (middle و shows as long ū). The na- prefix means 'we'. The final -a ending is the subjunctive mood, used after 'that/so that' to express purpose ('that we may be'). Joined by wa- ('and').
12.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, coming to be

13.meaning: 'On it / upon it / over it' — the preposition 'alā ('on, upon, against') joined to the pronoun 'it/her', referring to a single feminine or grammatically feminine thing.
13.grammar: 'ʿalā' is a preposition meaning 'on/upon/over'; its ending shifts to -ay when a pronoun is attached. The suffix -hā is the object pronoun for a single feminine (or feminine-gender) thing. Together they mean 'on it'. Words after a preposition stand in the genitive, though attached pronouns like -hā do not visibly change form.

14.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
14.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

15.meaning: 'The witnesses / those who testify' — people who observe and bear testimony, affirming the truth of something.
15.grammar: al- is 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the following 'sh', heard as ash-shā…). The active participle shāhid ('one who witnesses') takes the sound masculine plural ending -īna, which makes it plural and marks the accusative/genitive case — typically the object of a verb, or the object of a preposition, or part of a possessive phrase.
15.root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d) — to witness, to testify, to be present

1.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
1.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

2.meaning: "Isa" — the personal name of the prophet Jesus, son of Mary.
2.grammar: A proper name (a foreign/non-Arabic name). It is fully indeclinable: its ending does not change for case, so it stays the same as subject, object, or after a preposition.

3.meaning: 'Son' — a male child or descendant. It expresses the relationship of being the son of someone.
3.grammar: A noun. The -u ending is nominative, the case used for the subject or for a noun in apposition (a word that renames or further identifies another). The initial alif is a connecting hamza, normally elided after a preceding word, so it is read as 'bnu'. It is typically followed by the name of the father or parent ('son OF …').
3.root: ب-ن-و / ب-ن-ي (b-n-w/y) — son; to build (offspring as that which is built up)

4.meaning: "Maryam" — the personal name Mary, the mother of the prophet Jesus.
4.grammar: A proper name (feminine, foreign origin). It is diptote: it takes no -n (nunation), and in the genitive and accusative it ends in -a rather than -i, so the -a ending shown serves for both object and "of" positions.

5.meaning: O Allah — a vocative address to Allah. It is the divine name Allah with an added ending standing in place of the call-word 'O', so the whole word means 'O Allah' — an invocation calling directly upon Allah.
5.grammar: The proper name Allah used in direct address (vocative), with the suffixed -umma serving the function of the vocative 'O' that normally precedes a called noun. The word is fixed in this form for calling upon Allah ('O Allah').

6.meaning: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'our': the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and lovingly nurtures, addressed collectively as 'our Lord' — a communal calling upon the Sustainer.

parts.en: accusative ending (vocative of a possessed noun)

6.grammar: The noun rabb with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā ('our'). It is used as a vocative, calling out 'O our Lord'. Because the noun is possessed (a muḍāf) and called out in the vocative, it takes the accusative; that -a case vowel sits on the doubled consonant before the pronoun. The pronoun -nā shows the address is made by a group.
6.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

7.meaning: Send down! / Bring down! — a command to cause something to descend, especially to send down from above as a bestowal.
7.grammar: A command (imperative) verb of the causative (Form IV) pattern, addressed to a single masculine 'you'. The pattern turns 'come down' into 'cause to come down, send down'. It ends in a vowelless final letter (sukūn), the typical shape of a direct order.
7.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — descending, coming/sending down

8.meaning: 'Upon us' / 'over us' / 'against us' — the preposition ʿalā ('on, over, upon') with an attached 'us'. It conveys something resting on, incumbent upon, or bearing against the group.
8.grammar: A preposition (ʿalā, 'upon/over') with an attached pronoun, first person plural (-nā, 'us'). When a pronoun is attached, ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay-. Such prepositional phrases put their pronoun in the object/genitive role.

9.meaning: A table spread (with food) / a laden feast — a set dinner-table, especially one bearing provisions.
9.grammar: A feminine singular noun. The final -tan (nunation on the feminine -t) marks it as indefinite ('a table-spread') and in the accusative case — the form used for the object of a verb.
9.root: م-ي-د (m-y-d) — swaying; providing a laden table

10.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
10.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

11.meaning: The sky or heaven — the canopy overhead; the expanse above the earth, also that which is elevated or raised over something. With the definite article it means 'the sky / the heaven'.
11.grammar: A noun with the definite article al- ('the'), in the genitive marked by the -i ending. (The 'l' of al- assimilates in sound into the following 's', a 'sun letter', though it is still written.) The genitive -i ending typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …').

12.meaning: It is / it will be / so as to be — a verb of 'being', expressing existence or a state of being.
12.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person feminine singular ('it', e.g. a feminine thing). The ta- prefix here marks a feminine 'it' as the subject. The final -u ending is the indicative mood, marking a plain statement of being. From a hollow root whose middle و appears as the long ū.
12.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, coming to be

13.meaning: A combination of the preposition 'for / to' with the pronoun 'us', meaning 'for us' or 'to us / on our behalf'.
13.grammar: A preposition ('for / to') joined to the attached pronoun 'us'. The pronoun -nā always means 'us / our' regardless of position. Together they express benefit or direction toward the speakers ('for us').

14.meaning: A festival / recurring feast-day — an appointed occasion of celebration that returns again and again; an ʿīd.
14.grammar: A masculine singular noun. The final -an (nunation, written with the extra alif) marks it as indefinite ('a festival') and in the accusative case — the form used for the object of a verb or a predicate of 'to be'.
14.root: ع-و-د (ʿ-w-d) — returning, recurring

15.meaning: For the first of us — directed to the earliest among a group ('our first ones'), with 'for/to' marking the beneficiary.
15.grammar: A noun ('first') governed by the preposition li- ('for/to'), with the attached possessive 'our'. The preposition normally calls for the genitive ending; the attached -nā ('us/our') stands in its place.
15.root: أ-و-ل (ʾ-w-l) — being first, primacy, beginning

16.meaning: And the last of us / the later ones among us — those who come afterward or at the end ('our last ones').
16.grammar: A noun ('last/latter') with the attached possessive 'our', joined by wa- ('and'). It stands in the genitive position (paired with the earlier 'for the first of us'); the attached -nā ('us/our') occupies the place of the case ending.

17.meaning: And a sign / token / miraculous proof — something set up to point beyond itself, a mark or evidence that signifies a deeper truth; also a verse of revelation.
17.grammar: A feminine singular noun. The final -tan (nunation on the feminine -t) marks it as indefinite ('a sign') and in the accusative case — the form used for the object of a verb. Joined by wa- ('and').

18.meaning: From You — origin or source traced back to a single addressee ('You'), as in a gift or sending that comes 'from You'.
18.grammar: The preposition min ('from') with an attached pronoun 'you' (masculine singular). Attached pronouns after a preposition are the object of that preposition; here it conveys 'from you'.

19.meaning: A command/request meaning 'and provide us; and grant us sustenance / our daily provision' — to bestow on someone the food, livelihood, and means of life one needs.
19.grammar: A command (imperative) verb. The bare imperative stem addresses a single 'you', and the attached -nā is the object pronoun 'us', so the whole means 'provide for us'. Often used as a petition directed to Allah.
19.root: ر-ز-ق (r-z-q) — to provide sustenance, livelihood, provision

20.meaning: 'And You' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'you' (addressing a single male). The independent pronoun stresses the subject, as in 'and You [Yourself] …'.
20.grammar: A connective 'and' plus a detached subject pronoun. 'anta' is the masculine-singular 'you'; as a standalone pronoun it adds emphasis or introduces a statement about the addressee ('You are …').

21.meaning: 'Best / the best (of)' — superior to all others in goodness, excellence, or worth; the finest in its class.
21.grammar: khayr functions as a comparative/superlative noun ('better / best'). The -u ending marks the nominative case, which typically signals the subject or predicate of a sentence and also opens a possessive phrase ('the best OF …').
21.root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — goodness, that which is good or best

22.meaning: 'The providers / the sustainers' — those who supply provision and the means of life; a plural describing the doers of the act of providing.
22.grammar: A definite active participle in the masculine sound plural. The pattern fāʿil ('rāziq') names the one performing the act; the '-īna' ending marks a masculine plural in the object/genitive state (the form used after prepositions, as a non-subject, or after certain particles).
22.root: ر-ز-ق (r-z-q) — to provide sustenance, livelihood, provision

1.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
1.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

2.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
2.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

3.meaning: 'Truly I' or 'indeed I' — the emphatic affirming particle inna ('truly, indeed, certainly'), which strengthens and confirms a statement, joined to the pronoun 'I'.
3.grammar: An emphasizing particle with an attached pronoun. 'Inna' is a particle of emphasis and affirmation that introduces a statement and lends it certainty ('it is certainly the case that…'). The attached -ī is the first-person singular pronoun ('I / me') in the object form this particle requires. Together: 'Indeed I…'.

4.meaning: 'One who sends it down / the sender-down of it' — a doer-noun describing the one who causes something to descend or be sent down, with 'it' (feminine) as the thing sent.
4.grammar: An active participle of the intensive (form II) verb 'to send down', combined with the attached pronoun -hā ('it', referring to a feminine noun). The participle is nominative, and that nominative case ending — the short vowel '-u' (ḍamma) sitting on its final consonant — surfaces between the base and the pronoun, giving 'munazzil-u-hā'. Because the noun governs a following pronoun in a possessive-style construction (iḍāfa), it keeps this case vowel: literally 'the sender-down of it'.
4.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, come down; (form II) to send down

5.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
5.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.

6.meaning: A compound meaning 'then whoever' or 'so whoever'. It combines 'then/so' with the conditional/relative 'who', introducing whatever person meets a stated condition.
6.grammar: The connector fa- ('then/so', often answering or following a condition) joined to man ('whoever / the one who'), which refers to people and introduces a condition: 'whoever does X…'. man does not change its ending; the clause after it supplies the rest of the meaning.

7.meaning: To disbelieve, to reject faith; to deny the truth and to be ungrateful, covering over and refusing what is true.
7.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it'). The final consonant carries no vowel (jussive form), an ending that typically appears after conditional or commanding particles and gives the sense 'whoever/if … disbelieves'.
7.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover over; to disbelieve, reject, be ungrateful

8.meaning: After; afterward, subsequent in time or sequence. It points to what comes following something else. In this particular vowel-form it stands on its own as 'afterward' without naming what it comes after.
8.grammar: An adverb of time. The final -u here is a fixed ending taken when the word is used absolutely ('afterward'), with the thing it follows understood rather than stated, rather than being linked to a following noun.

9.meaning: A combination meaning 'from among you' or 'of you' — singling out a part or some individuals out of a larger group being addressed.
9.grammar: The preposition min ('from, among, some of') with the attached pronoun -kum, which means 'you' for a group of two or more (grammatically masculine plural). Because the pronoun follows a preposition, it is in the object form; the whole expression partitions or draws out individuals from the addressed group.
9.root: — (min is a particle/preposition; -kum is a pronoun)

10.meaning: A phrase meaning 'so indeed I…' — joining 'so/then' to an emphatic assertion about the speaker, strongly affirming what follows as true and certain.
10.grammar: Combines fa ('so, then') with inna, a particle of emphasis and certainty ('indeed, truly') that strongly affirms the statement. The attached -ī is the first-person pronoun ('I/me'), which inna takes in the accusative as its subject. Together: 'so indeed I…'.

11.meaning: 'I punish him / I will punish him' — to inflict chastisement or torment on someone, spoken in the first person about a male object.
11.grammar: A present/future-tense verb of the intensive form (severe or repeated punishing). The 'u-' prefix marks the subject 'I'; the attached -hu is the object 'him'. The bare ending (no extra suffix) is the normal indicative used for present or future action.

12.meaning: 'A punishment / torment.' A noun naming chastisement or painful suffering inflicted as a penalty.
12.grammar: A masculine noun. The -an ending marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and in the accusative case — the form a noun takes as the object of a verb or as the thing being described/quantified.
12.root: ع-ذ-ب (ʿ-dh-b) — to torment, punish, chastise

13.meaning: 'Not' — a particle of negation. Depending on context it denies a present fact, forbids an action, or rules something out ('do not / there is no').
13.grammar: A negating particle, 'not / no'. It is used to deny or prohibit — negating present-tense statements, expressing 'there is no...', or, with a command form, forbidding an action ('do not...').

14.meaning: 'I punish him / I will punish him' — to inflict chastisement or torment on someone, spoken in the first person about a male object.
14.grammar: A present/future-tense verb of the intensive form (severe or repeated punishing). The 'u-' prefix marks the subject 'I'; the attached -hu is the object 'him'. The bare ending (no extra suffix) is the normal indicative used for present or future action.
14.root: ع-ذ-ب (ʿ-dh-b) — to torment, punish, chastise

15.meaning: Anyone / a single one: 'one' used to mean a sole individual, especially in negative or conditional contexts ('not anyone', 'any single person').
15.grammar: A noun meaning 'one / a single one', frequently used for 'anyone' when paired with a negation. The final -an (nunation) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case, the case typically used for a verb's object.
15.root: ء-ح-د (ʾ-ḥ-d) — oneness, a single one

16.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
16.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

17.meaning: 'The worlds / all created beings' — the entirety of created realms and their inhabitants (humans, jinn, and everything else); a plural conveying 'all that exists'.
17.grammar: A definite masculine sound plural. The '-īna' ending marks the plural in the object/genitive state (used as a non-subject, after a preposition, or after certain particles), as opposed to the subject form '-ūna'.
17.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know; (ʿālam) a world, a domain of knowing/created order

1.meaning: 'And when / and at the time when' — the connective 'and' joined to a word that points to a past moment or circumstance ('when'), introducing the recollection of an event or situation.
1.grammar: A connective particle plus a time-word. The wa- prefix means 'and'. 'Idh' is an invariable adverb pointing to a definite time in the past ('when, at the moment that'); it has no case ending and typically introduces a clause recalling a past event.

2.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
2.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

3.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
3.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

4.meaning: O ʿĪsā (Jesus) — a direct address, 'O ʿĪsā,' calling upon the prophet ʿĪsā by name.
4.grammar: A vocative phrase: the particle 'yā' ('O') used to call or address someone, attached to the proper name ʿĪsā. Being a foreign (non-Arabic) name, it does not change its ending for case.

5.meaning: "son" — a male child or descendant.
5.grammar: A noun beginning with a helping (elidable) vowel. The -a ending is accusative, which marks the word as the object of a verb or as an appositive describing a preceding accusative noun. When placed between two names, it functions as "son of …"

6.meaning: "Maryam" — the personal name Mary, the mother of the prophet Jesus.
6.grammar: A proper name (feminine, foreign origin). It is diptote: it takes no -n (nunation), and in the genitive and accusative it ends in -a rather than -i, so the -a ending shown serves for both object and "of" positions.

7.meaning: 'Did You …?' — the questioning particle 'a' (introducing a yes/no question) joined to the standalone pronoun 'you' (single male): 'Was it you who …?'
7.grammar: An interrogative prefix 'a-' (turns a statement into a yes/no question) attached to the detached subject pronoun 'anta' ('you', masculine singular). Fronting the pronoun emphasizes the doer: 'Was it YOU who …?'

8.meaning: 'You said' — to have uttered or stated something; addressed to a single male in the completed past.
8.grammar: A past-tense verb. The suffix '-ta' marks a completed action done by 'you' (masculine singular): 'you said'.

9.meaning: To the people, for mankind — addressed or directed toward human beings in general; 'an-nās' is the collective word for 'people, humankind'.
9.grammar: The preposition 'li-' (to/for) joined to 'an-nās' (the people); the article's 'a' drops in pronunciation and its 'l' assimilates into the noun's 'n' (shown by the doubling). The -i ending is the genitive case, required because the word follows the preposition 'li-'. 'nās' is a collective noun for humankind with no singular of its own root form.

10.meaning: 'Take me (as) …' — a command addressed to a group: 'adopt me, take me for yourselves (e.g., as an object of devotion)', with 'me' as the object.
10.grammar: A command (imperative) of a form VIII verb meaning 'to take/adopt for oneself'. The stem is 'ittakhidh'; the attached wāw supplies the '-ū' that marks a plural 'you all' as the commanded subject; the following '-nī' (with its protective 'n') is the object 'me'. Reconstructed: ittakhidh + ū + nī = 'take me'.
10.root: أ-خ-ذ (ʾ-kh-dh) — to take, seize; (form VIII) to take for oneself, adopt

11.meaning: 'And my mother' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the noun 'mother' carrying the possessive 'my'.
11.grammar: Connective 'and' plus the noun 'mother' with the first-person possessive ending '-ī' (here realized as '-iya'): 'my mother'. The attached possessive can stand on any case, so it does not by itself signal subject or object.
11.root: أ-م-م (ʾ-m-m) — origin/source; (umm) mother, that from which a thing stems

12.meaning: 'Two gods / two deities' — the dual of 'ilāh' (a god, an object of worship), i.e., exactly two such objects of worship.
12.grammar: A dual noun (exactly two). The '-ayni' ending marks the dual in the object/genitive state (used as a non-subject or after a preposition), as opposed to the subject-form dual ending '-āni'.
12.root: أ-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — to worship, deify; (ilāh) a god, that which is worshipped

13.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
13.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
13.root: — (preposition)

14.meaning: A noun used to mean 'besides', 'other than', 'apart from', or 'short of'. It points to something or someone set apart from, or lower/lesser than, a named party. Often used in the phrase 'besides Allah'.
14.grammar: 'dūn' functions as an adverb-like noun of place/relation. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, which appears because it follows a preposition (such as 'min', 'from') and because it links to a following noun ('other than …'). It commonly heads the construction 'besides/other than [someone]'.
14.root: د-و-ن (d-w-n) — to be low/beneath, to fall short; hence 'below, other than, besides'

15.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
15.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

16.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
16.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

17.meaning: 'Glory be to You / how far above all flaw You are' — a set exclamation declaring Allah utterly free of any imperfection, partner, or unworthy attribute, paired with 'You.'
17.grammar: A verbal noun, subḥān ('glorification, utter freedom from imperfection'), bound to the attached pronoun -ka, 'You/Your' (one masculine addressee). It stands in the accusative (-a ending) as the exclamatory object of an understood verb ('I declare Your absolute glory') — a fixed formula of praise.
17.root: س-ب-ح (s-b-ḥ) — glorifying, declaring (Allah) free of all imperfection

18.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
18.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

19.meaning: 'It is / it comes to be' — the present-tense verb of being and becoming (from kāna). It expresses that something is the case, exists, or comes about.
19.grammar: A present/future-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he/it is, becomes'. The ya- prefix means 'he/it', and the final -u is the indicative ending, marking a plain factual statement (as opposed to a command or a negated/subjunctive form).
19.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

20.meaning: 'to Me' or 'for Me' — the preposition 'to/for' fused with the first-person pronoun, expressing direction, benefit, or belonging toward the speaker.
20.grammar: A preposition ('to/for') with the attached pronoun '-ī' ('me'). Together they express benefit, direction, or attribution toward the first person.

21.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
21.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'
21.root: — (particle; no root)

22.meaning: '(that) I say' — first-person 'I say/utter', in the form used after particles meaning 'that', 'so that', or 'to'.
22.grammar: A present-tense verb with the 'a-' prefix meaning 'I'. The final '-a' is the subjunctive ending: it appears when the verb follows a particle such as 'that / so that / in order to', giving the sense 'that I should say'.
22.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak, utter

23.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
23.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

24.meaning: A special negating verb meaning 'is not / are not'. Unlike a simple particle, it behaves like a verb (frozen in the past-tense form) and serves to deny that something is the case, cancelling an assertion of being.
