24.grammar: A defective verb fixed in the 3rd-person masculine singular ('he/it is not'). The final -a is its frozen ending; it does not conjugate for tense like other verbs. Grammatically it raises its subject to the nominative and puts its predicate in the accusative, functioning to negate a state of being.

25.meaning: 'to me / for me' — the preposition 'to/for' fused with the pronoun 'me'; expresses that something belongs to, is owed to, or is directed toward the speaker.
25.grammar: A preposition of belonging/direction ('to, for') plus the first-person pronoun 'me'. The combination conveys possession or entitlement ('I have / it is mine / it is owed to me').

26.meaning: 'with truth / rightfully' — the preposition 'with/by' joined to 'ḥaqq' (truth, right, what is true and rightful), i.e., 'in a manner that is true and warranted'. The '-in' marks it as indefinite ('a right / any right').
26.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') plus the noun 'ḥaqq'. The '-in' (nunation) ending shows the noun is indefinite and in the genitive state required after a preposition: roughly 'with a [valid] right'.
26.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — to be true, right, established; (ḥaqq) truth, reality, a rightful due

27.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
27.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

28.meaning: A verb meaning 'I was / I had been,' the core verb of being placed in the past for the speaker. It links 'I' to a past state or description: 'I used to be / I came to be in such a condition.'
28.grammar: The past-tense verb 'to be,' first-person singular. The suffix '-tu' is the past-tense ending that means 'I' (the one who did/was). It expresses a completed or settled past state — 'I was, I had been.'
28.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

29.meaning: 'I said it' — first-person completed past 'I said', with 'it' (a male/masculine thing) as what was said.
29.grammar: A past-tense verb: the '-tu' suffix marks a completed action by 'I', and the attached '-hu' is the object 'it/him'. Together: 'I said it'.

30.meaning: A two-part connector: fa- means 'so', 'then', or 'and so', linking what follows as a result or consequence; qad before a past-tense verb intensifies it, conveying 'certainly', 'indeed', or 'already' — stressing that the action has truly and definitely occurred.
30.grammar: fa- is a connecting particle meaning 'so' or 'then', often marking a result. qad is a particle of emphasis; placed before a completed (past-tense) verb it affirms that the action has definitely or already happened. Neither part takes a case ending.

31.meaning: 'You knew it / You would have known it' — second-person (single male) completed knowing, with 'it' (masculine) as the thing known.
31.grammar: A past-tense verb: the '-ta' suffix marks a completed action by 'you' (masculine singular), and the attached '-hu' is the object 'it/him': 'you knew it'.
31.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know, be aware, have knowledge

32.meaning: You (masculine singular) know, are aware of, or have knowledge of something. A simple present-tense verb of knowing.
32.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The ta- prefix marks a second-person masculine singular subject ('you'). The final -u ending is the indicative mood, used for a straightforward statement ('you know / you do know').

33.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
33.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

34.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
34.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

35.meaning: 'Myself / my own soul'. The word nafs means a self, soul, person or inner being; with the attached 'my' it points to the speaker's own self.
35.grammar: Noun plus the attached possessor -ī meaning 'my'. This 'my' suffix replaces the case-ending, so the noun's grammatical role (subject, object, or after a preposition) is read from context rather than from a final short vowel.

36.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
36.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

37.meaning: 'I know' — a present-tense verb of knowing: to have certain knowledge or awareness of something.
37.grammar: A present/future (Form I) verb, first-person singular ('I'), marked by the prefix a-. This a- is the first-person agreement marker built into the conjugation, not a free-standing pronoun. The final -u marks the indicative — a plain statement of ongoing or habitual knowing.

38.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
38.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

39.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
39.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

40.meaning: 'Yourself / your own self / your soul' — the noun 'nafs' (self, soul, person, inner being) carrying the possessive 'your' (single male).
40.grammar: The noun 'nafs' ('self/soul') with the second-person masculine-singular possessive ending '-ka' (here '-ika'): 'your self'. The attached possessive can sit on any case, so it alone does not mark subject or object.
40.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — soul, self, breath; the inner being of a person

41.meaning: 'Indeed you' — an emphasis particle meaning 'truly / indeed' joined to the pronoun 'you', used to open a statement with certainty and stress about the person addressed.
41.grammar: The emphasis particle 'inna' ('indeed, truly') with an attached pronoun. 'inna' adds strong assertion to a sentence and grammatically governs the following noun/pronoun in the accusative. The suffix '-ka' means 'you' (masculine singular) as its subject.

42.meaning: 'You' — the standalone, independent pronoun for addressing a single male person directly.
42.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, second-person masculine singular. Unlike attached pronoun suffixes, it stands alone and is typically used to identify or emphasize the subject ('you [yourself]').

43.meaning: Great Knower / All-Knowing — an intensive form meaning one who knows utterly and completely, especially of hidden things; a possessor of total knowledge.
43.grammar: An intensive noun of the 'faʿʿāl' pattern, expressing knowledge to the highest degree ('one who knows all things'). The final -u is the nominative case; the word commonly stands in construct with a following noun, meaning 'the All-Knower OF …'.

44.meaning: The unseen / the hidden things — the plural of that which is concealed or absent from perception: secrets, mysteries, all that lies beyond the reach of the senses.
44.grammar: A plural noun made definite by 'the.' The final -i is the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun in an 'of …' relationship or follows a preposition.
44.root: غ-ي-ب (gh-y-b) — to be hidden, absent, unseen

1.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
1.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

2.meaning: 'I said' — first-person completed past of uttering/stating: 'I said'.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb. The suffix '-tu' marks a completed action done by 'I': 'I said'.

3.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
3.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

4.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
4.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

5.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
5.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

6.meaning: 'You commanded me / ordered me' — second-person (single male) past act of commanding, with 'me' as the one commanded.
6.grammar: A past-tense verb: '-ta' marks a completed action by 'you' (masculine singular); the attached '-nī' (with the protective 'n') is the object 'me': 'you commanded me'.

7.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
7.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

8.meaning: That — an explanatory particle introducing the content of a preceding statement or command, roughly 'namely that …' or 'to the effect that …'. It unpacks what was said or commanded.
8.grammar: An explanatory particle 'an' meaning 'that / namely,' used to spell out the substance of a foregoing verb of saying or commanding (so the words that follow explain it). Its base form ends in a vowel-less 'n'; the -i shown here is a helping vowel added only to ease pronunciation before a following consonant, not a case ending.

9.meaning: 'Serve!,' 'worship!,' 'devote yourselves in obedience!' — a command to render worship and humble service. The underlying sense is to submit oneself wholly, in reverence and obedience, to the one served.
9.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a group. The '-ū' ending means the order is given to several people: 'you all do it!' The initial vowel is a helping prosthetic vowel that lets the word begin, since the bare command stem would otherwise start with a vowelless letter.
9.root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — to worship, to serve, devotion

10.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
10.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

11.meaning: 'My Lord' — the Master, Sustainer and Nurturer, claimed in close personal relation by the speaker.
11.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord') with the attached pronoun -ī meaning 'my'. This 'my' ending merges with the case-vowel of the noun, so a single long -ī is heard. The sense is 'the Lord who is mine'.
11.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to be lord/master, to nurture and sustain

12.meaning: 'And your Lord' — and the Lord, Master, Sustainer, and Nurturer of you all; 'Rabb' denotes the one who owns, governs, and cares for His creation, bringing it to its completion.
12.grammar: A connecting wa- ('and') with the noun 'Lord' and the possessive pronoun -kum ('your', for a group) attached. The -a vowel before the pronoun is the accusative case, typically marking the direct object of a verb.
12.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master; (Rabb) Lord, Sustainer, Owner

13.meaning: 'And I was / and I have been' — the conjunction 'and' plus the past-tense verb 'to be' in the first person, used to set a state or describe what one continually was.
13.grammar: Connective 'and' plus the past tense of the verb 'to be'; the '-tu' suffix marks 'I'. It expresses a past or ongoing-past state: 'I was / I used to be'.
13.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

14.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
14.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
14.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

15.meaning: 'A witness' — one who sees and attests, who can give evidence; also carries the sense of one who is present and observant, and at times 'a martyr' (one who bears witness with their life).
15.grammar: An intensive describing-noun (pattern fa‘īl) meaning 'a witness, one who fully attests', indefinite. The -an ending (the accusative with 'tanwīn') marks it as indefinite and in the accusative — the case used for a direct object, or for a word that describes the state or role in which someone stands.
15.root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d) — witnessing, being present, testifying

16.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
16.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.

17.meaning: 'I remained / I continued / as long as I stayed' — first-person past of a verb meaning to persist or go on being in a state; often used with the sense 'so long as I was …'.
17.grammar: A past-tense verb with the '-tu' suffix marking 'I'. It denotes continuing or persisting in a state, frequently introducing a 'for as long as I remained …' clause.
17.root: د-و-م (d-w-m) — to last, endure, continue, persist

18.meaning: "in them / among them" — the preposition 'in/among' joined to the pronoun 'them,' locating something within or amid a group of people.
18.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun, giving 'fīhim.' The preposition 'fī' keeps its long 'ī.' The pronoun '-him' is the third-person masculine plural ('them'); its vowel is 'i' (rather than '-hum') because it follows the high front vowel 'ī' of 'fī'.
18.root: — (preposition; the pronoun has no triliteral root)

19.meaning: A connector meaning 'then, when' — it joins to what came before ('then/so') and sets up a 'when…' clause whose outcome follows. It frames a moment: 'and then, at the point when…'.
19.grammar: A compound of the connecting particle fa- ('then/so', linking to the preceding statement) and lammā, a particle meaning 'when' that introduces a past circumstance and leads the listener to expect a following result clause.

20.meaning: 'You took me in full / You caused me to pass away / You took me back' — second-person (single male) act of taking a soul completely (commonly used of death or of taking one up), with 'me' as the object.

parts.en: took in full / caused to pass away

20.grammar: A past-tense verb of the form (form V) meaning 'to take something in full'. The '-ta' suffix marks 'you' (masculine singular); the attached '-nī' (protective 'n') is the object 'me': 'you took me fully / caused me to die'.
20.root: و-ف-ي (w-f-y) — to fulfil, complete, render in full; (form V) to take in full / cause to die

21.meaning: 'You (single male) were / used to be' — the past tense of 'to be', describing a past state, and often an ongoing or habitual condition in the past ('you used to…').
21.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) form of the verb 'to be'. The suffix -ta marks the subject as 'you', a single male. It states a condition that held in the past; paired with a following present-tense verb it often gives the sense 'you used to / you would (habitually)'.
21.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, becoming, coming to exist

22.meaning: 'You' — the standalone, independent pronoun for addressing a single male person directly.
22.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, second-person masculine singular. Unlike attached pronoun suffixes, it stands alone and is typically used to identify or emphasize the subject ('you [yourself]').

23.meaning: 'The watchful overseer / the ever-watching guardian' — one who observes, keeps watch over, and carefully guards everything; a name conveying vigilant supervision.
23.grammar: A definite noun in the intensive 'faʿīl' pattern, denoting a constant, thorough watcher. The final '-a' is the accusative/object ending, the form a noun takes when it serves as the object of a verb or after certain particles.
23.root: ر-ق-ب (r-q-b) — to watch, observe, keep guard over

24.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
24.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
24.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

25.meaning: 'And You' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'you' (addressing a single male). The independent pronoun stresses the subject, as in 'and You [Yourself] …'.
25.grammar: A connective 'and' plus a detached subject pronoun. 'anta' is the masculine-singular 'you'; as a standalone pronoun it adds emphasis or introduces a statement about the addressee ('You are …').

26.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
26.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

27.meaning: 'every,' 'each,' or 'all' — a word expressing totality or completeness. It indicates the entirety of something: when joined to a singular indefinite noun it means 'every (single) one,' and when joined to a definite noun it can mean 'all of' or 'the whole of.'
27.grammar: A noun of totality. The final '-i' ending is genitive (the 'of/possession' case): it marks the word as governed by a preceding preposition or as the first term of a possessive link to a following noun, so it typically reads 'of every…' or 'every…' leading into what follows.

28.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
28.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
28.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

29.meaning: A witness — one who sees and observes directly and can testify to what is true; also carries the sense of an ever-watchful observer.
29.grammar: An intensive descriptive noun (pattern 'faʿīl') meaning one who witnesses fully and constantly. The '-un' ending is nominative and indefinite: the nominative typically marks the subject or predicate ('is a witness'), and the final 'n' sound marks it indefinite.

1.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
1.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

2.meaning: 'You punish them / chastise them' — second-person (single male) act of inflicting punishment, with 'them' (a male/mixed group) as the object.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb of the intensive form (severe or repeated punishing). The 'tu-' prefix marks the subject 'you' (masculine singular); the attached '-hum' is the object 'them'. The vowel-less ('sukūn') ending on the stem reflects the jussive/conditional form used after particles like 'if' or 'whether'.

3.meaning: 'for indeed they …' — a connective 'for/so' joined to an emphatic particle that strongly affirms what follows, plus the pronoun 'they'. The combination introduces a firmly stressed statement about a group.
3.grammar: The particle 'inna' gives strong emphasis ('indeed, truly') and grammatically takes a following noun or pronoun in the accusative; here that is the attached -hum ('they', masculine plural), which serves as its subject. The leading 'fa' connects the clause to what precedes ('and so / for').

4.meaning: Servants or bondservants — those who belong to and worship a master, with an attached 'your' marking the master they belong to. The base noun denotes human beings considered as creatures wholly owned by and devoted to Allah.
4.grammar: A plural noun in the nominative case: the -u ending typically marks the word as the subject of a sentence or the thing being identified ('… are …'). The attached -ka means 'your' (addressing one male) and puts the noun in a possessive construction, so the case vowel sits before the pronoun. Plural of ʿabd, 'servant/slave.'
4.root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — to serve, worship, be a devoted slave

5.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
5.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

6.meaning: To cover over, pardon, and forgive — especially sins, blotting them out and shielding the wrongdoer from their consequences. The form is a present-tense verb addressed to a single male: 'you forgive / you cover over (sins).'
6.grammar: A present/imperfect verb. The ta- prefix marks a second-person singular masculine subject ('you'). The bare -ir ending with no added vowel reflects a jussive/conditional or otherwise unmarked mood (as after a conditional particle), rather than the plain indicative which would end in -u.

7.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
7.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

8.meaning: A two-part opener meaning roughly 'then/so, truly You …': a connecting 'then/so' joined to an emphatic particle that asserts what follows with certainty, plus an attached 'You.' The emphatic particle (inna) strongly affirms the statement, like saying 'indeed' or 'it is certainly the case that.'
8.grammar: A particle cluster, not a verb. fa- is a connector ('then, so, and thus'). inna is an emphatic/affirming particle that places the following noun or pronoun in the accusative; here that pronoun is the attached -ka ('you,' one male), the topic being emphasized. There is no tense or case ending of its own.

9.meaning: 'You' — the standalone, independent pronoun for addressing a single male person directly.
9.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, second-person masculine singular. Unlike attached pronoun suffixes, it stands alone and is typically used to identify or emphasize the subject ('you [yourself]').

10.meaning: "the All-Mighty / the Ever-Dominant" — one who is mighty, invincible, and held in honour; as a divine name 'al-ʿAzīz' denotes the One who is supremely powerful, unconquerable, and exalted above all.
10.grammar: A definite intensive adjective/noun on the faʿīl pattern, conveying a strong, enduring quality. The 'al-' prefix makes it definite ('the'). The final '-u' is the nominative case ending, the form used when the word is the subject of a sentence or a predicate/description following it.

11.meaning: The All-Wise — one possessing perfect wisdom, who puts everything in its right place and acts with flawless judgment; can also carry the sense of one who decrees and decides soundly.
11.grammar: A definite noun/adjective in an intensive pattern (faʿīl) stressing the depth and constancy of the quality. The prefix 'al-' means 'the'; the final -u (ḍamma) marks the nominative case, which typically signals the subject of a sentence or a describing predicate.
11.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge wisely, to be wise

1.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
1.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

2.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
2.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

3.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
3.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

4.meaning: A day — a period of time; by extension an appointed Day or occasion of decisive events. The base noun yawm denotes a day in the broadest sense, often used for a momentous appointed time.
4.grammar: A singular masculine noun in the nominative case: the -u ending marks the word as the subject of a sentence or as the thing being named/identified. (When this noun instead leads a possessive phrase, its case vowel is determined by its own role in the sentence — nominative -u, accusative -a, or genitive -i — not fixed by being the first term.)
4.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a span of time

5.meaning: He/it benefits, profits, or brings advantage to someone; to be of use.
5.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he' or 'it'). The final -u ending is the indicative mood, used for a plain, ongoing or habitual statement of fact ('benefits / is benefiting').

6.meaning: The truthful ones — those who are sincere and speak the truth, whose words and deeds match reality. A plural describing people characterized by truthfulness and sincerity, prefixed with 'the.'
6.grammar: A masculine plural active participle ('the ones who are truthful') with the definite article 'the.' The -īna ending is the sound masculine plural in its accusative/genitive (oblique) form: it marks the word either as an object of a verb or as following a preposition or possessive, as opposed to the subject form -ūna.
6.root: ص-د-ق (ṣ-d-q) — truthfulness, sincerity, telling the truth

7.meaning: Truthfulness or sincerity — being truthful in word and deed, conformity between what one says and what is real. The base noun ṣidq names this quality, with an attached 'their' linking it to its owners.
7.grammar: An abstract masculine noun in the nominative case: the -u ending typically marks the word as the subject ('their truthfulness …') or the thing being identified. The attached -hum means 'their' (a group of males or mixed group) and forms a possessive construction, with the case vowel sitting before the pronoun.
7.root: ص-د-ق (ṣ-d-q) — truthfulness, sincerity, telling the truth

8.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
8.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

9.meaning: Gardens — lush, enclosed places of greenery, trees, and shade; the plural of a single garden, evoking abundant, sheltered groves.
9.grammar: A feminine plural noun, indefinite. The final -un (nunation) marks it as nominative and indefinite ('gardens'), the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or for a predicate ('they are …').
9.root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n) — covering, concealing (a garden's foliage covers the ground)

10.meaning: A verb 'it flows, runs, streams' — used of water and rivers moving along, and of things that run or course freely. It describes continuous, ongoing motion.
10.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, 3rd person feminine singular. The ta- prefix here marks a feminine 'it/she' subject. The verb describes an ongoing or habitual action: 'it flows / keeps flowing.'

11.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
11.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

12.meaning: 'Beneath it / underneath it' — the noun for the underside or lower region of something, with an attached pronoun 'its' (referring to a feminine thing). It points to the space below or underneath a thing.
12.grammar: A location noun ('underneath') with the attached pronoun '-hā' ('its/her'), referring to a feminine noun. The -i ending is the genitive case, normally triggered here because words of place like 'under' commonly follow a preposition such as 'from' (min taḥti = 'from beneath').
12.root: ت-ح-ت (t-ḥ-t) — underneath, below

13.meaning: 'The rivers / the streams' — the definite plural of a word for a flowing river or watercourse. It denotes large, running channels of water.
13.grammar: A definite plural noun ('the rivers'). The -u ending is the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence — the doer of the verb or the thing being described.
13.root: ن-ه-ر (n-h-r) — river, flowing water

14.meaning: Ones who abide / remain forever — those who dwell perpetually and permanently in a state or place, without end. The word denotes lasting, undying permanence.
14.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' word: 'ones abiding'). The -īna ending is the sound masculine plural in its accusative/genitive form, used when the word is an object or governed by a preceding element. It describes people characterized by perpetual abiding.
14.root: خ-ل-د (kh-l-d) — perpetuity, everlasting abiding

15.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
15.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.
15.root: — (particle plus pronoun; no root)

16.meaning: An adverb meaning 'ever / forever / at any time' — used to stress that something will never (or always) be the case throughout all time, especially with a negative to mean 'never, not ever'.
16.grammar: A noun used adverbially. The ending -an is the indefinite accusative, the form regularly used to turn a word into an adverb of time ('… ever / forever'); the -n (nunation) marks it as indefinite. Paired with a negation it strengthens it to 'never, not ever'.

17.meaning: To be pleased, well-content, and approving — to accept something with satisfaction and good will. A past-tense verb describing a single subject who became and is pleased: 'he was pleased / he approved.'
17.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb with no prefix. Its bare form with the final -a vowel marks a third-person singular masculine subject ('he'). The perfect tense presents the action as completed: 'was/became pleased, was content.'
17.root: ر-ض-و / ر-ض-ي (r-ḍ-w/y) — to be pleased, content, approving

18.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
18.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
18.root: — (proper divine name)

19.meaning: From them; away from them; concerning them. The preposition ʿan conveys moving away from, departing from, or 'on behalf of / concerning', combined with the pronoun 'them'.
19.grammar: A preposition joined to the attached pronoun -hum, 'them' (referring to a group, grammatically masculine plural). The preposition ʿan basically signals separation or removal ('away from'), and can also mean 'about/concerning' or 'on behalf of' depending on usage.
19.root: — (a preposition; no triliteral verbal root)

20.meaning: 'And they were pleased / and they were content' — the act of being satisfied and approving, here done by a group. Joins a connecting 'and' to a past-tense verb whose ending marks a plural 'they' as the ones who became pleased.
20.grammar: A connector wa- ('and') plus a past-tense (perfect) verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'), presenting the action as completed: 'they were/became pleased.' The trailing alif is a silent spelling convention after this plural ending, not pronounced.
20.root: ر-ض-و / ر-ض-ي (r-ḍ-w/y) — to be pleased, content, approving

21.meaning: A combination meaning 'from him / from it / about him.' The preposition denotes moving away from, departing from, or concerning a thing, and the pronoun refers to a single masculine entity.
21.grammar: A preposition with a fused object pronoun. ʿan governs the genitive and conveys separation or 'concerning.' The attached -hu marks a third-person masculine singular object ('him/it').

22.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
22.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

23.meaning: 'The success' / 'the triumph' — attainment of what is sought and safety from what is feared; winning, salvation, the great achievement. With the article it is 'the (true) success'.
23.grammar: A definite masculine noun. The -u ending is the nominative case, marking it as a subject or as the thing identified (e.g. 'that IS the success').
23.root: ف-و-ز (f-w-z) — to win, triumph, attain salvation

24.meaning: 'the Most Great / the Immense' — vast, mighty, and tremendous in greatness and grandeur. As a divine name it conveys overwhelming magnificence and majesty.
24.grammar: A definite adjective/noun in an intensive pattern ('the Magnificent'). The -u ending is nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or for an appositive descriptive title attached to such a subject.
24.root: ع-ظ-م (ʿ-ẓ-m) — to be great, mighty, immense

1.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'li-' meaning 'to', 'for', or 'belonging to', attached to the name 'Allah'. It conveys 'to Allah' or 'for Allah'.
1.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('to/for') pulls the following noun into the genitive case, which is why 'Allah' ends in '-i' (llāhi). The '-i' ending is the regular result of a noun governed by a preposition.

2.meaning: Kingdom, dominion, sovereign rule — full ownership and authority over a realm; the right and power to command and dispose.
2.grammar: A singular noun. The final -u marks the nominative case, used when the noun is the subject of a sentence or the thing being identified ('the dominion is …'). The absence of nunation here points to its being made definite by a following possessor in a genitive link.
2.root: م-ل-ك (m-l-k) — to own, rule; kingship, dominion

3.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
3.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.

4.meaning: 'And the earth' — the connective 'and' joined to 'the earth', meaning the ground, land, or the world beneath the sky.
4.grammar: The connective 'wa-' ('and') with the definite feminine noun 'al-arḍ' ('the earth'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the earth') or follows a preposition, here matching the case of what it is joined to.

5.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
5.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

6.meaning: A small unit: the preposition 'in / within / during' joined to the attached pronoun 'them' referring to a group of feminine things.
6.grammar: 'fī' is the preposition 'in/within/during'. The attached -hinna is the object pronoun 'them' for a group of feminine items, so the whole means 'in/among them'. Pronouns attached to a preposition like this always take the genitive form.

7.meaning: 'And He' — the connective 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'He' (a single masculine person or thing), often introducing a new clause about the same subject.
7.grammar: A connective particle plus an independent pronoun. The wa- prefix means 'and', joining clauses or words. 'Huwa' is the detached third-person masculine singular pronoun; it carries no case ending, its final -a being fixed.

8.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
8.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

9.meaning: 'every,' 'each,' or 'all' — a word expressing totality or completeness. It indicates the entirety of something: when joined to a singular indefinite noun it means 'every (single) one,' and when joined to a definite noun it can mean 'all of' or 'the whole of.'
9.grammar: A noun of totality. The final '-i' ending is genitive (the 'of/possession' case): it marks the word as governed by a preceding preposition or as the first term of a possessive link to a following noun, so it typically reads 'of every…' or 'every…' leading into what follows.

10.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
10.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
10.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

11.meaning: 'All-Powerful,' 'fully able,' 'one who has complete power and capability.' An intensive form expressing that the one described possesses perfect, unrestricted power to do whatever is willed — a quality applied supremely to Allah.
11.grammar: An intensive adjective on the faʿīl pattern, conveying a deep, established capability. The '-un' ending (tanwīn al-ḍamm) marks the nominative case (the 'subject/predicate' case) together with indefiniteness — typically the role of a subject or, very often, a predicate describing who or what something is.
